This profile was surfaced as a General Catalyst portfolio company and is maintained by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline; Aatmunn publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: Upstream Security
providers.description: Upstream Security is a cloud-based automotive and smart-mobility cybersecurity company. Its purpose-built vehicle data platform delivers Cyber XDR detection and response for connected vehicles, runtime AI and API security, proactive quality detection, and advanced analytics, alongside AutoThreat PRO threat intelligence and Vehicle Security Operations Center (vSOC) services for OEMs, Tier 1 and 2 suppliers, fleets, insurers, EV charging, and mobility IoT operators. Upstream publishes no public developer portal or API; the platform is sold as enterprise SaaS with demo-based onboarding.

providers.name: Helium Network
providers.description: Helium operates two decentralized wireless networks - a global LoRaWAN network for low-power IoT devices and a cellular + Wi-Fi offload network for mobile connectivity (Helium Mobile). The network is settled on the Solana blockchain with HNT, IOT, and MOBILE tokens. Developer surface includes the Helium Console / LoRaWAN Network Server APIs used to onboard devices and stream uplinks, on-chain Solana programs for the Helium DAO and rewards, the open-source Helium-Program-Library and helium-wallet SDKs, and partner-operated Network Servers (e.g. Nova Labs, MeteoScientific).

providers.name: Evidation Health
providers.description: Evidation Health is a San Mateo, California digital health company, founded in 2012, that measures health in everyday life and runs permissioned real-world data research at scale. Its consumer app and platform — Achievement — rewards members for connecting wearables, apps and health records, and its enterprise Research & Engagement Platform gives life-sciences, payer, government and non-profit customers eConsent and onboarding, ePRO and survey capture, passive and active device monitoring, program analytics, and participant education. Evidation combines data from sources including Apple Health, Fitbit, Garmin, Dexcom and EHR/claims records (via a partnership with 1upHealth's FHIR-based Patient Connect, and with HealthVerity), and has enabled 175+ virtual real-world studies and 70+ peer-reviewed publications. Evidation publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API contract; its programmatic surfaces are the member app backend and enterprise data deliveries, neither of which is publicly documented.

providers.name: Instrumental
providers.description: Instrumental is a platform for manufacturing intelligence that helps companies detect and prevent product failures during the manufacturing process. The Instrumental API enables programmatic access to retrieve unit and inspection test data and metadata from Instrumental projects.

providers.name: Metromile
providers.description: Metromile is a pay-per-mile auto insurance platform powered by telematics and data science. Customers attach the Pulse OBD device to their vehicle to track mileage; premiums consist of a base monthly rate plus a per-mile charge, rewarding low-mileage drivers with significant savings. Beyond consumer insurance, Metromile Enterprise offers a cloud-based REST API platform for property and casualty insurers covering touchless claims automation, accident reconstruction (Replay), fraud detection (Detect), digital FNOL reporting (Report), and back-office workflow automation (Streamline). Metromile was acquired by Lemonade in July 2022.

providers.name: Electric
providers.description: Electric (Electric AI) is an IT and security management platform for small and medium-sized businesses, consolidating device management, application and SaaS management, security posture monitoring with automatic remediation, and employee onboarding/offboarding into a single platform that requires no in-house IT skills and syncs with HR systems. Founded in New York and backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Electric bundles partner tooling (JumpCloud MDM/SSO, Keeper, ThreatDown, Harmony Email, Perimeter81 VPN, Drata) behind an AI-powered IT Hub, help desk, and hardware procurement service. It is not a developer-API company: there is no public developer portal, API reference, or SDKs at this time. This profile was surfaced as a Bessemer portfolio company and enriched from Electric's public web surface.

providers.name: Glowforge
providers.description: Glowforge is a Seattle-based consumer hardware company that makes desktop 3D laser printers (Glowforge Pro, Plus, Aura, and Spark) which cut and engrave materials such as wood, acrylic, leather, fabric, and paper. The machines are cloud-connected: designs are prepared in the browser-based Glowforge App (app.glowforge.com) and sent to the printer over the internet, with camera-based material placement, autofocus, and an online design catalog and marketplace. Glowforge does not publish a public developer API; its developer-facing footprint is limited to open-source GPL firmware and kernel components on GitHub (published for license compliance) and a public system status page.

providers.name: The Travelers Companies
providers.description: The Travelers Companies, Inc. (NYSE: TRV) is a leading United States property and casualty (P&C) insurance carrier providing auto, home, and business insurance to individuals, agencies, businesses, government units, and associations. Travelers is a component of the Dow Jones Industrial Average, generated approximately $48.83 billion in revenue in 2025, holds roughly $143.7 billion in total assets, and employs approximately 34,000 people plus 15,000 independent agents and brokers across the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and the Republic of Ireland. The company operates through three reportable segments — Business Insurance, Bond & Specialty Insurance, and Personal Insurance — distributing primarily through a network of independent agents and brokers, and through direct-to-consumer channels for segments of its personal lines. Travelers has a developer portal at developer.travelers.com that surfaces APIs intended for appointed agents, agency-management-system (AMS) vendors, and integration partners; the portal is gated (Salesforce Experience Cloud) and individual API specifications, endpoints, and pricing are not publicly published. The company also publishes the IntelliDrive and IntelliDrivePlus telematics mobile apps used to score personal-auto driving behavior for rating credits.

providers.name: Hippo Insurance
providers.description: Hippo is a modern homeowners insurance carrier that also offers landlord, fire, flood, pet, and auto add-ons, backed by 70+ carrier partners. Hippo's smart-home angle is the Hippo Home app, which delivers DIY maintenance checklists, seasonal guidance, and a home health score. Hippo's B2B distribution runs through First Connect, an API-driven independent-agent platform with 100+ carriers and MGAs, and Spinnaker for MGA carrier paper.

providers.name: Tovala
providers.description: Tovala is a Chicago-based food-technology company that pairs a fresh meal delivery service with its proprietary smart countertop ovens. Weekly rotating, chef-crafted meals ship with QR codes that the Tovala Smart Oven (5-in-1) and Smart Oven Pro (6-in-1 with steam) scan to cook automatically, eliminating shopping, prepping, and cleanup. The company also offers GLP-1 balanced and high-protein menus, flexible meal plans, and a consumer mobile app backed by its api.tovala.com platform. Tovala is a Y Combinator portfolio company.

providers.name: Guardhat
providers.description: Guardhat (now operating as Aatmunn) is an industrial safety and asset intelligence platform serving more than 250 companies across oil & gas, utilities, logistics and warehousing, chemicals, mining, infrastructure, and manufacturing. Its SPANR platform is a unified intelligence layer that collects data from connected safety devices and wearables, normalizes it into a single source of truth, applies business logic, and surfaces insights through a suite of applications for digital safety inspections, lone worker safety, gas detection, human condition monitoring, control access zoning, and asset tracking. Originally known for connected hard hats and wearable safety technology, the company rebranded from Guardhat to Aatmunn. Guardhat is a venture-backed portfolio company of General Catalyst. This profile has been enriched from the company's public web presence; no public developer API or OpenAPI surface was found at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Bevel
providers.description: Bevel is a consumer digital-health application, built by Finerpoint, Inc., that acts as an AI-powered "connected health coach." It consolidates and interprets health data from wearables (Apple Watch, Oura, Garmin, Amazfit) and lab providers (Labcorp, Quest, LifeLabs) into a single view, scoring daily strain, sleep, recovery, stress/energy, nutrition, cycle, biological age and strength training. Its "Bevel Intelligence" layer delivers conversational, research-backed guidance, personalized workout plans and daily check-ins. Bevel is a mobile-first consumer product with no publicly documented developer API; this profile captures its public web, support, roadmap and legal surface. Backed by General Catalyst.

providers.name: Growatt
providers.description: Growatt New Energy is a global manufacturer of solar PV inverters, energy storage systems, and smart energy management products for residential, commercial, and utility-scale installations. Growatt operates the ShineServer / ShinePhone cloud monitoring platform and publishes a token-authenticated Open API (V1) that lets third-party systems read plant and device telemetry, retrieve historical energy data, and read or write inverter parameters for MIN (TLX) string inverters and SPH (MIX) hybrid inverters across regional endpoints. Originally surfaced as a portfolio company of IDG Capital; enriched from Growatt's public developer surface.

providers.name: Platform Science
providers.description: Platform Science is an enterprise connected-vehicle and fleet management platform for commercial trucking and transportation. It combines ELD and telematics, driver applications (Hours of Service, DVIR, navigation, workflow, media management), back-office fleet management, and video safety intelligence on a single connected-vehicle platform. Its Virtual Vehicle Marketplace hosts 100+ partner integrations across 18 categories (asset tracking, compliance, fuel, navigation, sensors, TMS, and more), and a gated developer program (the Remote Platform Management system, an Android SDK, and a data-retrieval API governed by SPEED Certification) lets partners build edge and cloud integrations against the platform.

providers.name: Stratasys
providers.description: Stratasys Ltd. (Nasdaq: SSYS) is a global leader in polymer additive manufacturing (industrial 3D printing), headquartered in Rehovot, Israel and Eden Prairie, Minnesota. Stratasys builds FDM, PolyJet, stereolithography (SLA), selective absorption fusion (SAF) and powder-bed (P3) printing systems, the materials that feed them, and the GrabCAD software platform that drives them. Its developer surface is the GrabCAD ecosystem: GrabCAD Print / GrabCAD Print Pro for job preparation, GrabCAD Control and GrabCAD Shop for fleet and shop management, and the GrabCAD Software Development Kit — a partner program of connectivity SDKs (Printer Connectivity SDK, MT Connect SDK, PLM SDK) that use standard protocols and APIs to integrate Stratasys printers with ERP, PLM, MES and smart-factory systems for automation, data collection and analytics.

providers.name: Alif Semiconductor
providers.description: Alif Semiconductor is a fabless semiconductor company headquartered in Pleasanton, California with engineering operations in Grenoble, France. It designs secure, AI/ML-enabled 32-bit microcontrollers and fusion processors for edge computing, built around Arm Cortex-M55 cores and dedicated Arm Ethos-U55 Neural Processing Units. Its Ensemble (E1C, E1, E3, E4, E5, E6, E7, E8) and Balletto (B1) product families target battery-powered edge AI and generative-AI workloads, pairing hardware AI acceleration with autonomous aiPM power management and a multilayered hardware Root of Trust security subsystem. Alif ships an embedded developer surface rather than a public web API: a Zephyr-based SDK, CMSIS Device Family Packs, VS Code project templates, the Conductor configuration tool, evaluation kits, datasheets, and reference manuals published across its support hub and GitHub organization. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and Mayfield.

providers.name: Monarch Tractor
providers.description: Monarch Tractor is a Livermore, California agricultural-technology company that builds the MK-V, a fully electric, driver-optional smart tractor, together with WingspanAI (Wingspan Ag Intelligence) — an AWS-hosted farm-management and fleet-telemetry platform that collects in-field video, machine telemetry, energy and emissions data from connected tractors and presents it to growers through web and mobile apps. The company markets an "open ecosystem" in which third parties integrate with the MK-V and WingspanAI, and has pivoted toward selling autonomy as software and licensing its autonomy stack to other equipment makers. Monarch publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable specification; the WingspanAI platform is reachable only through a customer login.

providers.name: Parklio
providers.description: Seamlessly integrate your existing systems or products with Parklio API so you can scale your operations and monitor parking space usage in real time. It provides access to your data in a way that works best for you, whether through integration, automation, or full customization. The API is RESTful with JSON responses, and Android and iOS SDKs are available on request.

providers.name: Upciti
providers.description: Upciti is a French smart-city company that equips cities with intelligent computer-vision sensors and the Upciti OS platform, turning streets into clear, anonymous data for informed municipal decisions across parking, mobility, energy, water, gas, lighting, temperature, weather, air quality, pollen, illegal dumping, and noise. Sensors process video 100% locally with no image storage (GDPR-native, DTPR-supporting), and the platform advertises an open API for connecting GIS, BI, and business tools with no proprietary lock-in. Product documentation is customer-gated.

providers.name: CropX
providers.description: CropX is an Israeli ag-IoT company that combines in-field soil and weather hardware with a cloud Farm Management Software (FMS) platform. The hardware portfolio includes SV-series soil sensors (moisture, temperature, conductivity, salinity at depth), ET-series evapotranspiration sensors, WS-series weather stations, RG rain gauges, the Apex root-zone sensor, an in-development nitrate sensor, and TD-series cellular telemetry gateways. The FMS covers farm / field / crop data, device management, irrigation scheduling, disease monitoring, nutrition, effluent, and reporting. CropX does not publish a public developer portal; integrations with third-party sensors and machinery are arranged through their team.

providers.name: JubileeTV
providers.description: JubileeTV is a remote caregiving system that turns an aging loved one's existing television into a simple connection, monitoring, and video-calling hub. A small console plugs into the senior's TV and pairs with a mobile app so that family caregivers can control the TV remotely, place video calls that appear full-screen on the TV, send medication and appointment reminders, share photos, and run wellness check-ins from anywhere in the world. Seniors keep using their familiar remote or an included voice remote with no learning curve. JubileeTV is sold as a hardware console plus an ongoing membership (monthly, annual, or one-time), is available in the U.S. only, and is backed by Greylock. The storefront runs on Shopify.

providers.name: FordPass / Ford Pro
providers.description: FordPass is Ford Motor Company's consumer connected-vehicle mobile app and service platform for Ford and Lincoln owners, exposing remote start/stop, remote lock/unlock, vehicle status (fuel/charge, tire pressure, oil life, odometer, location), Vehicle Health alerts, BlueCruise hands-free driving, Wi-Fi hotspot, Phone As A Key, scheduled service, and roadside assistance via the embedded FordPass Connect 4G LTE modem. Ford Pro is Ford's commercial fleet brand spanning Ford Pro Telematics, Ford Pro Intelligence, Ford Pro E-Telematics for EVs, Ford Pro Charging, Ford Pro FinSimple, and dealer/upfit services. The Ford Developer Marketplace (developer.ford.com) hosts Ford's partner-facing API program — FordConnect Query API for consumer-vehicle data and remote command access (with vehicle-owner consent via FordPass account OAuth), plus a Ford Pro REST API surface for fleets including Vehicle Status, Vehicle Historical Status, Vehicle Metadata, Vehicle Efficiency (fuel/energy/idle), Driver Behavior, Trip Reports, and Vehicle Health. Ford Pro Telematics is integrated with Geotab, Fleetio, Samsara, Motive, Verizon Connect, and other fleet platforms, and Smartcar offers a consumer OAuth bridge to Ford vehicles using FordPass Connect credentials. Access to Ford APIs is gated behind a partner application and credentials issued through the Ford Developer Portal; Ford has periodically restricted individual-developer access. No public OpenAPI specification is published outside the partner portal, so this profile documents the Ford developer surface as an index without a generated machine-readable contract.

providers.name: VanMoof
providers.description: VanMoof is an Amsterdam-based e-bike company that designs and sells smart electric city bikes with integrated anti-theft technology, GPS tracking, and a companion rider app. Originally backed by Balderton Capital and relaunched after its 2023 restructuring, VanMoof operates a connected-bike platform, but publishes no public developer API — the app and bike APIs are private, and existing client libraries are community-built and reverse-engineered.

providers.name: Tulip Interfaces
providers.description: Tulip is a manufacturing operations platform that enables frontline operations teams to build apps, connect machines and devices, and analyze production data without code. The Tulip REST API provides programmatic access to apps, tables, connectors, stations, automations, and analytics, supporting integration with ERP, MES, and industrial equipment on the shop floor.

providers.name: Zip Security
providers.description: Zip Security is a cloud-based security, IT, and compliance platform that automates identity management, device management (MDM for macOS, Windows, iOS, and Android), and endpoint threat detection for small and mid-sized businesses. It unifies tools such as Microsoft Intune, Jamf, and CrowdStrike behind a single dashboard, deploying frameworks, policies, and controls that are continuously enforced to help teams reach SOC 2, HIPAA, ISO 27001, CMMC, and PCI readiness, often within two weeks. Zip Security is backed by General Catalyst. This profile currently exposes no public developer API; it is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile.

providers.name: BrainCo
providers.description: BrainCo is a Harvard-innovation-lab-founded neurotechnology company building non-invasive brain-computer interface (BCI) hardware and the developer SDKs that surround it. Its consumer and research line centers on wearable EEG headbands - Focus, Focus1 and FocusCalm - that measure attention and stress from brainwave signals for education, wellness and biofeedback, alongside the BrainRobotics neuroprosthetic hand and the Revo (Revo1/Revo2/Revo3) family of dexterous robotic hands for robotics and embodied-AI developers. BrainCo ships first-party SDKs rather than a public REST API: the Crimson SDK for its portable EEG devices (Node.js and native/BLE), the Focus SDK for headband brainwave measurement, and the Revo Hand SDKs (Python and C/C++, distributed on PyPI and GitHub) that speak RS-485, CAN 2.0A/CAN FD, EtherCAT and Protobuf, plus ROS 2 drivers and URDF/MJCF/USD simulation assets. The company is backed by IDG Capital and operates in the healthcare, neurotech, robotics and education-technology sectors.

providers.name: Owletcare
providers.description: Owlet (Owletcare) is a baby-monitoring technology company that builds connected-nursery hardware and companion apps for parents. Its flagship Dream Sock is marketed as an FDA-cleared smart baby monitor that tracks a sleeping infant's pulse rate, oxygen levels, movement and sleep patterns, alongside the Dream Sight HD video monitor and the combined Dream Duo system. Products pair a wearable/camera with the Owlet Dream mobile app for real-time wellness insights and notifications. The consumer storefront at owletcare.com runs on Shopify; sign-in is handled by Shopify's Customer Account API (OIDC/OAuth), and Owlet does not currently publish a first-party developer API program. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and enriched from Owlet's public web surface.

providers.name: Progressive Insurance
providers.description: One of the largest auto insurance providers in the United States offering personal auto, motorcycle, boat, RV, home, renters, and commercial insurance. Progressive is known for its direct-to-consumer model (1-800-PROGRESSIVE and progressive.com), its independent-agent channel, the comparative rate quoting experience, and the Snapshot usage-based insurance program that prices premiums against telematics-captured driving behaviour from a plug-in OBD-II dongle or the Snapshot mobile app. Progressive also runs the ForAgents agent portal and a public Developer Portal at developer.progressive.com that hosts embedded-quoting APIs for partners — including the Embedded Direct auto quoting API, the Commercial Auto Quoting product, and the Certificate of Insurance API — alongside private B2B integrations with comparative-rater carriers, agency-management systems, and telematics providers.

providers.name: Root Insurance
providers.description: Root is a U.S. app-first auto insurer that prices policies primarily on real driving behavior captured by smartphone telematics. The Root mobile app handles enrollment, telematics scoring, policy management, claims, and optional roadside assistance, with renters insurance as an add-on line. Root has reorganized its tech stack around APIs to power embedded auto insurance with partners such as Carvana and Hyundai Capital America; partner APIs are gated and not publicly documented. Note: Root Insurance (joinroot.com) is distinct from the unrelated Root Platform (rootplatform.com) insurtech in South Africa / UK.

providers.name: Cala Health
providers.description: Cala Health is a bioelectronic medicine company that develops wearable neuromodulation therapies for chronic disease. Its FDA-cleared Cala kIQ and Cala TRIO systems deliver TAPS (Transcutaneous Afferent Patterned Stimulation) therapy through a wrist-worn device that is physician-prescribed and clinically proven to reduce action hand tremors associated with essential tremor and Parkinson's disease. Patients manage therapy and view results through the MyCala portal, and clinicians access data through the Cala 360 provider portal. Cala Health is a GV (Google Ventures) portfolio company operating in the life-sciences / medical-device sector. This profile currently exposes no public developer API; enrichment has captured the company's public security, privacy, and support surface.

providers.name: Lucis
providers.description: Lucis is a Paris-based, AI-powered preventative health platform (Y Combinator P25; backed by General Catalyst) that helps members understand their biology through comprehensive lab testing and personalised coaching. Members receive two annual lab assessments (blood, urine, and saliva) at 450+ partner labs across Europe, producing 110+ data points across 11 body systems — metabolic, cardiovascular, hormonal, nervous, and more — which an AI engine turns into personalised action plans spanning nutrition, supplementation, sleep, activity, and mental health. The platform ingests wearable data (Garmin, Withings, Oura, Strava; Apple Watch and Whoop coming soon) for ongoing monitoring. Lucis is a consumer health product; as of this profile it exposes a member web/mobile application and a compliance portal but publishes no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Nirvana Tech
providers.description: Nirvana Insurance (Nirvana Tech, Inc.) is a technology-driven commercial trucking insurance provider that pairs A-rated fleet insurance coverage with an AI-powered active safety platform. Nirvana ingests telematics and connected-vehicle data from motor carriers to price risk more accurately, help fleets save up to 20% on premiums, and reduce accidents through real-time safety alerts, driver coaching, and predictive risk scoring. The company serves fleets and independent insurance agents through a digital quoting and policy-management agent portal, and is backed by General Catalyst. Nirvana raised a Series D round to expand its data-driven insurance and safety products across the trucking industry. As of this profile Nirvana operates a marketing site plus an agent sign-in portal and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Ordr
providers.description: Ordr provides AI-powered security for connected devices, delivering a Cyber Asset Attack Surface Management (CAASM) platform that discovers, classifies, and secures IT, IoT, OT, and IoMT devices across enterprise networks. The platform combines device intelligence, risk and vulnerability management, network segmentation, and zero-trust enforcement to move organizations from visibility to action. Ordr integrates with existing security and networking infrastructure (Cisco, Palo Alto Networks, CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, Fortinet, Aruba, Juniper) and serves healthcare, manufacturing, financial services, government, and retail sectors. The company is headquartered in Santa Clara, California. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and enriched from Ordr's public web surface; Ordr does not publish a public developer API or developer portal.

providers.name: Silicon Labs
providers.description: Silicon Labs (Silabs) is a fabless semiconductor company headquartered in Austin, Texas that designs silicon, software, and solutions for a more connected, IoT world. Its portfolio includes wireless connectivity SoCs and modules for Bluetooth, Bluetooth Mesh, Zigbee, Thread, Matter, Z-Wave, Wi-Fi, and proprietary sub-GHz protocols, along with 32-bit microcontrollers, sensors, and timing devices. Developers build on Silicon Labs hardware using the Simplicity Studio IDE, the Simplicity SDK (formerly Gecko SDK), the docs.silabs.com developer documentation, and the Silicon Labs Community. Silicon Labs is a hardware and embedded-software provider rather than a web-API vendor: its public developer surface is embedded C/C++ SDKs, tools, and reference examples on GitHub (github.com/SiliconLabs), not a hosted REST API — so this profile carries identity, developer-portal, and security signals rather than API specifications.

providers.name: Ambiq Micro
providers.description: Ambiq Micro is a semiconductor company that designs ultra-low-power System-on-Chip (SoC) solutions for battery-powered and endpoint-AI devices. Its proprietary Subthreshold Power Optimized Technology (SPOT) platform lets its Apollo family of Arm Cortex-M microcontrollers and Artasie real-time clocks run at extremely low energy, powering wearables, hearables, healthcare, smart-home, industrial and gaming devices. Ambiq's developer surface is an embedded C/C++ toolchain - the AmbiqSuite SDK and the open-source neuralSPOT AI SDK/Toolkit - plus a set of first-party Python AI toolkits (heartKIT, sleepKIT, physioKIT, neuralspotx) published on PyPI and GitHub (AmbiqAI, AmbiqMicro). This is not a web/REST API provider; it is profiled here for its open-source developer and AI SDK footprint.

providers.name: Insta360
providers.description: Insta360 (Arashi Vision Co., Ltd) is a consumer and professional imaging company best known for its 360-degree and action cameras (the X, GO, ACE, Link, and Pro/Titan lines). For developers, Insta360 runs a first-party developer program through its Insta360Develop GitHub organization and a VitePress developer-documentation site. Cameras expose on-device HTTP control APIs: consumer models implement Google's Open Spherical Camera (OSC) API over the camera Wi-Fi AP, and the Pro/Titan line adds a JSON-over-HTTP command API (ProCameraApi) for capture, live streaming, and file access. Native SDKs wrap this surface for C++ (camera control and media stitching/editing), Android, and iOS so third-party apps can connect to, configure, capture from, and post-process footage from Insta360 hardware.

providers.name: Halter
providers.description: Halter is a New Zealand-founded agri-technology company that builds GPS-enabled, solar-powered smart collars for cattle paired with a mobile and web app, letting farmers set and move virtual fences, remotely shift and hold herds, and monitor animal location, behavior, heat and health without physical fencing or manual labor. The platform combines wearable IoT devices (including direct-to-satellite connectivity) with pasture-management and grazing-allocation tools for dairy and beef operations. Halter operates across New Zealand, Australia and the United States and is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Bond Capital and DCVC. No public developer API surface has been identified; this profile captures the company identity, web properties and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Hopper
providers.description: Hopper is a travel marketplace and fintech, best known for consumer flight, hotel, car, and homes booking with fintech ancillaries such as Price Freeze, Cancel for Any Reason, and Disruption Assistance for Any Reason. Hopper Technology Solutions (HTS) is the B2B arm that exposes Hopper's e-commerce (Stays, Cars, Packages), fintech ancillaries, loyalty portals, and HTS Assist agentic AI to banks, airlines, and travel providers including Capital One, Air Canada, Virgin Australia, Tripadvisor, Frontier, Wizz Air, and Porter.

providers.name: Kace
providers.description: KACE is the endpoint and systems management product line from Quest Software, originally founded in 2003 as KACE Networks (backed by Norwest Venture Partners, Sigma Partners, and Focus Ventures), acquired by Dell in 2010, and now sold as Quest KACE. The portfolio centers on the KACE Systems Management Appliance (SMA) for inventory, patching, software distribution, scripting, and service desk; the KACE Systems Deployment Appliance (SDA) for OS imaging and provisioning; and KACE Cloud for mobile device management and modern endpoint management. The KACE SMA ships a REST API (JSON and XML) that lets administrators programmatically manage assets, inventory, managed installations, scripting, users, and service-desk tickets on the customer-hosted appliance. This profile enriches the original Norwest portfolio lead with the real Quest KACE identity and its documented API surface.

providers.name: AMPAworks
providers.description: AMPAworks builds AI-powered smart-shelf inventory management for healthcare and defense supply chains. Its platform pairs computer-vision cameras and rolling kiosks that image inventory to auto-count stock in real time with software that tracks supplies 24/7, automates reordering, and gives teams live visibility to prevent stock-outs. The company reports outcomes such as $15M in cost reduction, 25,000 hours saved on hand counting, and 72% fewer stock-outs across more than 28 healthcare and operational organizations. Backed by 500 Global, AMPAworks operates from offices in Santa Monica CA, Buffalo NY, Hackensack NJ, and Ann Arbor MI.

providers.name: NTT
providers.description: NTT (Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corporation) is a Tokyo-headquartered global technology and telecommunications group with roughly 340,000 employees and a 150-year history of innovation. The group operates through five business divisions — Consulting & IT Services, Mobile Solutions, Smart Tech, Consumer & Business, and Research & Development — and is anchored by major subsidiaries including NTT DOCOMO (Japan's largest mobile carrier), NTT Communications / NTT DOCOMO BUSINESS (enterprise cloud, network, and platform services), NTT DATA Group (global IT services and systems integration), NTT Ltd. (managed services), and NTT Research. NTT exposes a substantial developer surface through the NTT DOCOMO BUSINESS Developer Portal at developer.ntt.com, which catalogs enterprise APIs across Network (Arcstar Universal One, Flexible InterConnect, Global M2M), Cloud (Smart Data Platform, Enterprise Cloud 2.0), Voice, App (Safety Confirmation, Text & Language Analysis, Speech Recognition), Management (asset visibility, vulnerability), and Core (Authorization, Billing, API Log, Business Process, Service Order, Pay-per-use, Price, Organization, Personal Profile) categories. The group also publishes IoT APIs (Things Cloud) and a docomo Developer support portal at dev.smt.docomo.ne.jp. NTT's primary open source presence is the nttcom GitHub organization, which ships the Enterprise Cloud Python and Go SDKs (eclsdk / eclcloud), the eclcli command-line tool, Terraform providers for Enterprise Cloud 2.0 (terraform-provider- ecl) and Flexible InterConnect (terraform-provider-fic), the ksot network-IaC framework, the pola stateful PCE / PCEP library, the fluvia eBPF/XDP IPFIX exporter, and threatconnectome for SBOM-driven vulnerability management. NTT DATA additionally maintains regional GitHub orgs (NTTDATA, NTTDATA-EMEA, NTTDATA-DACH, NTTDATAInnovation, launchbynttdata, nttdata-oss) covering testing automation, Kubernetes plugins, and LLM observability tooling. NTT also drives the IOWN (Innovative Optical and Wireless Network) initiative, photonics and optical-quantum research, and responsible AI development across its R&D arm.

providers.name: Cowboy
providers.description: Cowboy is a Brussels-based mobility company that designs and manufactures premium connected electric bicycles for urban commuting. Its lineup — the Cruiser, Cruiser ST, Cross, and Cross ST — pairs a lightweight frame with removable batteries, integrated GPS tracking, crash detection, and its proprietary AdaptivePower motor assistance, all managed through the Cowboy mobile app. The company sells direct-to-consumer and through a network of 125+ service centers and mobile technicians across 40+ European cities, complemented by leasing, business, and student programs. Backed by Index Ventures, Cowboy operates a Shopify-based storefront and a connected-bike app platform; it does not publish a public developer API. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead and enriched with the company's real identity, legal, support, and security surfaces.

providers.name: Fightcamp
providers.description: FightCamp is a consumer connected-fitness company that sells an at-home boxing and kickboxing training system combining physical equipment (a free-standing bag, quick-wrap gloves, and Bluetooth motion-tracking punch trackers) with a subscription app of on-demand classes led by professional fighters. The trackers use motion sensors and AI to measure punch output, speed, and workout stats, syncing to a member app and customer dashboard for progress tracking. FightCamp is a direct-to-consumer hardware-plus-membership business (backed by IVP) and does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its public web, commerce, support, and domain-security surface for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Jala
providers.description: JALA is an Indonesian aquaculture technology company providing end-to-end solutions for the shrimp farming industry, describing itself as a fully connected system powered by data farmers can trust. It connects farmers, processors, and buyers through the JALA App for real-time pond monitoring and data analytics, the Baruni technology platform, farming supplies (post-larvae, feed, technical assistance), harvest and cold-chain logistics services, and traceable certified supply chains for processors and buyers. Backed by 500 Global, JALA operates a consumer/operator SaaS platform (app.jala.tech) rather than a public developer API program. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and enriched by the pipeline.

providers.name: SkyFoundry
providers.description: SkyFoundry, founded in 2009 and headquartered in Glen Allen, Virginia, develops SkySpark, an analytics and informatics platform that connects, stores, analyzes, and visualizes data from smart devices, automation and control systems, meters, and sensors to "find what matters" in large equipment and facility datasets. SkySpark automatically detects issues, patterns, deviations, faults, and cost-reduction opportunities across intelligent buildings, industrial, agriculture, energy, government, and healthcare facilities, and has been applied to over 15,000 buildings spanning more than a billion square feet. SkySpark is a native Project Haystack server: external applications integrate through the Haystack HTTP REST API (ops such as read, hisRead, hisWrite, pointWrite, watchSub/watchPoll, eval, commit, and nav) with Zinc, JSON, Trio, and CSV data formats, and authenticate using the Haystack SCRAM (SHA-256) handshake with bearer authTokens. The company sells through a network of 140+ OEM, systems-integrator, and value-added-distributor channel partners rather than a self-service public SaaS.

providers.name: Zebra Technologies
providers.description: Zebra Technologies is a global leader in barcode printing, RFID, mobile computing, and machine vision solutions for manufacturing, warehousing, healthcare, and retail. The Zebra Developer Portal and TechDocs expose cloud REST APIs for printing, device management, barcode generation, RFID IoT connectivity, asset tracking, and label design, enabling integration of Zebra hardware into enterprise workflows and manufacturing operations systems.

providers.name: Cloudpost Networks
providers.description: CloudPost Networks is a Santa Clara, California device-security company founded in 2015 that rebranded as Ordr (ordr.net). It builds an AI-powered device intelligence and network-security platform that discovers, classifies, and secures connected devices across IT, IoT, OT, and IoMT environments, tying device identity to behavioral analytics so organizations can detect risk and automatically apply micro-segmentation and enforcement policies. Ordr serves 500+ healthcare, banking, and manufacturing organizations and integrates with vendors such as Cisco, Palo Alto Networks, CrowdStrike, and Fortinet. It maintains SOC 2 Type 2 compliance. No public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal is published.

providers.name: Fort
providers.description: Fort is a Y Combinator (W26) hardware startup building a screenless wearable that automatically tracks strength training for people who care about longevity. Founded by three former Tesla engineers, the device uses heart rate and motion sensing to detect gym sessions, workout classes, sleep, and recovery without requiring the wearer to manually log reps, sets, or exercises, then delivers actionable feedback on how lifestyle factors affect strength progress. Fort is styled as jewelry rather than performance gear, ships in three finishes with 7+ day battery life, and pairs with Fort Foundations, an expert-led training program built around core movement patterns. The product is currently available for pre-order and has no public developer API or programmatic surface at this time; this profile captures the company's public web and commercial presence.

providers.name: Fueloyal
providers.description: Fueloyal is an automotive IoT and connected-vehicle platform company that builds proprietary IoT gateway hardware and software for fleet management, fuel management, predictive maintenance, dual dash cameras, EV services, and OEM connected-vehicle solutions. Its products help fleets and vehicle manufacturers monitor, connect, and service vehicles, with an OEM connected-platform and marketplace for delivering connected-vehicle services and mobile apps. Backed by Techstars, Fueloyal was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API specification was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Helloheart
providers.description: Hello Heart is a digital heart health company that combines a connected blood pressure monitor, an AI-guided mobile app, and clinical expertise to help people manage hypertension and cardiovascular risk. Its platform includes the Hello Heart app for blood pressure tracking and personalized guidance, a free connected blood pressure monitor for members, the Nia AI chatbot offering 24/7 heart-health support with clinical guardrails, and a forthcoming connected pill box for medication adherence. Hello Heart is sold primarily through employers, health plans, public sector organizations, labor unions, and benefits consultants, and reports outcomes such as fewer hospital days and per-member cost savings. Backed by Khosla Ventures, the company operates a consumer-facing digital health service and does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its identity, trust, and security posture in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Hykso
providers.description: Hykso, Inc. is the company behind FightCamp, an at-home boxing and kickboxing training system that pairs a free-standing bag, quick-wrap gloves, and wireless motion-tracking punch trackers with an on-demand library of trainer-led workouts. The Hykso punch trackers began as standalone wearable sensors that measure punch count, speed, and output for boxers and gyms, and now power FightCamp's real-time performance stats and workout scoring. This profile is a company stub in the API Evangelist network; Hykso/FightCamp is a direct-to-consumer connected-fitness brand and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Irhythmtech
providers.description: iRhythm Technologies is a publicly traded (NASDAQ: IRTC) digital healthcare company specializing in ambulatory cardiac monitoring for the detection and management of heart arrhythmias. Its Zio service pairs a wearable single-lead ECG biosensor patch (Zio monitor and Zio AT) with FDA-cleared AI/deep-learning algorithms, qualified cardiac technician verification, and cloud-based data analytics to produce end-of-wear diagnostic reports for clinicians. The platform includes the ZioSuite clinician portal for report interpretation and patient management, the MyZio patient app for symptom logging and education, EHR integration, and telehealth workflows. iRhythm was surfaced as a portfolio company of Norwest Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. It does not publish a public developer API or documentation portal; enrichment is limited to public identity, trust, and domain-security signals.

providers.name: Mero
providers.description: Mero is a Canadian SaaS platform for commercial building cleaning operations that uses smart sensors and analytics to automatically log, validate, and prove cleaning activity without manual input from janitorial staff. Its product is organized into three modules: Validate (hands-free proof that cleaning was completed), Dispatch (occupancy- and supply-driven scheduling), and Inspect (in-app QA and inspection tooling). Mero serves janitorial companies, property managers, and commercial facilities, with data captured across roughly 100M square feet at customers including Harvard, Colliers, and Toronto Pearson Airport. The company advertises a data-integration API and a Zapier connector to send and receive data with other tools, but publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable specification; API access is gated behind a sales demo.

providers.name: SAVA
providers.description: SAVA (sava.health) is a health-monitoring company developing a minimally invasive, continuous multi-molecule biosensor worn just beneath the skin. The platform is designed to capture real-time molecular data - glucose, lactate, ketones, sodium, histamine, urea, alcohol, and cortisol - and surface it through a connected mobile app, aiming to shift healthcare toward preventative monitoring and personal wellness. The company is early stage and pre-launch, operating a waiting-list model for early access to its device rather than a public product. It publishes no first-party developer API or health-data API; its marketing site is built on Wix and exposes the Wix Site MCP endpoint and a published llms.txt for agentic access to public site content only. Backed by Balderton Capital.

providers.name: iBasis
providers.description: iBasis is a global communications solutions provider serving mobile operators, MVNOs, over-the-top players, and IoT device companies worldwide. Its portfolio spans international and managed voice, 5G data roaming and roaming hub/breakout, A2P and RCS messaging monetization, and IoT connectivity built on eSIM technology, the Simfony connectivity-management platform, MVNO-as-a-Service, and fixed wireless access. iBasis also offers signaling and fraud security (FraudLock iQ360, Security iQ360, Signaling Vulnerability Scanner) and business intelligence for carriers. Customer and partner operations run through the eCare portal behind single sign-on; iBasis does not currently publish a public developer program, OpenAPI specifications, or SDKs. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of CRV and enriched from the public iBasis web presence and live domain probes.

providers.name: Justos
providers.description: Justos is a Brazilian digital auto insurance insurtech founded in 2020 and headquartered in Barueri, São Paulo. Operating as a managing general agent (MGA), Justos uses smartphone-collected driving data (telematics) to reward safe drivers with lower, usage-based pricing — advertised as up to 30% cheaper than traditional plans — plus weekly bonuses and perks like gas vouchers, maintenance, and ride credits. Its products are distributed digitally through a consumer mobile app and a broker (corretor) portal, with claims tracked in-app and 24/7 support. Backed by Ribbit Capital, Kaszek, SoftBank Latin America and GGV; its auto insurance is underwritten by Companhia Excelsior de Seguros (SUSEP code 05690). No public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal is published at this time.

providers.name: KITRO
providers.description: KITRO is a Swiss company founded in 2017 in Zurich that helps professional kitchens measure and reduce food waste through AI-powered automation. Its KITRO TARE device pairs an IoT scale with a camera and computer vision to automatically identify, weigh and categorize discarded food with no change to kitchen workflow, feeding a cloud analytics dashboard that surfaces waste trends by time, item and station, compares performance across properties, and exports reports for sustainability and EU food-waste compliance reporting. KITRO serves hotel groups and resorts, hospitals and care homes, corporate canteens, universities and schools, and river and ocean cruise operators in 20+ countries, with customers including Marriott, Hyatt, TUI BLUE, Pestana, 25hours Hotels and Sydney Opera Bar. KITRO publishes no public developer API, SDKs or developer portal — the only customer-facing software surface is the authenticated dashboard at my.kitro.ch — but it does publish an llms.txt agent-readable company description at www.kitro.ch/llms.txt.

providers.name: Squadle
providers.description: Squadle is a food safety and operational compliance platform for multi-unit restaurant and foodservice operations. It combines IoT remote temperature monitoring (its Remote Temperature System) with digital food-safety checklists, shift management, and patented ZeroTouch technology that automates temperature logging and triggers corrective actions. The platform reports 3.3B+ completed tasks and 100M+ temperatures measured. Squadle was acquired by Crunchtime and now operates as part of the Crunchtime Operations Execution platform; the squadle.com domain redirects to crunchtime.com/squadle. No public API or developer platform is currently published.

providers.name: Intenseye
providers.description: Intenseye is an AI-powered workplace safety platform that applies computer vision to a facility's existing CCTV cameras to detect unsafe conditions and behaviors in real time and prevent Serious Injuries and Fatalities (SIF). Its Environment, Health and Safety (EHS) product surfaces hazards, compliance gaps, and operational risks across manufacturing, logistics, food & beverage, and other high-risk industries, and can trigger Hard Stop emergency alerts. Intenseye offers cloud, private cloud, and on-premise deployment, is SOC 2 / AICPA certified and GDPR-aligned, uses AES-256 encryption at rest and TLS in transit, and does not use facial recognition. Backed by Insight Partners, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and Point Nine. Intenseye publishes no public API, SDK, or developer portal; product access is through its dashboard and login. It maintains a public GitHub organization of mostly open-source forks and workshops rather than first-party client libraries.

providers.name: Arrcus
providers.description: Arrcus is an AI-native networking software company that builds policy-driven routing, switching, and AI fabric spanning the edge, datacenter, and cloud. Its flagship ArcOS network operating system runs on merchant-silicon hardware and is complemented by ArcRR (scale-out route reflector), ArcIQ (analytics and visibility), ACE / ACE-AI (the Arrcus Connected Edge control and AI-networking platform), AINF (Arrcus Inference Network Fabric), and the TGAX AI switch. Arrcus targets GPU cluster connectivity for AI training and low-latency inferencing networks that reduce token cost. The company is venture backed by General Catalyst and Lightspeed Venture Partners. It exposes a login-gated customer portal and academy rather than a public developer API; no public OpenAPI, SDKs, or hosted API surface were found during enrichment.

providers.name: exein
providers.description: Exein is a Physical AI and embedded/IoT cybersecurity company (Italy) that secures connected devices, firmware, and Linux/RTOS embedded systems. Its platform pairs on-device runtime threat detection (Exein Runtime) with AI-powered firmware analysis and SBOM ingestion (Exein Analyzer), mapping findings to standards including the EU Cyber Resilience Act, ETSI EN 303-645, IEC 62443, RED 3.3, and the US Cyber Trust Mark. Exein does not publish a hosted public REST API; its developer surface is open-source security tooling in the exein-io GitHub organization — notably Pulsar (an eBPF-powered runtime security agent) and Kepler (a NIST-based CVE lookup store and API). Surfaced as a portfolio company of balderton-capital, hv-capital, and partech.

providers.name: Universal Electronics
providers.description: Universal Electronics Inc. (UEI) is a global leader in universal control and sensing technologies for the smart home, known for its QuickSet software platform, UEI TIDE smart thermostats and sensors, the Nevo white-label control platform, and the One For All retail remote-control brand. QuickSet Cloud provides device discovery, interoperability, and entertainment control via a device knowledge graph spanning roughly one million devices across 12,000 brands, with web APIs and native SDKs (Linux, Android, RDK, Android TV) offered to OEM and service-provider partners through a gated developer portal at developer.quicksetcloud.com. Surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio company; UEI publishes no public self-serve API.

providers.name: Cloudflare.com
providers.description: cloudflare-com is an alias profile for Cloudflare. The canonical company profile lives at the cloudflare repository in the API Evangelist Network; this entry exists so that the ".com" form of the brand resolves into the same canonical record. Cloudflare's developer surface includes a single unified REST API at api.cloudflare.com covering DNS, zones, SSL/TLS, Workers, KV, Durable Objects, Queues, R2, Pages, Stream, Email Routing, Zero Trust, WAF, Magic Transit, Spectrum, Load Balancing, Analytics, and Account Management. Authentication is via API tokens with scoped permissions or legacy global API keys.

providers.name: Eero
providers.description: eero makes home mesh Wi-Fi systems that are simple, powerful, secure, and reliable. eero pioneered home mesh wifi and sells products for homes, businesses, service providers, pro installers, and communities, including the eero Pro 7, eero PoE 7, and eero Signal, plus the eero Plus subscription for enhanced security and multi-network management. Devices are managed through the award-winning eero app and are deployed across 27+ countries. eero LLC is based in San Francisco, CA and is an Amazon company. eero does not publish a public developer API or first-party SDK; the eero app communicates with a private, unpublished backend.

providers.name: Omnitracs
providers.description: Omnitracs is a commercial fleet management, telematics, and transportation-management provider, now part of Solera Inc. (acquired 2021, operating under Solera Fleet Solutions). Its Omnitracs One platform and the Omnitracs Roadnet routing platform serve roughly 15,000 fleet customers with ELD / Hours-of-Service compliance, telematics and GPS positioning, driver workflow and messaging, routing and dispatch, and video safety. Omnitracs exposes real integration APIs and web services (Roadnet Web Services, the Services Portal Entity Management web services, and the SOAP/XML Event Subscription Service that streams positions, messages, HOS, and critical events), but access is partner- and customer-account gated - there is no open, self-service public developer portal. API credentials (a username/password with API access) and the integration developer wiki are provisioned to contracted customers and integration partners. Endpoints documented here for gated surfaces are honestly modeled from public integration notes, not from an open reference.

providers.name: Sensata Technologies
providers.description: Sensata Technologies is a major US corporation and Fortune 1000 company. The Sensata Technologies API provides programmatic access to its platform services, data, and integrations for enterprise customers and partners.

providers.name: Alif
providers.description: Alif Semiconductor is a Silicon Valley fabless semiconductor company building secure, ultra-low-power 32-bit microcontrollers and fusion processors for edge AI/ML. Its Ensemble, Ensemble Gen AI, and Balletto product families pair Arm Cortex-M and Cortex-A cores with dedicated Ethos-U55 neural processing units, hardware AI acceleration, wireless connectivity, and a multilayered security architecture so machine-learning and generative-AI workloads can run directly on battery-powered devices. Developer resources center on Zephyr-based SDKs, CMSIS device family packs, VS Code project templates, evaluation kits, datasheets, reference manuals, and the Conductor configuration tool rather than a hosted web API. The company is backed by Kleiner Perkins.

providers.name: Aeva
providers.description: Aeva Technologies is a Mountain View, California sensing and perception company that builds 4D LiDAR based on proprietary Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (FMCW) technology, measuring instant velocity in addition to 3D position for every point in a scene. Its product line spans Atlas and Atlas Ultra long-range automotive-grade sensors, the Omni wide-view short-range sensor, and Eve 1 precision laser speed sensors for factory automation, serving autonomous vehicles, robotics, industrial automation, security, and physical-AI markets. Aeva is a hardware and perception-software provider rather than a web-API company: its developer surface is open-source software on the aevainc GitHub org (the AevaScenes Python SDK and Doppler ICP), the AevaScenes dataset, and product SDK/EULA-gated software delivered with its sensors. No public REST or web API is published.

providers.name: Plumerai
providers.description: Plumerai builds AI software for intelligent cameras that pairs tiny on-device edge AI models with cloud Vision Language Models (VLMs). Its Video Intelligence products cover detection of people, vehicles, animals and packages, Familiar Face Identification, cross-camera Re-Identification, noise-robust motion detection, VLM-based video search, and custom AI notifications. The Plumerai Inference Engine is a deep-learning model compiler and runtime optimized for CPU inference on Arm Cortex-M / Cortex-A, RISC-V and x86_64. Plumerai integrates via SDKs (C++, C, Python, Rust, Java) rather than a hosted REST API, with the same unified API running from microcontrollers to servers. Plumerai also maintains the open-source Larq ecosystem for training and running Binarized Neural Networks.

providers.name: TE Connectivity
providers.description: TE Connectivity is a global manufacturer of connectors and sensors headquartered in Galway, Ireland with operational headquarters in Berwyn, Pennsylvania. TE provides electrical connectivity and sensor solutions for transportation, industrial, and communications markets, with strong automotive Tier 1 supply relationships.

providers.name: KitchenMate
providers.description: KitchenMate is a Toronto-based autonomous retail and workplace food-service company that operates 24/7 unattended micro-markets built around two pieces of proprietary hardware, a checkout-free Smart Fridge that uses vision sensors to detect what a customer removes and bill them automatically, and induction-based Smart Cookers that heat chef-prepared entrees in seven to ten minutes. The kiosks are installed in workplaces, condominiums, schools, hospitals and other commercial locations, require roughly seven square feet plus standard electrical and network connectivity, and accept Visa, Mastercard, Amex, Apple Pay and Google Pay at the unit. A companion iOS and Android app carries loyalty rewards, dietary filters and meal feedback. The company has since rebranded its platform business as Micromart, which markets the same autonomous smart-store technology under the tagline "Be anywhere. Sell anything." across a stated 2,000+ locations in North America. KitchenMate publishes no public API, developer portal or SDKs; this profile captures its identity and probed security posture only.

providers.name: ServiceMax
providers.description: ServiceMax is asset-centric field service management (FSM) software that helps equipment manufacturers and service organizations maximize equipment uptime, optimize technician productivity, and streamline service delivery. Its cloud platform, built natively on the Salesforce platform (ServiceMax Core and Asset 360), spans work order and workflow management, scheduling and dispatch (Service Board), preventive and predictive maintenance, contract and entitlement management, parts and inventory, offline-capable mobile tools (ServiceMax Go), real-time technician collaboration (Zinc), and customer self-service (Engage). Founded in 2007 and acquired by PTC in 2023, ServiceMax integrates with PTC's IoT and PLM portfolio (ThingWorx, Windchill) and exposes its data and workflows through the underlying Salesforce API surface rather than a standalone public developer API.

providers.name: str8bat
providers.description: str8bat is a Bangalore, India based sports-technology company that builds a pocket-sized IoT sensor which attaches to a cricket bat and captures batting metrics in real time — bat speed, impact speed, back-lift angle, timing, sweet-spot placement and a 360-degree view of every shot. The sensor pairs with the str8bat mobile app (iOS and Android) to deliver instant, visual and actionable insights plus an AI cricket coach. The company reports 30,000+ active users, 6+ million shots recorded and operations across 350+ Indian cities and 14+ countries. str8bat is a consumer hardware and mobile-app company and publishes no first-party developer API; its str8bat.com storefront runs on Shopify, which exposes standard commerce discovery surfaces (customer-account OIDC and a Universal Commerce Protocol agent-commerce MCP endpoint).

providers.name: Aclima
providers.description: Aclima is a San Francisco-based environmental intelligence company that maps and analyzes air pollution and greenhouse gas emissions at hyperlocal, block-by-block resolution. Using a network of roving (vehicle-mounted) and stationary sensors, Aclima measures multiple pollutants and climate gases simultaneously at up to 100,000x greater resolution than traditional monitoring, then translates billions of scientific measurements into environmental intelligence for governments, companies, and communities. Its professional analytics software, Aclima Pro, delivers visualization and automated analytics for emissions reduction and public-health programs, while its free air.health app maps address-level air and climate insights for the communities Aclima serves. Co-founded by CEO Davida Herzl, Aclima is backed by DCVC and is added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: EyeLights
providers.description: EyeLights is a French deep-tech company building augmented reality head-up display (HUD) technology for riders and pilots. Its products project GPS navigation, speed, intercom, radar and call information into the rider's line of sight: EyeRide, a universal HUD accessory compatible with any motorcycle helmet; the GT-AIR 3 Smart, an integrated head-up display visor built into a SHOEI helmet; the APEX HUD glasses for general aviation; and Pulse Ultra, a universal Bluetooth intercom. The company sells direct-to-consumer through a Shopify storefront at eye-lights.com and runs customer support on Odoo. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio lead; EyeLights publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time, so this record captures its consumer web, identity, and security posture rather than an API contract.

providers.name: Freedom Robotics
providers.description: Freedom Robotics is a San Francisco-based robotics infrastructure company founded in 2017 that builds mission-critical software to help robotics companies build, operate, support, and scale heterogeneous robot fleets. Its cloud platform — sometimes referred to as Mission Control — provides device and fleet management, remote teleoperation (Pilot), live data streaming, smart alerts and notifications, fleet maps and heatmaps, deployment and service management, remote development, and analytics across cobots, industrial robots, AMRs, drones, and custom hardware. The platform is robot- and OS-agnostic, installs on a device in seconds via a single-line Freedom Agent installer, and integrates with ROS, ROS 2, Python, microcontrollers, Protobuf, Docker, and the cloud offerings of AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure. Freedom exposes a public REST API at api.freedomrobotics.ai covering accounts, devices, alerts, statistics, uploads, tokens, users, user groups, and zones, plus a Python SDK (freedomrobotics.link) with Link, MicroLink, message, log, image, and command-callback primitives for programmatic control and telemetry of large numbers of robots. The company has raised approximately $17M in venture funding and operates on a per-robot subscription model (publicly cited at roughly $300 per robot per month) with custom enterprise plans negotiated through sales.

providers.name: Imperfect
providers.description: Imperfect (Imperfect Wellness, Inc.) is a San Francisco-based, Y Combinator-backed (Spring 2026) consumer startup building an adaptive AI training coach for endurance athletes across cycling, trail running, swimming, and other sports. The mobile app connects to a user's wearables and health apps to generate real-time training, recovery, and nutrition recommendations that adapt to how the athlete's body is actually responding day to day, rather than following a static plan written weeks in advance. Founded by Matin Tamizi (previously built and sold two fintech companies and authored a widely used open-source Garmin library used by Stanford Health). Imperfect ships as a consumer mobile application (Google Play) and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Revivn
providers.description: Revivn provides an integrated hardware lifecycle platform for managing end-of-life IT equipment. The company handles secure device pickup, certified data sanitization and destruction, and redistribution of usable hardware to underserved communities through nonprofit partnerships. Its software surface (the Revivn App at app.revivn.com) lets IT and asset-management teams schedule retrievals, track chain-of-custody, generate compliance and sustainability reporting, and — per Revivn's marketing — integrate Revivn's API with their IT software stack for customized workflows. No public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI, or SDK is published; the integration API appears to be a private, enterprise-only surface. Revivn is a 500 Global portfolio company.

providers.name: Hidrate
providers.description: HidrateSpark is the world's smartest water bottle brand, tracking daily water intake with a Bluetooth-connected sensor puck that glows to remind you to drink and syncs to the HidrateSpark hydration app, Fitbit, and Apple Watch. The company (originally Hidrate, Inc., a Techstars-backed startup) sells its smart bottles and accessories through a Shopify-hosted direct-to-consumer storefront at hidratespark.com. It does not publish a first-party developer or product API; the only machine-facing surface is the Shopify platform layer — OIDC/OAuth customer accounts and the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) agent-commerce endpoints that let buyer-approved AI shopping agents browse and check out.

providers.name: Juxta
providers.description: Juxta is a San Francisco positioning-technology company building a hardware-free Universal Positioning System (UPS) that delivers real-time indoor and outdoor tracking for people, assets, and robots with sub-meter accuracy indoors and roughly 3-meter accuracy outdoors. Rather than relying on satellites, beacons, or cameras, Juxta uses the inertial (IMU) sensors already present in mobile devices, robots, and machinery combined with machine-learning "synthetic fingerprinting" to map and track subjects in GPS-denied environments such as warehouses, hospitals, underground facilities, and battlefields. Its drag-and-drop deployment ingests a floorplan, satellite image, or CAD file and goes live in hours, priced by mapped area and assets tracked. Juxta serves defense, logistics and robotics, and healthcare, and is backed by Y Combinator and other early-stage investors. Access today is through a partner portal and booked demo; no public developer API is documented.

providers.name: Roborock
providers.description: Roborock is a global consumer robotics company best known for its robot vacuum and mop cleaners, wet/dry wash-and-fill floor washers, and connected home-cleaning appliances controlled through the Roborock mobile app. Founded in 2014 and headquartered in Beijing, the company was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. Roborock operates a private cloud that backs its consumer mobile app but publishes no public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or SDK program. It does operate a public Trust Center documenting the security and privacy design of its IoT products, including TÜV Rheinland EN 303 645 and UL Diamond IoT Security certifications.

providers.name: Versuni
providers.description: Versuni is a global domestic-appliances company headquartered in Amsterdam, Netherlands, formed when Philips Domestic Appliances was carved out and acquired by Hillhouse Investment in 2021. With more than 130 years of heritage, roughly 6,400 employees and a presence in over 100 countries, Versuni designs and sells cooking, coffee, garment-care, floor-care and climate-care products under brands including Philips, Saeco, Gaggia, Preethi, Senseo and L'OR Barista. Its connected appliances are supported by the consumer HomeID app (formerly NutriU). Versuni publishes no public developer API program; its public API-adjacent surface is limited to an RFC 9116 security.txt and a responsible-disclosure program.

providers.name: Optiwatt
providers.description: Optiwatt is a consumer-centric energy management platform that helps electric-vehicle drivers and homeowners lower their electricity bills by automatically scheduling EV charging and smart-thermostat use for off-peak, low-cost, and low-carbon hours. Its consumer app (getoptiwatt.com) connects to vehicles, chargers, and thermostats via direct OEM integrations such as the Tesla Fleet API and aggregators like Smartcar, while its utility platform (optiwatt.com) orchestrates these distributed energy resources as virtual power plants across demand-response and load-shaping programs for utility partners. Backed by GV. Optiwatt is primarily a consumer of third-party APIs rather than a public API producer; no public developer API or OpenAPI has been found.

providers.name: Trackonomy
providers.description: Trackonomy is a supply chain visibility company that digitizes real-world operations with barely-there smart label sensors. Its SmartTape and THL Tape products provide item-level tracking, monitoring location, temperature, humidity, and light in real time, while its platform connects, automates, controls, and remediates operations processes at global scale for logistics, industrial, utilities, healthcare, government, and airline customers. Trackonomy is backed by 8VC. It advertises a customizable RESTful API and webhook-based real-time data exchange for platform customers, but publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Optivolt Labs
providers.description: Optivolt Labs (operating as Optivolt) is a Burlingame, California solar technology company building intelligent home solar systems with power electronics embedded directly inside each panel. Its patented Balancer device shuffles power from stronger to weaker zones within a panel to keep energy flowing in shaded and non-ideal conditions, delivering up to 50% more annual energy and improved shaded performance versus conventional panels. The product line includes 450W N-type mono half-cut panels, universal battery and inverter compatibility, and a real-time monitoring app for tracking energy and savings. Optivolt is a Techstars-backed hardware company; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Biobeat
providers.description: Biobeat Technologies is an Israeli med-tech company whose remote patient monitoring (RPM) health-AI platform pairs a disposable short-term chest-monitor and a reusable long-term wrist-monitor - both using a photoplethysmography (PPG) sensor - to continuously track up to 13 vital signs, including FDA-cleared cuffless blood pressure, pulse rate, respiratory rate, blood oxygen saturation, temperature, stroke volume, cardiac output, and one-lead ECG (chest-monitor). Readings stream to Biobeat's HIPAA- and GDPR-compliant, cloud-based patient management platform, where clinicians view real-time data, trends, and configurable alerts. Biobeat offers programmatic data access and EMR/EHR integration as a paid add-on for hospitals, health systems, and research partners; there is no publicly documented self-serve developer API.

providers.name: Conservation Labs
providers.description: Conservation Labs is a Pittsburgh-based smart water technology company, backed by Techstars, Amazon, RET Ventures and SustainVC. Its flagship product, H2know, is a clamp-on acoustic smart water monitor that measures a building's inbound pipe every second and uses patented sound-detection technology and machine learning to translate those signals into accurate water-flow estimates, leak alerts and water-usage insights delivered through a companion mobile and web app. The company also offers Sustainable Machines, an edge-to-cloud platform for machine condition monitoring and predictive maintenance. Conservation Labs serves residential homes, commercial real estate, restaurants and hotels, and industrial operators. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes a consumer-facing app but publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or webhook documentation.

providers.name: Mill
providers.description: Mill is a consumer sustainability company that makes a smart kitchen bin which dries and grinds household food scraps overnight into dry, nutrient-rich "Food Grounds," keeping food waste out of landfills and cutting the methane it would otherwise produce. Sold as a membership starting around $799 or roughly $66/month, the bin is odorless, reduces food-waste volume by about 80%, and the resulting grounds are reused in gardens, as chicken feed, or through farm partnerships. Mill also runs a commercial line for grocery, offices, food service, and municipalities. Backed by GV (Google Ventures), Mill is a consumer hardware and subscription business with a companion mobile app; it exposes no public developer API — its /api/ path is an internal app backend disallowed in robots.txt.

providers.name: Fleetmatics
providers.description: Fleetmatics was a fleet management, telematics, and GPS vehicle tracking SaaS company whose Reveal platform tracked commercial vehicles, drivers, and mobile assets for small and mid-sized fleets. Founded in Dublin and later headquartered in Massachusetts, Fleetmatics IPO'd on the NYSE in 2012 and was acquired by Verizon in 2016 for about USD 2.4 billion, becoming the core of Verizon Connect. Its Reveal platform exposes a documented REST API and webhook suite - the Fleetmatics Integration Manager (FIM) / Reveal Integration Services APIs - covering vehicles, drivers, GPS positions and history, trips and segments, driver status and safety, hours-of-service logbooks, geofences (places), groups, and non-powered asset tracking. The API gateway still runs on Fleetmatics-branded hosts (fim.api.us.fleetmatics.com); access is gated to Reveal customers and approved integration partners who request Integration Manager and Reveal REST credentials before calling the documented endpoints. The Fleetmatics brand now redirects to Verizon Connect.

providers.name: Highway 9 Networks
providers.description: Highway 9 Networks delivers AI Wireless Infrastructure as a Service, providing secure private mobile networks and deterministic 5G connectivity for enterprise AI workloads. Its Virtual Mobile/AI Cloud (VMC) platform combines a cloud control plane (Mobile Center), distributed edge running a 5G core and AI services (Mobile Edge), private 5G wireless infrastructure (Mobile Network), and connected device and robot fleets (Mobile Zones) to give autonomous robots, cameras, and edge devices ultra-reliable, ultra-low-latency connectivity across manufacturing, warehousing, higher education, and energy environments. Highway 9 exposes Mobile Center streaming APIs for orchestration, telemetry, device management, alerting, and analytics, though the full specification is available only through its partner portal for signed partners. The company is backed by Mayfield and was added to the API Evangelist network as an enriched provider profile.

providers.name: Tile (thetileapp)
providers.description: Tile is a consumer Bluetooth-tracker company whose Tile Mate, Pro, Slim, and Sticker devices help people find everyday items such as keys, wallets, bags, and phones, backed by the crowd-sourced Tile "Find" network that anonymously relays location when another Tile user passes a lost item. Founded in 2012, Tile was acquired by Life360 in 2021 and now operates as part of the Life360 family-safety platform. Tile publishes consumer apps for iOS and Android and a support and legal surface, but does not offer an official public developer API, developer portal, or SDK; only third-party community libraries wrap its private app API. This API Evangelist profile captures the company's public web and security-program surface. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Slow Ventures.

providers.name: Cactos
providers.description: Cactos is a Finnish clean-energy company that designs, manufactures, and operates smart battery energy storage systems (BESS) for commercial, industrial, and grid-scale use. Its hardware line (Cactos Mylo commercial storage and Cactos Cardo backup power, built in part from second-life Tesla EV batteries) is paired with Cactos Spine, a cloud software platform that optimizes each unit for load shifting, peak shaving, demand-charge reduction, solar self-consumption, backup power during outages, and participation in electricity and grid-balancing markets. Cactos serves logistics, manufacturing, EV charging, agriculture, real estate, and commercial-property operators. It is a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures. As of this profile, Cactos publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation; the Cactos Spine app at app.cactos.com is a customer-facing management console rather than a documented developer API.

providers.name: Nova Labs
providers.description: Nova Labs, Inc. is the company behind the Helium Network, a decentralized wireless network that replaces traditional carrier infrastructure with community-hosted Hotspots and is coordinated on the Solana blockchain and incentivized with the HNT token. Helium operates two networks: a global LoRaWAN network for low-power IoT devices and a cellular/Wi-Fi offload network for mobile connectivity (Helium Mobile). Nova Labs open-sources the network's protocol surface as gRPC/Protobuf service definitions (the helium/proto config, router, and proof-of-coverage services) and publishes a set of first-party client libraries, a command-line tool, and Rust crates for cryptography and protobuf types. This profile was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and enriched from Nova Labs' public developer surface; much of the legacy Helium IoT REST API tooling is archived following the network's migration to Solana.

providers.name: Robotiq
providers.description: Robotiq designs and manufactures collaborative robotics hardware and software — adaptive grippers, vacuum grippers, force-torque sensors, wrist cameras, and pre-engineered workcells for palletizing, machine tending, screwdriving, and assembly. Founded in 2008 and headquartered in Lévis, Quebec, Canada, the company helps manufacturers automate repetitive tasks by embedding task intelligence ("Intelligence Made Physical") directly into end-of-arm tooling for platforms such as Universal Robots, FANUC CRX, and Omron/Techman. Robotiq publishes open-source ROS drivers and a C++ gripper SDK through its GitHub organization, but it does not operate a public web/REST API — this profile captures its developer-facing identity, open-source SDKs, and domain security posture rather than a hosted API surface.

providers.name: Beewise
