providers.description: Beewise is an agricultural technology company building the BeeHome, an AI- and robotics-enabled beehive that autonomously monitors, cares for, and protects honeybee colonies to reduce colony loss and deliver reliable pollination. Founded to address bee colony collapse, Beewise combines computer vision, robotics, and cloud software to detect pests and disease, regulate hive climate, and dispatch precision pollination for growers. The company serves growers with guaranteed pollination services, beekeepers with technology-enhanced hive management, and property owners through its Bees for Buildings program. Beewise is a venture-backed company (Insight Partners portfolio) surfaced into the API Evangelist network; it operates a customer grower portal but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Bloxtel, Inc.
providers.description: Bloxtel, Inc. builds a decentralized private 5G platform that lets enterprises deploy standalone 5G networks in hours. Its all-in-one 5G Access Point runs Open6GC, Bloxtel's decentralized network core, and pairs with tokenized dSIM electronic-SIM technology and a Web3 Operator dApp for configuring networks, managing dSIM subscriptions, and AI-powered predictive maintenance. Solutions span indoor coverage, SIM-swap protection, neutral hosting, peer nodes, and network analytics, targeting lower latency, reduced threat surface, and lower cost versus traditional carrier deployments. Backed by 500 Global. As of this profile Bloxtel publishes a marketing and lead-generation site only, with no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI, or SDK yet available.

providers.name: Cool Planet
providers.description: CoolPlanet is an enterprise energy-management and decarbonisation software company. Its platform, CoolPlanetOS, centralises real-time energy data across multi-site industrial estates, applies AI-driven anomaly detection and efficiency insights, benchmarks performance across facilities, and automates energy and compliance reporting. CoolPlanet pairs the software with consulting and on-site execution services to help manufacturing, pharmaceutical, food and beverage, commercial real estate, mining and shipping enterprises cut energy costs and carbon emissions. Backed by GV (Google Ventures). No public developer API surface is currently published.

providers.name: Datakrew
providers.description: Datakrew is a Singapore-based deep-tech company, a spin-off from NTU Singapore supported by Enterprise Singapore, building EV battery intelligence, fleet management, and AI-driven telematics for logistics and delivery, public transport, vehicle OEMs, rental/leasing and shared mobility operators, and mining and construction fleets. Its integrated hardware, software, and AI stack spans the OxRed (MyFleet) fleet-management and intelligence platform, OxRed Lens camera-based visualization telematics, OxRed AutoCert automated certification and compliance, GuardianAI driver-safety and collision-warning analytics, the Ask OX natural-language fleet assistant, and the ITUS Max and ITUS AutoScan edge terminals for telemetry, CAN-bus integration, and vehicle diagnostics, all aimed at optimizing battery health, safety, and operational efficiency.

providers.name: HelloTech
providers.description: HelloTech is a consumer technology-services company providing in-home and online tech support across the United States through a nationwide network of vetted technicians. Services span computer and printer repair, WiFi and home-networking setup, mobile-device support, audio/video and home-theater installation, TV mounting, smart-home device installation, and home-security setup, offered on-demand or through a HelloTech Home membership plan. HelloTech operates as a consumer services brand and does not publish a public developer API; this profile tracks its public web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Illumix
providers.description: Illumix is an enterprise-grade spatial AI company spun out of Stanford's Computer Science Department, providing a core stack for real-world location intelligence that runs at the edge with centimeter-level precision. Its hardware-agnostic platform delivers sub-second localization and 3D mapping across mobile devices, AR/VR wearables, and robotics using standard cameras — with no LiDAR or GPS dependency — combining multimodal vision-language AI with long-term memory that learns behavior over time. Illumix serves AI/XR wearables, enterprise and logistics, defense and security, location-based entertainment, and robotics, with deployments referenced for Disney, Six Flags, Cedar Fair, MGM Resorts, Warner Bros, Verizon, and Sony. The company markets developer APIs and an SDK as part of a full-stack offering, but publishes no public developer portal, reference documentation, or machine-readable API specification at this time.

providers.name: Myndlift
providers.description: Myndlift is a digital neurofeedback and mental-health company that pairs a consumer/clinical mobile app with a wearable EEG brain-sensing headband (Muse) to deliver therapist-guided, personalized brain-training programs. The platform provides brain mapping and assessments, gamified real-time neurofeedback sessions, progress tracking, and remote-monitoring dashboards used by both individuals and mental-health practitioners for attention, anxiety, stress, sleep, and peak-performance goals. Backed by 500 Global, the company reports 26,000+ members and more than one million neurofeedback sessions delivered. No public developer API, SDK, or developer portal is currently published; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record with verified identity links.

providers.name: Pebble
providers.description: Pebble is a Silicon Valley electric-vehicle and consumer-hardware company that designs and manufactures the Pebble Flow, an all-electric travel trailer (RV) with an integrated battery, solar, and motor-assist drivetrain. The product line pairs the trailer with the Pebble mobile app for remote control and monitoring, offering features such as autonomous "Magic Hitch" coupling, remote-control positioning, automatic leveling and setup, and up to seven days of off-grid capability. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, Pebble sells direct-to-consumer under the tagline "Where Home Meets the Road." As of this enrichment pass Pebble publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or documented API surface; its only software touchpoint is the consumer-facing Pebble Control Center app.

providers.name: Retrocausal
providers.description: Retrocausal builds AI-powered copilot software for manufacturing operations, applying patented computer vision and machine learning to manual assembly lines. Its products include Assembly Copilot (real-time AI-tracked work instructions, poka-yoke error prevention, and cycle-level video traceability), Kaizen Copilot (AI-powered time studies, standard work, automatic line balancing, and ergonomic analysis for industrial engineers), and Ergo Copilot (ergonomic risk assessment from smartphone video). The platform runs on AWS, is ISO 27001 certified, and integrates with MES systems, OPC UA for PLCs and smart tools, barcode scanners, torque wrenches, light towers, and projectors, with SSO via Azure Active Directory and Okta. Retrocausal is a Techstars portfolio company. It publishes no public developer API; integrations are delivered as custom MES/OPC UA and identity connections rather than a developer platform.

providers.name: Runwise
providers.description: Runwise provides wireless smart-control systems that automate heating, cooling, water, and gas infrastructure in multifamily and commercial buildings. Its retrofit hardware and cloud platform replace legacy boiler, steam, and HVAC controls, cutting heating, cooling, and water bills by roughly 23% with same-day installation. Runwise reports more than 10,300 buildings under management and over $175 million in cumulative utility savings for customers. The company is backed by Fifth Wall, Initialized Capital, and Menlo Ventures. This API Evangelist profile tracks Runwise's public web presence; as of this pass no public API, developer portal, or programmatic integration surface has been identified.

providers.name: Sioma
providers.description: SIOMA is a Colombian precision-agriculture (agtech) software platform for tropical crops such as oil palm, banana, and cacao. It helps plantations monitor field labor, track harvest and weighing (pesaje) operations with GPS, and make data-driven decisions to raise productivity. The product combines a mobile field-management app, GPS-based labor tracking, smart weighing hardware (Nukak, Sigma, Jaco, and Bascula-G scales), and Siomi, an AI assistant for agriculture. SIOMA is delivered as a customer web and mobile application and is backed by 500 Global. No public API or developer program is currently published.

providers.name: Smartex
providers.description: Smartex is an AI and computer-vision company founded in 2018 and headquartered in Porto, Portugal that builds hardware-enabled software for the textile manufacturing industry. Its systems inspect fabric in real time on the knitting machine to detect defects at the source, cutting textile waste, CO2 emissions, water, energy and rework. The product suite spans CORE (a machine-vision inspection add-on for circular knitting machines), FACT (an all-in-one digital factory-management platform for production visibility and quality control) and LOOP (supply-chain communication and traceability). Smartex is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, DCVC, Tony Fadell's Build Collective, H&M Group, SOSV/HAX, Spider Capital, Momenta Ventures and Fashion for Good. It does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; customer access is through the FACT platform login. This profile was surfaced from the VC-portfolio pipeline and enriched from Smartex's public web surface.

providers.name: Synapsor
providers.description: Synapsor (legal entity Ottai Technology (Wuxi) Co. Ltd.) is a Chinese medical-device company based in Wuxi, Jiangsu that develops AI-powered, medical-grade smart wearable devices. Its flagship product is the Ottai continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) system - a waterproof, calibration-free wearable sensor paired with a mobile app and AI assistant for 24/7 glucose tracking and diabetes management, sold in China and internationally via ottai.com. Investors include Qiming Venture Partners, Huatai Zijin Investment, Wuxi Industry Development Group, YuanBio Venture Capital, and Shunwei Capital. Synapsor publishes no public developer API, portal, or machine-readable API specifications as of July 2026.

providers.name: Automox
providers.description: Automox is a cloud-native IT operations and endpoint management platform that automates patching, configuration, and software deployment across Windows, macOS, and Linux devices from a single console. The Automox API is a REST API that gives developers programmatic access to organizations, zones, devices, groups, policies, packages, worklets, commands, events, reports, and users for building integrations and automating endpoint management workflows, authenticated with API keys.

providers.name: Natural Cycles
providers.description: Natural Cycles is a Swedish women's-health company behind the first birth-control application cleared by the US FDA (2018) and CE-marked in Europe as a Class IIb medical device. Its subscription app uses a proprietary temperature-based algorithm to identify fertile and non-fertile days from a user's daily basal body temperature, supporting both preventing and planning pregnancy as well as cycle, ovulation, and perimenopause tracking. Temperature is captured with a paired Bluetooth basal thermometer or through consumer wearables the app integrates with — Apple Watch, Oura Ring, and the NC B1 band. Natural Cycles publishes clinical research, an educational content library (CycleMatters), an e-commerce shop for thermometers and tests, and a public bug-bounty / responsible-disclosure program, but it does not expose a public developer API, developer portal, or OpenAPI. Backed by EQT Ventures.

providers.name: Rex Inc
providers.description: Rex Inc, operating as Rex.fit (BabylonAI Inc.), is a Y Combinator (W23) health and fitness company building AI-powered, fully automated nutrition tracking. Its consumer products include Rex Nutribot, a WhatsApp AI nutrition coach; the Drop, a wearable AI camera pendant that detects meals and automatically logs calories, protein, carbs, and fats via computer vision; an AI body scanner; and personalized coaching with daily health reports. Rex also offers a white-label B2B nutrition-and-fitness AI that fitness chains and app builders integrate to add meal logging (photo, barcode, or text), recipe and meal-plan generation, workout logging, 3D body scans, and nutrition analytics under their own brand.

providers.name: WOO Sports
providers.description: WOO Sports makes a sensor-based performance-tracking system for kitesurfing, wingfoiling, and windsurfing. The WOO 4.0 device mounts to a board and measures jump height, airtime, G-force, and landing impact, syncing sessions through the WOO Sports mobile apps (iOS, Android, Apple Watch, Wear OS, and Garmin) to a global community platform with leaderboards, spots, activity feeds, and events. More than 100,000 riders use WOO to track sessions and compete, including on the GKA Kite World Tour. WOO Sports is a Techstars-backed brand operated under Boards & More. This profile was enriched from the provider's public web surface; no public developer API was found (docs.woosports.com is a consumer user guide, not an API reference).

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: Gridware
providers.description: Gridware builds grid intelligence technology for electric utilities. Its Active Grid Response (AGR) platform pairs pole-mounted GridScope sensors with analytics to bring real-time visibility into the physical, electrical, and environmental condition of every span of the distribution grid, closing the "Hazard Awareness Delay" between when a fault or hazard occurs and when a utility detects it. Gridware supports fault prevention, faster power restoration, wildfire and hazard response, and grid asset management. Headquartered in San Francisco with an Applied Research Complex in Richmond, California, the company is backed by True Ventures. Gridware does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation; this profile captures its public identity, trust/compliance posture, and domain security.

providers.name: Hesai Technology
providers.description: Hesai Technology is a global leader in 3D LiDAR perception, designing and manufacturing high-performance lidar sensors for autonomous driving, advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS), robotics, and industrial automation. Its sensors are deployed by major automotive OEMs and autonomous-vehicle companies across more than 40 countries. Hesai does not expose a public REST/HTTP API; its developer surface is source-distributed C++ SDKs, ROS and ROS2 drivers, and integration plugins (including an NVIDIA DriveWorks plugin) published on the HesaiTechnology GitHub organization, alongside a developer portal and downloadable firmware, manuals, and tools. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from Hesai's public developer resources.

providers.name: Stellapps
providers.description: Stellapps is an end-to-end dairy technology company from Bangalore, India (IIT Madras incubated, founded 2011) that digitizes milk production, milk procurement, and cold-chain management through its SmartMoo full-stack IoT platform. Sensors in milking systems, animal wearables, chilling equipment, and procurement peripherals stream data to the SmartMoo Big Data Cloud for analytics and machine learning serving dairy farmers, cooperatives, and processors, with applications including mooON herd management, smartAMCU and smartCC milk procurement, ConTrak cold-chain monitoring, mooFlow ERP, and mooPay financial services. Stellapps publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs; the SmartMoo platform is accessed through hosted applications behind CAS single sign-on.

providers.name: Vodafone
providers.description: Vodafone Group plc is a UK-headquartered (Newbury, England) multinational telecommunications company and one of the world's largest mobile and fixed network operators, with operations in 15 country markets and partner-market agreements covering 40+ additional countries across Europe and Africa. The group serves 279 million mobile customers, 5 million business customers, and manages 215+ million IoT connections through its Vodafone IoT platform. Beyond mobile and broadband connectivity, Vodafone operates one of the largest IoT/M2M businesses in the industry, invests in 70+ subsea cables, and runs financial services like M-PESA (Africa) and Vodapay. Through Vodafone Business it sells connectivity, cloud, security, and managed-mobility services to enterprises, and through the GSMA Open Gateway and CAMARA initiative it exposes a growing portfolio of standardised network APIs (Number Verify, SIM Swap, Quality on Demand, Device Location, Match, MVNO Discovery, and more) via the Vodafone Developer Marketplace (developer.vodafone.com), which publishes 27+ commercial and CAMARA APIs across Identity, Mobile, Analytics, Boost/QoS, and Partner categories. The Marketplace exposes sandbox and live endpoints under api-sandbox.vf-dmp.engineering.vodafone.com and api.vf-dmp.engineering.vodafone.com, with OAuth2 (Consumer Key / Consumer Secret) authentication and Postman collections for every product. Vodafone is a premier member of the CAMARA alliance hosted at the Linux Foundation, a founding participant in the GSMA Open Gateway, and one of the principal telco operators driving network-as-an-API adoption globally.

providers.name: Zwift
providers.description: Zwift is a Long Beach, California online fitness company that operates a multiplayer indoor cycling and running platform combining stationary smart trainers and bikes with a 3D virtual-world game client. Riders and runners use a smart trainer, smart bike (such as the in-house Zwift Ride), treadmill, or pod to drive an avatar through fictional worlds (Watopia, Makuri Islands) and licensed real-world routes, joining structured workouts, group rides, races, training plans, and 24/7 events alongside a global community of more than a million members. The platform pairs with smart trainers and heart-rate monitors over Bluetooth and ANT+, and the Zwift Companion mobile app provides in-game messaging, ride control, and route discovery. Zwift does not operate a general public developer portal, OpenAPI reference, or open-source SDK. Its developer surface is limited to a private, application-only Structured Training API for approved training partners (TrainingPeaks, TrainerRoad, Wahoo SYSTM, JOIN Cycling and similar coaching platforms) that lets external workout builders push custom workouts into a rider's Zwift account, plus one-way activity-export connections to Strava, TrainingPeaks, Garmin Connect, MapMyRide, MapMyRun, Adidas Running, Technogym, Fitbit, Wahoo, Apple Health, and Withings. There is no public REST surface, OAuth client registration, or partner self-service available to general developers — third-party tools (community libraries, ZwiftPower, Sauce for Zwift) interact with Zwift via reverse-engineered private endpoints, not a sanctioned API. Zwift is a paid consumer subscription business; revenue comes from monthly memberships and hardware sales (Zwift Ride, Zwift Cog, Zwift Click, Zwift Play).

providers.name: Boldr
providers.description: Boldr is a Techstars-backed consumer hardware company building energy-saving smart home climate control devices. Its two products are Kelvin, a smart infrared heater, and Klima, a smart thermostat controller for mini-split air conditioners that also monitors appliance health so units last longer with fewer issues. Both devices are managed through the Boldr mobile app, which lets homeowners control climate settings remotely and track energy usage to lower utility bills. Boldr also runs Boldr Pro, a program for HVAC contractors. The company sells direct to consumers through a Shopify-hosted online store at shopboldr.com and does not currently publish a first-party developer API; its only public machine-readable surface is the Shopify Customer Account OIDC discovery served at the storefront host.

providers.name: Fiture
providers.description: Fiture is a consumer smart-home fitness company that makes interactive AI-powered fitness mirrors for at-home workouts. Its hardware line includes the Fiture Core flagship mirror and the compact Fiture Mini, each pairing a wall-mounted display with a camera and on-device AI that delivers real-time motion tracking, gesture recognition, rep counting, and posture feedback across a library of live and on-demand fitness classes sold through a membership. The company was founded in China and is backed by venture investor Hongshan (formerly Sequoia Capital China). Fiture operates a direct-to-consumer commerce and membership website but does not currently publish a public developer program, API, or SDK; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company and its public web surface (support, legal, and account pages).

providers.name: Amber Box
providers.description: AmberBox is an indoor gunshot detection company (San Francisco, CA) that builds sensor hardware and a response platform for schools, offices, and public buildings. Its patented tri-factor detection algorithm combines percussion, audio, and infrared signatures to identify a firearm discharge with a near-zero false-alarm rate, then automatically notifies on-site security and law enforcement to cut emergency response time by an average of five minutes. AmberBox integrates with existing physical-security estates (access control, IP video/VMS, PSIM, mass-notification, and fire-alarm-style life-safety systems) via closed-contact relay switches and TCP/IP relay input modules rather than a public developer API. Surfaced as an Uncork Capital portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; the company publishes no public REST/GraphQL API, developer portal, or SDKs at this time.

providers.name: Bevi
providers.description: Bevi is a smart beverage-dispenser company that manufactures connected, filtered-water machines for offices and commercial spaces. Its IoT-enabled Standup and Countertop dispensers deliver still and sparkling water plus dozens of fruit flavors and functional enhancements (vitamins, electrolytes, energy, focus), connect directly to a building's water supply, and track plastic bottles saved in real time. Bevi is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, Techstars, and Trinity Ventures. No public developer API surface (OpenAPI, docs, or developer portal) was found during enrichment; this profile carries identity and domain-security signals only.

providers.name: BirdBuddy
providers.description: Bird Buddy (Buddy Bird Inc, backed by General Catalyst) makes the world's most recognized smart bird feeder and companion mobile app for discovering and learning about birds. An AI vision-and-sound model identifies bird species from the photos and audio captured by its camera feeders, notifies owners of feathered visitors, and organizes captures into a personal collection with postcards and monthly reports. Bird Buddy does not publish an official public API; the app is powered by a private, account- authenticated GraphQL backend hosted on AWS, which the community has reverse-engineered through the third-party pybirdbuddy Python library and a Home Assistant integration.

providers.name: Sol
providers.description: Sol Reader is a wearable e-reader — marketed as the world's first wearable e-reader — built by Sol and backed by Initialized Capital. The device is a lightweight (104g) headset with dual 1.3" 271ppi side-lit E Ink displays, adjustable diopter optics and IPD, a handheld remote, and 25+ hours of battery for a distraction-free reading experience. It reads a connected Kindle library and DRM-free EPUB uploads, offers the Sol Store with over one million titles, plus AI question-answering and an AutoPilot speed-reading mode. Sol is a consumer hardware company; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Somnee
providers.description: Somnee is a consumer sleep-technology company behind a smart sleep headband that uses personalized neurostimulation to improve sleep. Developed over roughly eight years by a team of UC Berkeley neuroscientists (co-founders include sleep scientist Dr. Matthew Walker, Dr. Robert T. Knight, Dr. Rich Ivry, and CSTO Dr. Ram Gurumoorthy, with CEO Tim Rosa, former Fitbit CMO), the wearable pairs clinical-grade EEG+ sensors with a companion app and proprietary AI to deliver a 15-minute pre-bedtime session that the company says helps users fall asleep about 50% faster and cut nighttime wake-ups by roughly a third, without medication. Somnee sells the headband, accessories, and a sleep-service membership direct to consumers, and is backed by Khosla Ventures. Somnee publishes no public API or developer platform.

providers.name: Stel
providers.description: Stel Life provides cellular-connected remote patient monitoring (RPM) infrastructure for healthcare. Its cellular-enabled vitals hubs and connected medical devices — blood pressure monitors, pulse oximeters, glucometers, thermometers, and scales — let patients transmit vital-sign readings to electronic health record (EHR) systems without WiFi, broadband, a smartphone, or app setup, targeting elderly, low-income, rural, and low-tech-literacy populations. Health systems and digital health organizations use Stel across the care continuum, from wellness and chronic-care management to hospital-at-home. Stel is backed by Bloomberg Beta.

providers.name: Understory
providers.description: Understory is an insurtech company headquartered in Madison, Wisconsin (founded 2012) that combines its own network of ground-truth Dot weather sensors with a proprietary weather risk model to underwrite parametric insurance against severe weather, including hail coverage for automotive dealership open lots and agricultural weather risk. Its UnderstoryOS platform covers broker management, pricing and quoting, and automated weather-triggered claims. Understory publishes no public API or developer portal; the platform is offered to insurance partners rather than as a self-service developer product.

providers.name: Tozuda
providers.description: Tozuda is a Philadelphia-based safety technology company that makes mechanical, non-electronic head impact indicators for helmets. The patented indicator changes from clear to red when a helmet sustains force exceeding a set G-force threshold, making hidden helmet damage visible to workers, athletes, and safety inspectors across ANSI, DOT, EN, CSA, CPSC, and SNELL helmet types. Tozuda is a Techstars portfolio company and does not currently publish a public API or developer program.

providers.name: Apar Infotech Corporation
providers.description: Apar Infotech Corporation, which operates publicly as Apar Technologies, is a Singapore-headquartered IT services and consulting group serving clients across Asia Pacific, the Middle East and the Americas. The firm delivers technology consulting and application services, data management and business intelligence, collaboration and content management, enterprise applications, managed services, staff augmentation and collaborative development centres, with practice areas spanning artificial intelligence, cloud, CRM, ServiceNow workflow, RPA/BPM hyperautomation, enterprise mobility and IoT. Apar also publishes a small set of its own products — the Otomeyt HR technology and technical-assessment platform, the Innoculate IoT monitoring platform, and the eLite SIS and eLite BAM applications. Apar is part of the Apar Group and is backed by Insight Partners. As of this enrichment pass Apar publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, machine-readable API specification or self-service sign-up; its API work is delivered inside client engagements rather than as a public product surface.

providers.name: LARQ
providers.description: LARQ is a direct-to-consumer water technology company that designs self-cleaning and filtering drinkware and home water products. Its flagship Bottle PureVis uses UV-C light to neutralize up to 99.9999% of harmful, odor-causing bacteria in the bottle and on the water surface, and the range extends to filtered bottles, filtered pitchers, an under-sink water filter, and the cuva beverage flavor line. The company positions itself around sustainable hydration — reducing single-use plastic bottle consumption — and funds environmental nonprofits from a portion of each purchase. LARQ is a consumer hardware and e-commerce business: as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification, and no /.well-known/ discovery documents. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of dcm-ventures. Sector: consumer.

providers.name: NanoLumens
providers.description: NanoLumens is an American designer and manufacturer of direct-view LED (dvLED) displays and video walls, headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia and founded in 2006 by Rick Cope. It builds fixed and flexible indoor and outdoor displays in custom sizes, shapes and curvatures across the Engage Pro, Engage, NXT, Nixel, NanoPanel 55, Captivate, Performance, CLRVision, CLRVU and NanoBanner product lines, together with Aurora video processing and the NanoSuite display-management software. Its displays are deployed in retail, casinos, higher education, sports and arenas, control rooms, hospitality, themed entertainment, government, corporate and transportation environments. The software side of the business — the AWARE platform and NanoSuite, powered by the ISAAC ecosystem — markets a JSON REST API and webhook-based alerting for remote diagnostics, content scheduling and display-fleet monitoring, but that API is delivered to display owners through an authenticated tenant and has no public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: ams OSRAM
providers.description: ams OSRAM (ams-OSRAM AG) is a global leader in innovative optical solutions, designing and manufacturing intelligent sensors, emitters, and light-based semiconductors. Formed from the 2020 combination of ams AG (Austria) and OSRAM (Germany), the company builds LEDs, VCSEL and edge-emitting lasers, CMOS image sensors, ambient light and proximity sensors, direct time-of-flight (dToF) sensors, photodiodes, and LED/VCSEL driver ICs. Its sensing, illumination, and visualization technologies serve automotive and mobility (headlamps, interior lighting, ADAS), industrial automation and robotics, medical and healthcare devices, mobile and wearable devices, computing, and general lighting. Headquartered in Premstaetten, Austria and Munich, Germany, ams OSRAM employs roughly 18,500 people across 25 R&D sites and holds over 12,000 patents. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of iconiq-capital and enriched from ams OSRAM public web pages; the company exposes product/design support and a download center rather than a public developer API.

providers.name: Anker Innovations
providers.description: Anker Innovations is a global consumer-electronics company headquartered in Shenzhen, China, known for its Anker charging and power products, Soundcore audio, eufy smart-home and security devices, Nebula projectors, and Anker SOLIX portable power and solar storage. Through the Anker Open Platform (developer.anker.com) the company exposes a developer surface that lets partners integrate and control Anker devices from their own applications via API and SDK, gated behind an Open Platform login. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of IDG Capital and is being enriched with the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Volteum
providers.description: Volteum provides fleet electrification and EV fleet management software that helps companies plan, execute, and operate the transition of their vehicle fleets to electric. The platform covers electrification planning, charging optimisation, and live fleet management, connecting directly to vehicles through OEM APIs across 30+ brands with no hardware installation to track mileage, fault codes, charging sessions, maintenance intervals, and costs across electric, diesel, petrol, and hybrid fleets. Volteum is a Techstars portfolio company and publishes no public developer portal; its telematics and fleet-system API integrations are offered to customers directly.

providers.name: Acerta
providers.description: Acerta (Acerta Analytics Solutions Inc.) is a Canadian industrial-AI company whose LinePulse platform delivers AI-driven manufacturing quality analytics for discrete manufacturing. Founded in 2017 in Kitchener-Waterloo, Ontario, Acerta helps Tier-1 automotive and powertrain manufacturers detect defects early, reduce scrap and rework, and root-cause complex production issues in real time. LinePulse replaces statistical process control software, spreadsheets, and custom querying tools with real-time SPC, predictive monitoring, and machine-learning root-cause analysis, and ingests production data through a proprietary secure ingestion API. The platform is built on Microsoft Azure, is SOC 2 Type 1 certified, and is proven across 300+ production lines in 12 countries with customers including BorgWarner, Dana, Linamar, Ford, ZF, Ballard, and BMW. Acerta is a Techstars-backed portfolio company. Acerta exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, self-serve sign-up, or SDKs; integration is delivered through enterprise deployment with the LinePulse ingestion API.

providers.name: Athos
providers.description: Athos is a sports performance technology company founded in 2012 and based in Redwood City, California, that builds athletic apparel with embedded surface electromyography (EMG) sensors. Its garments and snap-on Athos Core module capture muscle activity, effort, and motion data, streaming it over Bluetooth to a mobile app and coaching dashboard so athletes, trainers, and sports scientists can measure muscular exertion, fatigue, and return-to-play readiness in real time. Athos is a consumer and team hardware brand with no publicly documented developer API; this profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and enriched for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Axiom Space
providers.description: Axiom Space, Inc. is a privately funded American space infrastructure developer headquartered in Houston, Texas, founded in 2016 by Kam Ghaffarian and former NASA International Space Station Program Manager Michael Suffredini. The company is building Axiom Station, the world's first commercial space station and planned successor to the ISS, and has flown private astronaut missions to the ISS (Ax-1 through Ax-4). Axiom Space also develops the Axiom Extravehicular Mobility Unit (AxEMU) spacesuit for NASA's return to the lunar surface, and sells human spaceflight, microgravity research, in-space manufacturing, and Orbital Data Center services (in-orbit cloud compute, with the ODC T1 node built alongside Kepler Communications and Skyloom Global). As of this enrichment pass Axiom Space publishes no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable API contract — every offering is transacted through direct enterprise, agency, and government engagement, and its only public code presence is a two-repository GitHub organization holding forks of NASA simulation software (Trick and GUNNS).

providers.name: Gabit
providers.description: Gabit is a one-stop health and wellness platform on a mission to add more healthy years to people's lives. Headquartered in Gurugram, India and founded in 2022 by Gaurav Gupta (ex-Zomato cofounder) and Arpana Shahi, Gabit treats health as an interconnected system across four pillars — fitness, nutrition, sleep, and mindfulness. Its consumer ecosystem spans the titanium Gabit Smart Ring, a smart body-composition scale, at-home Blood Work diagnostics, a continuous glucose monitor (CGM), the Sweden-born Näck nutrition supplement line, all-good-no-harm skincare, and coached Fitness & Nutrition Plans — all unified in the Gabit app, which tracks 150+ biomarkers and includes the free PEP AI health coach. India is the primary market, with Ring-only storefronts in the UAE and UK and an informational US/global page.

providers.name: Mira
providers.description: Mira is a San Francisco-based consumer hardware startup building AI-powered smart glasses positioned as an always-on "second brain." Founded in 2024 by Harvard builders AnhPhu Nguyen and Caine Ardayfio (rebranded from Halo), the camera-free glasses pair a dual-waveguide display, microphone, and iOS companion app to deliver live transcription, real-time translation across 60+ languages, hands-free AI assistance, and searchable memory of everyday conversations. Mira raised a $6.6M seed round led by General Catalyst and began shipping its first devices in January 2026. It is a privacy-first consumer wearable with an iOS companion app and does not currently expose a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Nix
providers.description: Nix (Nix Biosensors) develops wearable biosensor technology that analyzes sweat to deliver real-time hydration and electrolyte data. Its lightweight single-use biosensor patch continuously measures fluid and electrolyte losses and provides personalized hydration guidance to athletes, service members, and laborers. The company ships two consumer/enterprise offerings: Nix Solo, an individual app for self-monitoring hydration, and Nix Pro, a group-monitoring platform that lets coaches and supervisors track multiple users. Nix is a Techstars portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass it operates a direct-to-consumer commerce and mobile-app business with no public developer program, API documentation, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Oriient
providers.description: Oriient provides software-only, hardware-free indoor positioning ("indoor GPS") and navigation delivered as a SaaS SDK. Its geomagnetic technology reaches roughly 1-meter (3-foot) accuracy indoors without Wi-Fi, beacons, or installed infrastructure, powering product finding, order picking, visitor navigation, asset tracking, and in-store analytics for retail, grocery, and smart-building customers across thousands of locations. Oriient New Media Ltd is based in Tel Aviv and is a Techstars portfolio company. Oriient ships first-party mobile SDKs (including a React-Native Product Location AI package on npm) rather than a public REST API; integration is gated behind a customer dashboard and sales.

providers.name: Payment24
providers.description: Payment24 is a white-label payment platform specializing in fuel and fleet payment solutions for oil companies, banks, and retailers, primarily across Africa. Its technology lets clients design and launch branded payment products under their own name — fuel payments and mobile payments, loyalty and rewards, POS terminals, electronic vouchers, B2B and B2C prepaid and store-account cards, EV charging payments, and wet-stock and fuel-in-tank management — alongside banking-grade issuing, acquiring, card management, and merchant management, plus fleet fuel management and telematics. Payment24 operates as a technology partner rather than a public self-serve API provider, so it publishes no open developer portal or API documentation.

providers.name: Sensorum Health
providers.description: Sensorum Health is a healthcare technology company that provides home-based, fully passive sensor technology and integrated clinical services to identify and triage the earliest signs of health decline in older adults living with chronic conditions. The platform monitors patients 24/7 in their own homes without requiring wearables, smartphones, or WiFi, then coordinates clinical interventions when concerning health patterns emerge — with the goal of preventing avoidable hospital admissions. Backed by GV (Google Ventures). Added to the API Evangelist network as a company/provider record; no public API, specification, or developer program has been published as of this profile.

providers.name: Bosch
providers.description: Bosch is a German multinational engineering and technology company producing automotive components, industrial technology, consumer goods, and energy and building technology. Bosch operates the Bosch IoT Suite, an open IoT platform offering device management, software rollouts, edge services, and IoT data analytics, along with open source contributions to Eclipse Foundation IoT projects.

providers.name: Frontlinewildfire
providers.description: Frontline Wildfire Defense is a wildfire protection company that designs, manufactures, and installs exterior sprinkler defense systems for homes, businesses, wineries, summer camps, and new-home communities. The system combines roof- and ground-mounted sprinklers, a pump, and water/foam concentrate with a mobile app (iOS and Android) that lets property owners remotely activate the system, monitor nearby wildfires on a live fire map, and receive evacuation alerts. The company also publishes wildfire risk maps, home-hardening and defensible-space guidance, and works through a network of partner installers. Backed by Norwest Venture Partners. This is a consumer/hardware company profile; no public developer API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Roost
providers.description: Roost is a Sunnyvale, California home-telematics company that helps property and casualty insurance carriers modernize homeowners and commercial insurance with smart, in-home sensors and monitoring. Its Protection360 commercial loss-prevention service and Security360 white-label home-security bundle detect water leaks, extreme temperatures, and smoke-alarm events, delivering real-time alerts and risk data to insurers, property owners, and third parties. Roost partners with dozens of top P&C carriers, but does not publish a public developer API or developer portal; integrations are arranged directly with its engineering team.

providers.name: Wellxai
providers.description: Wellx (Wellxai) is a Dubai-based health insurtech company that transforms health insurance from reactive to proactive through AI-driven behavior change. Its consumer mobile app pairs behavioral science and gamification with wearable integrations (Fitbit, Apple Watch, Whoop) so members earn xCoins rewards by hitting health goals, step and sleep challenges, and wellness programs, then redeem them with marketplace partners. Wellx also sells to corporates and SMEs and partners with brokers and insurers, positioning healthier behavior as the driver of better-value health insurance. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network; the company exposes consumer iOS/Android apps backed by a private API but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Skyworks Solutions
providers.description: Skyworks Solutions, Inc. is an American semiconductor company headquartered in Irvine, California that designs, develops, and markets proprietary semiconductor products for wireless communications, automotive, broadband, connected home, industrial, defense, and consumer electronics applications. Skyworks is a leading provider of analog and mixed-signal semiconductors, with dominant market share in 5G RF front-end modules (35% market share). Products span amplifiers, filters, front-end modules, isolators, switches, and power management ICs serving mobile, automotive, IoT, and infrastructure markets. The company does not publish a public developer API but provides datasheets, evaluation tools, and design resources for hardware engineers.

providers.name: Customer Analytics
providers.description: Customer Analytics (CA) is a data, analytics and AI consultancy headquartered in Middleton, Wisconsin with a delivery centre in Guindy, Chennai, India. The firm delivers AI/ML and data analytics, data engineering, business intelligence and reporting, business solutions design and software development, platform implementation and software management (Microsoft Dynamics 365, Microsoft Fabric, Salesforce), and quality assurance. Alongside these services it packages six productised offerings — DataWorks 360, BI Xpert 360, AI Assist 360, Retail AI Insights 360, PBILens 360 and Smart IoT Data Track 360 — and publishes case studies across healthcare, manufacturing, retail/B2B, education, agriculture, clinical research, warehouse operations, the art industry and government. Customer Analytics is a professional services company: as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs or machine-readable API specifications.

providers.name: Detect Technologies
providers.description: Detect Technologies is an industrial AI company founded in 2016 and headquartered in Chennai, India, focused on transforming workplace safety, security, productivity, and asset inspections across asset-intensive industries such as oil and gas, steel, manufacturing, and energy. Its flagship platform, T-Pulse, is an AI-powered Health, Safety and Environment (HSE) management system that aggregates data from cameras, sensors, equipment, and processes to deliver near real-time risk and efficiency insights through computer vision and machine learning. The T-Pulse suite spans Workplace Safety, Workplace Operations, Workplace Inspections, and Workplace Security modules, complemented by predictive maintenance and turnaround (STO) orchestration capabilities. Detect Technologies is backed by Prosus Ventures.

providers.name: Humatics
providers.description: Humatics Corporation is a Waltham, Massachusetts microlocation company founded in 2015 by MIT professor David Mindell and led by CEO James Kinsey. It builds radio-frequency positioning systems — ultra-wideband beacons, RF-pulse ranging, radar and inertial sensors fused in software — that locate people, vehicles and robots at centimeter- to millimeter-scale precision. Two product lines are on sale today: MILO, a sub-millimeter positioning system for industrial automation and in-motion robotics, advertised as compatible with Yaskawa, Mitsubishi Electric, FANUC, Universal Robots and KUKA; and Mobility, a rail and transit portfolio covering the FOCUS track-geometry monitoring kit and the Humatics Rail Navigation System (HRNS), used on New York City MTA subway signalling projects. Humatics publishes no developer portal, no API documentation and no machine-readable description of any product API. Two rounds of probing humatics.com returned HTTP 404 for every /.well-known/ path, /llms.txt, /openapi.json, /openapi.yaml, /swagger.json, /api-docs and /graphql; *.humatics.com is a DNS wildcard onto one retired address, so api., docs., developer., portal. and status. resolve but time out on connect. The only machine-readable HTTP interface on any Humatics host is the WordPress REST API of the marketing site itself at humatics.com/wp-json/ — 375 routes across 19 stock core and commercial-plugin namespaces, exposing pages and posts rather than positioning, and so recorded as evidence rather than catalogued as a Humatics API. The GitHub organization github.com/Humatics is real and public, but 31 of its 33 repositories are forks of third-party embedded and robotics open source (Fast-RTPS, Fast-CDR, FreeRTOS, Orange Pi BSP, Yocto meta-layers, EIPScanner, donkeycar); the two non-forks are internal tools. There is no first-party SDK, client library or specification, and no package named humatics exists on npm or PyPI. Marketing material for the earlier KinetIQ OS / Spatial Intelligence Platform referenced an "extensible API", but no public interface for it was ever documented, and the news host that carried those announcements (now.humatics.com) no longer answers.

providers.name: Prisma Photonics
providers.description: Prisma Photonics is an infrastructure-monitoring company that turns existing optical fiber into a continuous sensing network using its Hyper-Scan Fiber-Sensing distributed acoustic sensing technology. The platform measures strain, temperature, pressure, and acoustic signatures at every point along hundreds of kilometers of fiber with sub-meter resolution, and applies AI-driven classification to detect and identify events in real time. It is used to protect and monitor power lines, oil and gas pipelines, perimeters, subsea assets, and smart rail and road infrastructure. Backed by Insight Partners, the company was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API or developer program.

providers.name: Reach
providers.description: Reach Power (Reach Labs) is a Y Combinator-backed (S2015) wireless power company building long-range wireless energy distribution networks, aiming to "do for power what Wi-Fi did for data." Its patented, AI-driven power-beaming systems use adaptive metamaterial antennas to steer electromagnetic waves and deliver electricity through the air to multiple devices simultaneously, scaling from microwatts to kilowatts across both mobile and stationary transmitters. Reach serves defense and intelligence, manufacturing and logistics, and public safety markets, powering autonomous vehicles, industrial robotics, sensors, and drones. Partners and customers include the U.S. Department of Defense, NASA, DARPA, the U.S. Army and Air Force, Aisin/Toyota, and Panasonic. The company is headquartered in San Francisco. As of this profile, Reach publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this is a hardware and energy-infrastructure company rather than an API platform.

providers.name: Syntiant
providers.description: Syntiant Corp is an Irvine, California edge-AI semiconductor company founded in 2017 that designs ultra-low-power Neural Decision Processors (NDPs) and the deep-learning models and tooling that run on them, bringing always-on speech, audio, sensor and vision inference to battery-powered devices without a cloud connection. Its silicon family spans the NDP100/NDP101, NDP102, NDP115, NDP120, NDP200 and NDP250, paired with a Training Development Kit (TDK) that maps TensorFlow models onto the NDP core and an embedded SDK for integration into customer firmware. In December 2024 Syntiant completed the USD 150 million acquisition of Knowles Corporation's Consumer MEMS Microphones business, taking the company from roughly 70 to nearly 1,700 employees and making microphones the majority of its revenue. Syntiant is a silicon, module and embedded-software supplier rather than an API provider - enrichment probing found no public web API, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, no developer portal, no first-party package-registry SDKs and no event surface; its SDK and TDK are distributed to customers through a private GitLab and under agreement.

providers.name: Karnott
providers.description: Karnott is a French agricultural technology company based in Lille that builds connected tracking devices and a digital management platform for farms, equipment cooperatives (CUMA), agricultural contractors (ETA), and wine growers. Its beacon automatically records equipment usage and field interventions without manual data entry, enabling real-time fleet and equipment monitoring, fuel-cost tracking, parcel mapping, and precise billing and regulatory documentation. Karnott is a portfolio company of Partech. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal was found on the provider's public surface as of this pass.

providers.name: Sensefinity
providers.description: Sensefinity is a supply-chain IoT company ("The IoT Transformation Company") delivering real-time tracking, monitoring, and analytics for global cargo and logistics operations. Its platform combines GPS/NB-IoT tracking devices for maritime containers, pallets, and vehicles with temperature and condition (cold-chain) sensors, indoor location tracking, a cloud analytics and machine learning layer, and digital product passport / blockchain integrations. The operational platform is delivered as a hosted web application (uiadmin.sensefinity.com) and mobile asset-management apps, serving enterprise customers across food, pharma, automotive, and manufacturing supply chains. No public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, or SDK surface is published as of this profile; a private API host (api.sensefinity.com) backs the platform.

providers.name: Feel Therapeutics
providers.description: Feel Therapeutics, an IQVIA business, is a Digital Precision Medicine company on a mission to reinvent how mental health is diagnosed, managed and cared for by bringing objective data, continuous passive measurement and novel digital biomarkers into mental healthcare. Rather than relying on episodic, subjective self-reported questionnaires, Feel develops digital biomarkers from wearable and passive sensor data to enable continuous, objective monitoring. Its solutions span the Feel Digital Precision Medicine Platform (DPMP), Feel DTx precision digital therapeutics, drug-plus / beyond-the-pill programs, and a wearable monitoring device. The company partners with pharma and biotech to advance clinical development, real-world evidence (RWE), and commercialization strategies, and has run 20+ research studies with 3000+ participants.

providers.name: FiberSense
providers.description: FiberSense is a distributed fiber optic sensing (DFOS / distributed acoustic sensing) company that turns existing and purpose-built fiber optic cables into dense arrays of vibration and acoustic sensors for real-time detection, localization and classification of objects and events across critical infrastructure. Its AI/ML algorithms filter noise and false alarms in dense urban, marine and underground environments, delivered as a subscription-based sensing platform rather than a public developer API. Product lines include DigitalAsset (critical infrastructure asset protection), DigitalCity (urban infrastructure and utility monitoring), DigitalMarine (subsea and marine cable route monitoring) and DigitalLeak (pipeline leak detection). Backed by Prosus Ventures; customer support runs through an Atlassian service desk portal.

providers.name: Happiest Baby
providers.description: Happiest Baby is a consumer sleep-technology company founded by pediatrician Dr. Harvey Karp, best known for the SNOO Smart Sleeper - an FDA-authorized responsive bassinet that uses sensor-driven motion and white noise to soothe infants and improve sleep. The company also sells the Sleepea swaddle and sleep sacks, runs a companion mobile app with parenting guidance, and operates a healthcare/hospital program. Its connected SNOO hardware communicates in real time over PubNub; Happiest Baby publishes no official public developer API, and the only programmatic access is via community-built wrappers around the undocumented mobile-app API. Backed by GV and Obvious Ventures.

providers.name: REEV
providers.description: REEV is a medical-technology company developing AI-powered wearable robotics for mobility recovery and neurological gait rehabilitation. Its REEV SENSE platform uses smart shoe- and leg-mounted sensors to analyze gait and visualize biomarkers in a mobile app, and its DREEVEN motorized knee-ankle-foot orthosis (KAFO) delivers robotic walking assistance personalized from REEV SENSE gait data. REEV serves outpatient clinics and rehabilitation centers treating stroke, multiple sclerosis, and paraplegia, and is backed by Techstars, NVIDIA Inception, and Bpifrance.

providers.name: Remedee Labs
providers.description: Remedee Labs is a French medical device company founded in 2016 in Grenoble that develops millimeter-wave neuromodulation solutions for chronic pain management. Its flagship product is the Remedee wrist bracelet, which stimulates nerve endings to trigger endorphin release, paired with the myRemedee companion app and human coaching. The company markets two subscription solutions, FibroRem for fibromyalgia and NoviRem for osteoarthritis pain. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech and added to the API Evangelist network; the product is consumer-facing and publishes no public developer API, SDK, or technical integration surface at this time.

providers.name: Motorq
providers.description: Motorq is a connected vehicle intelligence platform that taps native OEM connectivity to deliver AI-powered insights across the automotive ecosystem. It aggregates and normalizes vehicle telematics data from 25+ automotive brands and third-party sources without plug-in hardware or dongles, so fleets, fleet management companies, dealerships, lenders, insuretechs, and mobility companies can drive maintenance, safety, utilization, and EV use cases. Motorq offers access through a cloud fleet management portal, bi-directional APIs and data streams (Get Location, Create Geofence, and more), and a Snowflake data lake integration. Its Motorq Fuse AI layer surfaces prioritized recommendations ranked by severity and cost impact. API access is gated to enterprise and OEM partners; there is no public self-serve developer portal or OpenAPI definition. Backed by Insight Partners.

providers.name: Naviday Health
providers.description: Naviday Health is a Boston-based women's health technology company and Techstars portfolio company building clinical decision support that connects the continuous health data women generate every day from consumer wearables and patient-generated sources to the practitioners who need it most. Its LUCI Care platform surfaces actionable insights for clinicians between appointments, and the company partners with device manufacturers on wearable integration services. Naviday Health is HIPAA compliant and has been recognized by the Mayo Clinic Platform, StartUp Health, and MassChallenge. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, documentation, SDK, or well-known discovery surface.

providers.name: ECOVACS Robotics
providers.description: ECOVACS Robotics is a global home service robotics company founded in 1998 and headquartered in Suzhou, China, that designs, manufactures, and sells AI-powered autonomous cleaning devices for consumer and commercial use. Its product families include DEEBOT robotic vacuum and mopping robots, WINBOT window-cleaning robots, GOAT robotic lawn mowers, ULTRAMARINE pool-cleaning robots, and the DEEBOT PRO commercial line, all managed through the ECOVACS HOME mobile app. The company was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of IDG Capital; as of this enrichment pass ECOVACS publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documented API surface — this profile captures its public web, support, and legal properties plus a domain-security probe.

providers.name: Feetme
providers.description: FeetMe is a Paris-based medical device company, founded in 2013, that develops smart connected insoles and digital health software for real-time gait analysis and mobility care. Its CE-marked, ISO 13485 and ISO 9001 certified wearables embed plantar pressure sensors and a 6-axis inertial measurement unit to capture more than twenty gait and balance metrics per step, streaming them over Bluetooth Low Energy to the FeetMe Mobility dashboard used by clinicians for neurological, orthopedic and rehabilitation assessment. Product lines include FeetMe Evaluation, FeetMe Rehabilitation, FeetMe Monitor and FeetMe Stimulate. The company is backed by Partech. FeetMe does not currently expose a public developer API or OpenAPI-described web API; a partner SDK for raw-data integration is referenced in product materials but is not publicly documented.

providers.name: August Home
providers.description: August Home is a consumer smart-home and access-control brand best known for its retrofit August Smart Lock, Smart Lock Pro, Wi-Fi Smart Lock, Smart Keypad, Doorbell Cam, and the August Connect Wi-Fi Bridge. Founded in San Francisco and acquired by ASSA ABLOY, August products are now sold and supported alongside the Yale Home brand and operated through the shared Yale Access mobile app. August does not publish a public developer API or developer portal; programmatic access to August locks is reached through the private mobile/app API or via third-party universal-access platforms such as Seam, and integrations exist with Google Home, Amazon Alexa, Apple HomeKit, Airbnb, and Yale. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Cowboy Ventures and enriched from public sources.

providers.name: Belts
providers.description: Belts covers the landscape of APIs, data standards, and digital resources related to conveyor belts and industrial belt systems. This topic encompasses conveyor belt monitoring and predictive maintenance APIs, industrial IoT sensor data for belt condition tracking, and the standards bodies that govern belt conveyor design and safety. Key organizations include CEMA (Conveyor Equipment Manufacturers Association) and ANSI, which define design, installation, and safety standards for belt conveyors used in mining, manufacturing, food processing, and bulk material handling industries.

providers.name: Hula Earth
providers.description: Hula Earth is a Munich-based environmental technology company providing real-time biodiversity monitoring. It combines solar-powered, maintenance-free Hula BioT IoT sensors with AI-powered species detection, satellite-based Earth Observation, and the Hula Platform dashboard so organizations can monitor, manage, and report on biodiversity at landscape scale. Hula Earth serves renewables (solar and wind), agriculture, nature conservation, and urban development, turning environmental uncertainty into operational confidence and compliance-ready reporting.

providers.name: Inofab
providers.description: Inofab Health (a Clario company) is a digital respiratory health company headquartered in Ankara, Turkey, building connected spirometry and inhaler devices with cloud software for the home-based and clinical management of chronic respiratory conditions including asthma, COPD, and cystic fibrosis. Its product line spans the SpiroHome Personal portable ultrasonic spirometer, the SpiroClinic Pro and SpiroClinic Compact clinical-grade spirometers with EHR integration, the SpiroCloud web dashboard that collects and analyzes data from all connected SpiroHome and SpiroClinic devices, and the SpiroHaler smart inhaler attachments for medication adherence. Inofab was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; it does not currently publish a public developer portal, API documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Sleep Number
providers.description: Sleep Number Corporation (NASDAQ: SNBR) designs, manufactures, and retails smart adjustable-firmness beds and sleep-wellness products, sold through an omnichannel US retail model. Its Sleep Number 360 smart beds run the proprietary SleepIQ operating system, which captures biometric sleep data each night and returns actionable insights to improve sleep health. Sleep Number does not publish a public developer API or developer portal; the SleepIQ platform is a closed, undocumented backend consumed only by the first-party mobile and web apps. The community has reverse-engineered unofficial SleepIQ client libraries (Python, Go, PHP), but these are not first-party and are not endorsed by Sleep Number. This profile was surfaced as a legacy portfolio lead of Norwest Venture Partners and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: STAND+
providers.description: STAND+ is a Techstars-backed footwear company making biomechanically engineered "energy-recovery" shoes for people who spend long hours standing or walking - healthcare workers, frontline and workforce professionals, athletes, and everyday movers. Its proprietary midsole is designed to dissipate and disperse impact energy outward rather than returning it into the joints, which the company markets for fatigue and pain reduction. The product lineup includes the AntiGrav1, AntiGrav2, and AG3 recovery shoes, the Gales Pro and Gales Frontline workforce and healthcare lines, and standalone recovery insoles. STAND+ is APMA (American Podiatric Medical Association) certified and HSA/FSA eligible through a Truemed partnership. This is a direct-to-consumer e-commerce brand (standshoes.com) with no public developer API, SDK, or integration surface at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Atlas5D
providers.description: Atlas5D is a healthcare technology company that develops an Ambient Measurement System (AMS) for assessing health and wellness through motion in any environment. Its passive, privacy-preserving sensor platform recognizes specific individuals, characterizes and quantifies their movement, and interprets daily routines to predict trends and assess risk of adverse events such as falls, without wearables, without transmitting video, and without storing images. Atlas5D serves individuals monitoring aging loved ones, assisted-living and other institutional care settings, and healthcare and clinical-trial teams that need clinical-grade, real-world evidence of patient movement wherever people live. Backed by Techstars.

providers.name: Green Fusion
providers.description: Green Fusion GmbH is a Berlin-based climate-energy software company that provides an intelligent 360-degree energy management platform for the residential real estate sector (Wohnungswirtschaft). Its software digitizes and optimizes building heating systems: "Der Energiespar-Pilot" delivers digital boiler-room management and optimized operation of conventional heat sources (gas, oil, district heating, CHP/BHKW), while its AI platform for sector coupling (Sektorkopplung) integrates heat pumps, PV systems, storage, and grid connectivity for intelligent monitoring and control. The platform is TUV-certified under GEG section 71a. Green Fusion is backed by HV Capital and surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a climate-energy provider; it operates a customer control platform (control.green-fusion.de) but publishes no public developer API at this time.

providers.name: Optoscale
providers.description: Optoscale (OptoScale AS) is a Norwegian aquaculture technology company founded in 2015 in Trondheim that builds AI-powered, camera-based edge-computing monitoring for fish farming. Its Bioscope units capture real-time measurements of fish weight, biomass, sea-lice counts, welfare, behaviour and feeding, producing tens of thousands of validated measurements each day directly on the unit rather than on remote servers. Customers view trends, graphs and high-resolution imagery through the OptoScale web portal, export to Excel/CSV, and integrate the underlying data into their own analytics and farm-management systems via OptoScale's data API. OptoScale was acquired by Insight Partners in 2025.

providers.name: Plotlogic
providers.description: Plotlogic is a mining technology company that builds AI-driven sensing systems for real-time ore and material characterisation. Its flagship product, OreSense, scans rock in open-pit, stockpile, and underground mining operations and delivers decision-ready quantitative mineralogy in under 15 minutes, compared with more than an hour for traditional laboratory assay methods. The hardware is engineered for harsh mining environments and integrates into existing operational workflows so mines can reduce waste, improve grade control, and make faster material-routing decisions. Plotlogic is headquartered in Zillmere, Queensland, Australia, and is backed by the deep-tech venture firm DCVC. Customer access is delivered through an enterprise client platform rather than a public developer API; there is no published developer program, SDK, or API documentation at this time.

providers.name: Inspiren
providers.description: Inspiren is a healthcare technology company providing an AI-powered ecosystem for senior living communities that combines hardware and software to improve resident safety, care planning, and staff efficiency. Its platform pairs devices such as the AUGi sensor, Sense, Help Button, Resident Pendant, and Staff Beacon with the Inspiren HQ software platform and mobile app to deliver emergency call, real-time fall prevention and safety monitoring, data-driven care insights, and staff workflow coordination. Inspiren reports outcomes including reductions in falls, faster alert response times, and improved occupancy for the communities it serves. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Insight Partners and Scale Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network; Inspiren does not publish a public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API specifications at this time.

providers.name: PayRange
providers.description: PayRange is a fintech company providing cashless commerce and self-service retail technology for unattended machines. Its platform enables mobile payments, age and identity verification, and access control across laundromats, vending, car washes, campgrounds, hospitality, micro-markets, coffee, and transit ticketing. Hardware includes the BluKey family, BluCheck, and PayStation, paired with a consumer mobile app and an operator Business Management Suite. Backed by GV and Matrix Partners. No public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface was found during enrichment; integrations appear to run through direct partner and licensing channels.

providers.name: Silk Labs
providers.description: Silk Labs was an on-device artificial intelligence startup founded in 2015 by former Mozilla CTO Andreas Gal together with Chris Jones and Michael Vines, a team drawn from Mozilla's Firefox OS effort. The company's open-source Silk platform layered a Node.js runtime on Android so developers could build Internet of Things applications entirely in JavaScript, and it later shipped work on the "Sense" AI home camera focused on running real-time visual and audio recognition directly on the device. Silk Labs was backed by investors including 500 Global and was acquired by Apple in November 2018, after which it ceased independent operations; the silklabs.com domain is now parked on Apple nameservers. Its open-source Silk code, GitHub organization, and npm packages remain publicly available and are captured in this profile.

providers.name: EcoG
providers.description: EcoG is a Munich-based technology company that builds the software and hardware platform powering electric-vehicle DC fast chargers. Its EcoG OS operating system, Universal Core platform, and controllers let charger manufacturers, charge point operators (CPOs), and EV businesses design, launch, and scale DC charging solutions with reduced complexity, claiming more than 15% market share in Europe with operations across India and North America. For developers, EcoG OS exposes an on-device programmatic surface (an OpenAPI-based application interface, a local web interface, and the LifeC remote management tool) so smart value-added charging applications can be built and run at the device level. This profile was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and enriched from EcoG's public website; it publishes no public REST API developer portal or specification.

providers.name: Pillar Technologies
providers.description: Pillar Technologies provides construction jobsite risk management through environmental monitoring and data analytics. Its wireless, rugged "Pod" sensors measure eight environmental metrics on the jobsite (temperature, humidity, carbon monoxide, VOCs, particulates, noise, light, and pressure) with cellular connectivity and a one-year battery life, feeding a real-time software platform with customizable dashboards, floorplan integration, and drill-down reporting by site, floor, or sensor. A configurable alert system notifies teams via text, email, or phone. Pillar serves data centers, hospitality and multi-family housing, and science and healthcare construction projects to improve safety and protect schedules and budgets. Surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company. No public developer API, documentation, or developer portal was found as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Ai Fabrik
providers.description: AI Fabrik is an infrastructure company building an edge inference delivery network for high-performance AI tokens. Incubated within Gruve and led by founder Tarun Raisoni alongside Swati Deshpande and Tanuj Mohan, the company has deconstructed the traditional data center model and rebuilt every layer for real-time AI, delivering distributed inference close to users and cloud providers with sub-20ms latency, cost efficiency, and built-in compliance. AI Fabrik is deploying five initial production sites with 6,000+ B300 GPUs launching in 2026, backed by Mayfield, Xora (Temasek), Acclimate Ventures, and Cisco Investments.

providers.name: Deako
providers.description: Deako is a whole-home smart lighting company that designs modular smart switches, dimmers, plugs, and simple switches (motion, timer, nightlight, and fan controls) for residential new construction and retrofit. Its Deako Intelligence platform layers adaptive lighting, follow-me sound, intercom, and parent-care features on top of the hardware, and the devices integrate with Amazon Alexa, Google Home, Control4, Clare, and the Matter smart-home standard. Deako sells directly and through a network of homebuilders, electricians, and integrators. No public developer API, SDK, or developer portal is currently published; this profile tracks the company's public web, support, blog, legal, and smart-home integration surface, awaiting any future developer program.

providers.name: Detect
providers.description: Detect Technologies is an IIT Madras-incubated industrial AI company founded in 2016 and headquartered in Chennai, India. Its 360-degree Workplace Intelligence Platform, T-Pulse, combines proprietary IoT sensors, drones, robotics and machine vision with industrial AI to deliver automated inspections, predictive maintenance, gas and oil leak detection, structural health monitoring, and real-time workplace safety, operations and security monitoring for enterprises such as Shell, Vedanta, Adani Group and Hindustan Zinc. Backed by Accel and Elevation Capital. The company does not publish a public API or developer program; this profile captures its public identity and domain security posture.

providers.name: Drover AI
providers.description: Drover AI is a Los Angeles-based micromobility technology company that pioneers the use of computer vision, machine learning, and proprietary sensor fusion in shared light electric vehicles (LEVs) such as e-scooters and e-bikes. Its flagship PathPilot module is a plug-and-play IoT unit retrofit onto existing fleet vehicles that delivers granular infrastructure distinction (sidewalk, bike lane, crosswalk, street), real-time parking validation, and the ability to control vehicle behavior (speed reduction, throttle disable) based on rider location. The Drover Corral dashboard surfaces real-time compliance insights and validation to operators and cities in line with the MDS 2.0 standard, delivered via API and automated Slack alerts. Partners and customers include Spin, Voi, Bolt, Beam, Dott, and Felyx. Drover AI is a portfolio company of 500 Global. No public developer portal, OpenAPI, or SDK surface is published; integration is handled directly with operators.

providers.name: E-Peas
providers.description: e-peas is a Belgian fabless semiconductor company founded in 2014 in Louvain-la-Neuve that designs power management integrated circuits (PMICs) for energy harvesting, enabling battery-free and battery-assisted IoT devices to power themselves from ambient energy. Its flagship Ambient Energy Manager (AEM) family harvests from photovoltaic (light), thermal, vibration/piezoelectric, radio-frequency, and hybrid multi-source inputs, and the company also develops ultra-low-power microcontrollers for autonomous data acquisition. e-peas positions itself as a pioneer of the "Ambient IoT" concept serving smart buildings, industrial IoT, consumer electronics, and wearables, with an ecosystem of 30+ partners including Panasonic, TDK, Vishay, and Silicon Labs. This is a hardware/silicon company that does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or API documentation.

providers.name: Evigence Sensors
providers.description: Evigence Sensors is a freshness-management technology company for the food industry, combining low-cost physical sensors with data analytics to monitor food quality in real time from production to consumption at the individual item level. Its time-temperature indicator technology powers both digital (QR-scan) and visual freshness indicators applied to retail units, serving food brands, retailers, foodservice operators, cold-chain logistics providers, and consumers across the supply chain. Evigence holds 27 granted patents and its indicators meet WHO time/temperature monitoring standards. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Evigence publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDK, or machine-readable API surface; this profile captures its verified public company properties only.

providers.name: Forterra
providers.description: Forterra is a defense autonomy company headquartered in Clarksburg, Maryland, that builds combat-proven autonomous mission systems for ground operations in contested, GPS-denied, off-road environments. Founded in 2002 as Robotic Research and rebranded as Forterra, it retrofits existing military and commercial vehicles with self-driving capability through its AutoDrive autonomous driving system, the TerraLink modular vehicle-management and command-and-control platform, and the OASIS open architecture that lets the government and third-party developers add sensors, effectors, and payloads without vendor lock-in. Additional offerings span resilient communications, sensing, and ruggedized edge-compute hardware. The company is backed by SoftBank Vision Fund 2 and Enlightenment Capital and supplies autonomy to multiple active U.S. Department of Defense programs. Forterra does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or self-service developer portal; its systems are delivered as government and defense-integration programs.

providers.name: Freight Farms
providers.description: Freight Farms is a Boston-based vertical farming company that builds the Greenery container farm, a commercial-scale, modular, hydroponic farm assembled inside a shipping container so growers can produce hyper-local produce 365 days a year in any climate. Its Farmhand software platform provides remote farm control, farm data analytics and insights, crop planning, and pre-set growing recipes, backed by certified training, onboarding, logistics, and technical support. The company reports 800+ farms across 50 U.S. states and 3 territories and 2,100+ farmers in 42 countries.
