Freight Farms currently publishes no public developer API, portal, or OpenAPI surface; this API Evangelist profile captures its public web, brand, and legal properties plus a domain-security probe while a programmatic surface is monitored for.

providers.name: Fuchsia
providers.description: Fuchsia is an AI-native hardware certification and compliance platform ("Vanta for hardware") that helps hardware teams get products to market faster by streamlining regulatory testing and certification. The platform maps the applicable standards for a product (FCC, CE, UL, FDA 510(k), ISO, RF & EMC, environmental, and functional-safety categories), auto-generates the lab-ready technical documentation and test plans required for certification, connects teams with qualified testing labs specialized in their product category, and tracks compliance progress to surface blockers early. Fuchsia uses AI agents to manage the compliance workflow end to end — from design through testing and certification — including direct communication with testing labs, aiming to democratize regulatory compliance that has traditionally favored larger companies with dedicated compliance teams. Founded in 2025 and part of the Y Combinator Spring 2026 batch, Fuchsia is based in the San Francisco Bay Area and targets robotics, medical-device, IoT, and consumer-hardware builders. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company; as of this enrichment pass Fuchsia publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: INGU
providers.description: INGU is a pipeline integrity technology company delivering inline inspection for oil & gas and water/wastewater pipelines through its Pipers multi-sensor free-floating inspection system paired with AI analytics and GIS-based pipeline viewer software. The platform performs leak detection, deposit and wall-condition assessment, and detection of gas pockets, magnetic features, bends, and hot taps across pipelines of any diameter or material. INGU has inspected over 900 pipelines for operators including Chevron, Shell, TotalEnergies, SUEZ, and Vale. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global; the company publishes no public API or developer surface at this time.

providers.name: Jiobit
providers.description: Jiobit is a real-time GPS tracking device company owned by Life360, based in San Mateo, California. Its lightweight (18g) wearable tracker is designed for kids, pets, seniors, and adults, combining LPWA CatM1 cellular, GPS, WiFi, and BLE for location accuracy of 1-50 feet, up to 30 days of battery life, geofence and SOS/911 emergency alerts, and tamper-proof, government-level encryption. Jiobit is a consumer hardware and mobile-app product sold direct-to-consumer with a monthly connectivity subscription; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company discovery and monitoring.

providers.name: K4Connect
providers.description: K4Connect is a Morrisville, North Carolina technology company serving the senior living industry, backed by Sierra Ventures. Its patented FusionOS integration and data platform provides two-way ("One-to-Many") interoperability that shares the who, what and when of a community between every integrated system, connecting 50+ leading applications, devices and services. On top of FusionOS sits K4Community, an enterprise engagement suite of interconnected modules: Team Hub for staff, the Plus App for residents, Voice (Amazon Alexa), K4TV infotainment, Digital Signage, and smart-home Resident Check-In. K4Connect operates a partner-led integration model rather than a public self-serve developer API; integrations are built and coordinated through FusionOS.

providers.name: Kardome Technology
providers.description: Kardome develops Voice AI technology that lets voice-integrated products hear and understand speech with human-level accuracy in complex, real-world acoustic environments. Its two core technologies are Spatial Hearing AI, which understands the acoustic scene to localize sound sources and attribute speech to the correct speaker, and Cognition AI, which adds contextual awareness so devices understand what people mean in the moment. Kardome targets automotive in-car voice UI and smart-home voice interaction in noisy environments. The company is a Techstars portfolio company, tracked in the API Evangelist network; it licenses embedded voice technology to device makers rather than publishing a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Moj.io
providers.description: Mojio (moj.io) is a connected-car and connected-mobility platform that collects, processes, and monetizes vehicle telematics data at scale for mobile network operators, automotive OEMs, insurers, and fleet/field-service businesses. Its "Mobility Studio" platform exposes REST endpoints for vehicle data, a PUSH API for real-time insights, mobile SDKs, and a vehicle simulator, alongside a white-label consumer app (Motion) and a services ecosystem (Alexa, Google Maps, Bosch, and others). Mojio has processed 15+ billion miles of driving data. As of this pass the API and SDK surface is partner-gated — there is no public developer portal, published OpenAPI specification, or self-serve API documentation. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Neuron Mobility
providers.description: Neuron Mobility is a rental e-scooter and e-bike operator and micromobility technology developer running shared micromobility fleets in cities across Australia, the United Kingdom, and Canada. The company designs its own vehicles (including the N3 e-scooter), safety systems such as its patented Helmet Lock and ScootSafe rider training program, and the backend fleet-management, IoT, and geofencing technology that powers its rider apps and city operations. Backed by 500 Global, Neuron was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and profiled in the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no first-party developer API, GBFS data feed, or well-known discovery surface on its own domain; this profile captures its public web, legal, and support properties plus a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: OWLR
providers.description: OWLR (OWLR Technologies) is a London- and Fort Lauderdale-based consumer IoT company that builds universal remote-monitoring apps for home IP cameras, letting users view and manage cameras from many brands through a single mobile application. Its products include the OWLR Multi-Brand Viewer and brand-specific viewers for Foscam and D-Link, plus motion-alert notifications. OWLR emphasizes a privacy-first design in which camera credentials stay on the user's phone and nothing is stored on OWLR's servers. The company reports over two million users and was backed by 500 Global. OWLR is a consumer mobile product and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: PathSpot
providers.description: PathSpot Technologies provides a health-and-safety operating system for restaurants, commercial kitchens, food manufacturers, cafeterias, and hospitality venues. Its flagship HandScanner uses light-based spectroscopy to detect harmful contaminants on employees' hands in about two seconds after washing and drying. Alongside the scanner, PathSpot's SafetySuite bundles real-time temperature monitoring (PowerTemp), digital task management (PowerTasks), and food labeling (PowerLabels), rolling the data up into the SafetySuite Hub dashboard with analytics, automated compliance reporting, email reports, text alerts, and optional API-based data integration. PathSpot markets API integration as a data-delivery feature of SafetySuite but publishes no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI, or SDKs as of this profile.

providers.name: Preteckt
providers.description: Preteckt provides AI-powered predictive maintenance for transit buses, coach buses, and trucking fleets. Its platform ingests vehicle sensor telemetry and applies machine-learning algorithms to detect maintenance issues before they cause breakdowns, reducing diagnostic time by nearly 50 percent and preventing roughly 20 percent of failures. Preteckt processes more than one million sensor data points per day per vehicle across 20+ maintenance-focused algorithms. The company is part of Diesel Laptops. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Preteckt publishes no public developer, API, documentation, or sign-up surface.

providers.name: Siren
providers.description: Siren is a digital health company that makes temperature-monitoring smart socks to prevent diabetic foot ulcers. The seamless, machine-washable socks require no charging or smartphone; embedded sensors continuously track foot temperature to detect the early inflammation that precedes an ulcer, and licensed nurses review the data and alert the patient's healthcare provider. Siren pairs the hardware with a remote patient monitoring service billed through providers and payers, and operates as a HIPAA-regulated healthcare business rather than a developer platform. It is backed by 500 Global and DCM Ventures. As surveyed for the API Evangelist network, Siren publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: versatile.ai
providers.description: Versatile is a construction-technology company building AI-powered crane intelligence for jobsites, primarily serving steel erectors and general contractors. Its CraneView hardware device attaches to a crane's hook block and passively captures operational data, which the Control Center software turns into real-time insight on pace, progress, productivity, and delays without asking crews to change how they work. The company is backed by Insight Partners. As of this profile Versatile publishes no public API, SDK, or developer platform; this record captures its identity, published web properties, and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: WINT
providers.description: WINT (also styled Wint) is an AI-powered water management and leak-detection platform for commercial and industrial facilities. Its IoT flow sensors, automated shut-off valves, and 24/7 staffed monitoring center use signal processing and anomaly detection to catch leaks in real time across main feeds, domestic cold and hot water, HVAC loops, cooling towers, and irrigation systems, reporting 20-25% average water-consumption reduction and up to 90% less water damage and insurance loss. WINT is backed by Insight Partners and carries NSF International, ISO, and USGBC affiliations. During enrichment no public developer API, documentation, well-known discovery surface, OpenAPI, or SDK was found; this profile captures the company's public web properties and a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: Kepler Communications
providers.description: Kepler Communications operates a cloud-based infrastructure network in space, delivering real-time connectivity, on-orbit edge compute, and hosted payload services for satellite operators and space missions. Its offerings include the Kepler Network for space-based data relay and communications, Kepler Compute for on-orbit processing, and hosted payload services that reduce the cost and technical complexity of operating in orbit. Kepler is backed by Canaan Partners, Costanoa Ventures, and Techstars. No public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or SDK has been identified; services are accessed through the Kepler customer portal and an Atlassian-hosted support service desk.

providers.name: Koska
providers.description: KOSKA Corporation (株式会社KOSKA) is a Tokyo-based manufacturing technology company, founded in October 2018, that applies cost accounting and IoT to the Japanese factory floor. Its flagship product GenKan (原価管理自動化サービス) automates cost management for high-mix low-volume manufacturers: RFID and power sensors installed on existing equipment capture work progress and consumption without changing operator behavior, then make processing cost, material cost, and electricity cost visible line by line, feeding real actual-cost figures and KPI setting back to the shop floor and management. A second product, ながら記録 (Nagara Kiroku / "vScribe"), is an AI record-keeping app for manufacturing, construction, and logistics sites — photograph a paper form and AI generates the input form, then operators record hands-free by speaking, with the AI parsing natural speech into structured records, inspections, and reports. KOSKA is led by CEO Kenichiro Sone (Forbes 30 Under 30 Asia 2021) and advised by Hiroshi Obata, former chair of the Japan Cost Accounting Association. As of this profile the company publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal — it is a sensor-and-SaaS product company, not an API provider.

providers.name: EcoPlant
providers.description: EcoPlant provides an intelligent air compressor control and monitoring platform for industrial facilities. The Ecoplant 360 solution uses IoT sensors, AI-powered dynamic controls, and predictive analytics to optimize compressed-air systems in real time, preventing downtime, improving reliability, and reducing compressed-air energy costs by up to 50 percent. It installs in under a week with no installation fees and is compatible with most compressor brands and existing plant technology.

providers.name: Hippo
providers.description: Hippo is a US homeowners insurance carrier headquartered in Palo Alto, California, operating as the insurance subsidiary of Hippo Holdings Inc. (NYSE: HIPO). Founded in 2015, Hippo modernizes home insurance with instant online quotes — typically under sixty seconds — and a smart home oriented approach that pairs policies with proactive home maintenance guidance through the Hippo Home mobile app, DIY checklists, home health scoring, and partnerships with smart device makers. The company writes homeowners, condo, landlord, flood, auto, and pet policies and operates as both a direct-to-consumer brand and an MGA distributing through a network of 70+ carrier partners, including Bamboo, Stillwater, Nationwide, American Integrity, Liberty Mutual, and Progressive. Hippo's underwriting capacity is anchored by its wholly-owned admitted carrier, Spinnaker Insurance Company, acquired in 2020. Hippo serves 500K+ homeowners across the United States, with concentrated presence in Texas, California, Arizona, Colorado, Missouri, Ohio, South Carolina, Tennessee, and Virginia. There is no publicly documented developer API, SDK, or open-source release for Hippo or Spinnaker; the GitHub organization hippoinsurance exists but has no public repositories, and the api.hippo.com hostname is not exposed to the public internet. Integrations with smart home device partners, agents, and MGA carriers are handled through private partner channels rather than an open developer program.

providers.name: Aptos Orbital
providers.description: Aptos Orbital (legal entity Cryptosat, Inc.) is a space technology company, founded in 2021 and backed by the Techstars Space Accelerator, that builds integrated hardware for satellites and spacecraft. Its flagship Aptos Terminal combines space-hardened, radiation-tolerant edge compute (with proprietary SEU/SEL protection), persistent global satellite communications, and cloud connectivity to platforms such as AWS and Azure into a single device. The company advertises 5.5+ years of proven orbital operation, 99% global data coverage, and TRL9 readiness for LEO applications, with development licenses, engineering models, and flight models offered to spacecraft builders. Aptos Orbital was added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio lead; as of this pass the company publishes hardware brochures and a "start developing" onboarding form but no public API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: FANUC
providers.description: FANUC Corporation is a Japanese multinational headquartered in Oshino, Yamanashi at the base of Mount Fuji, and is one of the world's largest suppliers of factory automation, industrial robots, and CNC (computer numerical control) systems. Founded in 1972 after spinning out of Fujitsu's numerical control division (originated 1955) under Seiuemon Inaba, FANUC pioneered commercial NC and CNC technology and by the early 1980s held roughly half of the global CNC market. The company operates three primary business segments: FA (CNC systems, servo motors, lasers, and PMC controls for machine tools), Robot (industrial arms from the LR Mate and M-series through the heavy-payload M-2000iA, plus the CRX collaborative robot family), and ROBOMACHINE (ROBODRILL machining centers, ROBOCUT wire EDM, and ROBOSHOT all-electric injection molding machines). FANUC's primary developer surface is FOCAS (FANUC Open CNC API Specification), a licensed C/C++ library (fwlib32.dll) used by machine builders and MES/OEE vendors to read CNC state over Ethernet, plus KAREL and Teach Pendant (TP) programming on the robot controllers and a published ROS 2 driver for the CRX collaborative arms. FANUC does not operate a public REST developer portal or publish OpenAPI specifications; integrations are partner-driven through MTConnect adapters, OPC UA servers, FIELD system edge apps, and the FANUC America customer/training portals.

providers.name: Lumos Helmet
providers.description: Lumos (Lumos Helmet) is a consumer hardware company that designs and manufactures smart bike helmets and connected bike lights with integrated safety features such as turn signals, brake lights, and high-visibility LED lighting. Its product line spans commuter, e-bike, and kids' helmets plus standalone smart bike lights, controlled through companion iOS and Android mobile apps. Backed by Techstars, Lumos sells direct-to-consumer through an online store; it does not currently publish a public API, developer platform, or SDK. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline, which confirmed no programmatic API surface and captured the company's identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Nanit
providers.description: Nanit is a consumer smart baby-monitoring company whose camera-based system tracks infant sleep patterns, monitors breathing motion through wearable Breathing Wear, and sends real-time safety notifications to parents. Its products pair 1080p HD video with computer-vision analytics, alongside a companion mobile app, sound machines, and sleep-guidance content, sold direct-to-consumer as hardware plus app subscriptions. As of this enrichment pass Nanit publishes no public developer API, SDK, CLI, or webhook surface for third-party integration.

providers.name: NinjaBlocks
providers.description: Ninja Blocks Inc was an Australian Internet-of-Things startup (founded 2012, backed by 500 Global / 500 Startups) behind the Ninja Block and Ninja Sphere home-automation hubs. It offered a cloud-connected platform with a RESTful API (base https://api.ninja.is/rest/v0/) for reading sensor data and controlling actuators, plus first-party client libraries for Node.js, PHP, Ruby, Lua and Arduino, a `ninja-toolbelt` CLI, and OAuth-based authentication. The company ceased operation and its web and API hosts are no longer online; this profile preserves the surviving first-party open-source client libraries and API tooling published to npm and GitHub. Added to the API Evangelist network from the 500 Global portfolio and enriched from public package registries and the github.com/ninjablocks organization.

providers.name: Nodal Industries
providers.description: Nodal Industries, operating as Nodal Security, is a network security company and 500 Global portfolio startup that makes Numa, a plug-and-play network security appliance providing protective oversight of every connected device on a home or small-office network. Rather than per-device antivirus software, Numa works at the network layer, intercepting malicious traffic before it reaches devices using real-time threat intelligence powered by Suricata, with automatic updates and minimal setup. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a marketing website only and exposes no public API, SDK, developer documentation, or event surface.

providers.name: Open Bionics
providers.description: Open Bionics is a Bristol, UK-based medical technology company that designs and manufactures advanced multi-grip bionic arms for children and adults with upper-limb differences. Its Hero product family (Hero ARM, Hero PRO, Hero RGD, Hero FLEX and Hero GAUNTLET) pairs 3D-printed, lightweight myoelectric prosthetic hands with an ecosystem of MyoPods wireless electrodes and the Sidekick companion app, delivered through a network of specialist prosthetists and clinics in the US and UK. Added to the API Evangelist network as a Techstars portfolio company; enrichment probing found no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or event surface.

providers.name: Prophetic
providers.description: Prophetic is a San Francisco-based neurotechnology startup, incorporated in January 2023, building the world's first wearable device for stabilizing lucid dreams. Its "Halo" headband pairs EEG sensing with targeted transcranial focused ultrasound (tFUS) to noninvasively stimulate the prefrontal cortex, driven by an in-house AI model, Morpheus-1, that takes brain activity as its prompt and generates shaped ultrasonic waveforms as output. Backed by BoxGroup and a16z's Scout Fund, Prophetic sells its neuromodulation headbands direct-to-consumer. The company was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass Prophetic publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or programmatic integration surface — it is a consumer hardware and wellness company.

providers.name: Savi Technology
providers.description: Savi Technology provides Internet of Things (IoT) and active RFID (aRFID) solutions for real-time supply chain visibility, asset tracking, and cargo security. Combining active RFID tags, environmental condition sensors, and machine intelligence, Savi delivers location, condition, and estimated-time- of-arrival data for cargo and high-value assets across government, military (including U.S. Department of Defense in-transit visibility), and commercial supply chains. The company is headquartered in Wilmington, North Carolina. As of this enrichment pass, Savi Technology exposes no public developer portal, OpenAPI/Swagger definition, SDKs, or documented web API; its only authenticated surface is the aRFID-VI customer catalog (savirfidcatalog.net).

providers.name: Skylo
providers.description: Skylo Technologies is a satellite communications company based in Mountain View, California, operating a global Non-Terrestrial Network (NTN) that lets standard smartphones and IoT cellular devices connect directly to satellites over 3GPP Release 17 direct-to-device (D2D) standards for SMS, sensor telemetry, and other low-bandwidth messaging. Founded in 2017 and backed by DCM, SoftBank, Intel Capital, Innovation Endeavors, BMW i Ventures, Samsung Catalyst, Next47, Seraphim Space, and NGP Capital, Skylo has commercial service across the US, Brazil, Australia, New Zealand, and Europe. Skylo does not publish a public REST/HTTP API; developer integration is device-level (certified modules such as Quectel, Murata, Blues Notecard and Particle) with detailed procedures gated behind a partner Knowledge Base. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company and its developer surface.

providers.name: Volterra
providers.description: Volterra was a Santa Clara-based distributed cloud company founded in 2017 by Ankur Singla, Harshad Nakil, and Ashish Ranjan, offering the VoltMesh (multi-cloud networking and security) and VoltStack (edge application deployment) SaaS platforms on a global application delivery network. Backed by roughly $50M from Khosla Ventures, Mayfield, M12, Samsung NEXT, and Itochu Technology Ventures, Volterra was acquired by F5 in January 2021 for approximately $500M and became the foundation of F5 Distributed Cloud Services. Its API surface (ves.io.schema, console.ves.volterra.io) is catalogued in the F5 Distributed Cloud Services profile, while the Volterra-branded Terraform provider and vesctl CLI remain published and maintained by F5.

providers.name: Instabeat
providers.description: Instabeat is a San Francisco based swimming technology company that builds a heart-rate monitoring device integrated directly into swim goggles, giving swimmers real-time, color-coded effort feedback (heart-rate zones), automatic stroke detection, lap counting, pace, distance and rest-interval tracking without a chest strap or wrist watch. Paired with the Instabeat mobile app and myinstabeat.com, it delivers data-driven training insights so swimmers can adjust workouts in the water rather than after the session. The company sells the device through a Shopify storefront and has tested the product with 250+ swimmers across 56 countries. Added to the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio company; no public developer or API surface has been identified.

providers.name: Carnot Fleet
providers.description: Carnot Fleet (Carnotfleet) is a Seoul-based cold-chain technology company that converts non-refrigerated vehicles into temperature-controlled units in under 30 minutes using modular insulation panels and proprietary solid-state thermoelectric heat pumps, spanning frozen, chilled, and ambient ranges with humidity control. Its Adaptive Thermal Control System (ATCS) is an AI-based autonomous control platform delivering cloud-connected temperature monitoring at 10-second intervals. Carnot Fleet surfaces its capabilities through the CF Mobile Application, the CF Portal, and CF APIs that let customers integrate the ATCS into existing logistics solutions to detect, analyze, prevent, and discover cold-chain data points and reduce post-harvest to pre-retail loss across the supply chain.

providers.name: Autonomic
providers.description: Autonomic is a connected-vehicle cloud company founded in 2016, acquired by Ford Motor Company in 2018 and fully integrated into Ford in 2023. Its flagship product, the Transportation Mobility Cloud (TMC), is one of the largest connected-vehicle cloud platforms in production, providing an API-driven platform for developers to build applications that interact with vehicles while abstracting the complexity of different vehicle models and connectivity devices. The public developer surface (the TMC Developer Portal) is gated behind partner authentication, so most technical artifacts are not publicly harvestable. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Craft Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: Humanising Autonomy
providers.description: Humanising Autonomy is a London-based behavioural AI company that builds ethical computer-vision software to understand and predict human behaviour, providing context between people and machines. Its "Behaviour AI" platform combines novel deep learning, behavioural psychology and statistical AI to analyse existing camera and video footage across automotive & ADAS, fleet telematics, city infrastructure & planning, and health & safety use cases -- improving road safety and reducing liability. The company connects to a customer's existing cameras, platform or video footage rather than exposing a public developer API. Backed by Anthemis. NOTE: the primary website (humanisingautonomy.com) is currently unreachable / parked (HTTP 404) as of 2026-07-19, indicating the company may be inactive; this profile is reconstructed from archived (Wayback) sources -- no public API, SDK registry, or developer portal was ever published.

providers.name: Hinge Health
providers.description: Hinge Health is a San Francisco-based digital musculoskeletal (MSK) care company founded in 2014 by Daniel Perez and Gabriel Mecklenburg, delivering virtual physical therapy, pelvic health, and chronic pain care to enterprise health plans, employers, and their members. The platform combines on-demand exercise therapy with a multidisciplinary care team — physical therapists, health coaches, board-certified physicians, and orthopedic specialists — augmented by 3D motion tracking, computer vision, and an in-house AI Care Assistant. Hinge Health develops Enso, an FDA-cleared, drug-free wearable that delivers proprietary electrical stimulation waveforms for pain relief, and operates HingeConnect, an EMR/claims interoperability layer that ingests records from more than one million external providers across 120,000+ care sites to coordinate care, surface surgical and opioid risk, and feed real-time clinical context into the digital clinic. The company also runs HingeSelect, a national provider network for in-person MSK care, and contracts with all five major US national health plans plus employers including Boeing, Salesforce, and US Foods. Hinge Health raised more than $1 billion from Insight Partners, Tiger Global, Coatue, and Atomico before completing its IPO on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker HNGE on May 22, 2025, pricing at $32/share and opening at $39.25 for an initial market capitalization above $3 billion. There is no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release for Hinge Health, Enso, or HingeConnect — the platform is sold as a managed clinical service to health plans and employers, and the HingeConnect interoperability surface is operated internally rather than exposed to third-party developers.

providers.name: Limbo
providers.description: Limbo is a direct-to-consumer digital weight-loss and metabolic-health program operated by Vitals in View, Inc., with subsidiaries in the UK (company no. 15047668) and Ireland (company no. 725671). Members wear a body-worn "energy sensor" that reads metabolic signals, and a companion app turns those readings into personalized, nudge-based guidance intended to change eating habits without calorie counting. The company is Seedcamp-backed, raised a seed round in September 2022, and is mid-rebrand from Limbo (limborevolution.com) to Viv (viv.co), with the marketing site now served from content.viv.co. Limbo publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or /.well-known/ discovery surface; this profile captures its identity and probed security posture only.

providers.name: Cambridge Terahertz
providers.description: Cambridge Terahertz (thzcorp.com) is an MIT-spinout physical security company building compact, AI-powered terahertz imaging sensors that detect concealed weapons -- guns, knives, explosives, and 3D-printed weapons -- as people walk naturally through entrances, without pat-downs or metal detectors. The 2-pound sensors mount like security cameras, serve hospitals, enterprises, and government facilities, and integrate with existing VMS and security systems over standard REST APIs, though the company publishes no public developer portal or API documentation. Backed by Felicis with a $12M seed round and an NSF SBIR Phase II grant.

providers.name: Lyten
providers.description: Lyten is a San Jose, California advanced-materials company founded in 2015 that invented and commercializes Lyten 3D Graphene, a tunable three-dimensional carbon supermaterial produced by converting methane into nanostructured carbon while co-producing hydrogen. Lyten applies that materials platform across four product lines: lithium-sulfur battery cells and battery systems that contain no cobalt, nickel or manganese and target roughly 40% weight savings versus lithium-ion; 3D graphene reinforced 3D printer filament; concrete admixture and structural adhesives; and chemical/environmental sensors, including the Lyten Atmos continuous methane-intelligence platform that pairs solar-powered LTE field sensors with cloud analytics and dashboards for landfill and oil-and-gas emissions monitoring. The company has raised over $600 million from investors including Stellantis, FedEx and Honeywell, operates a 145,000 sq ft pilot manufacturing facility in the Alviso district of North San Jose, acquired Cuberg's San Leandro battery assets in 2024, and in 2025 acquired Northvolt battery manufacturing assets in Poland and Sweden, establishing a European headquarters in Gdansk, Poland. Lyten is a private company; its shares trade on secondary markets such as Forge Global. It publishes no public developer API, SDK or developer portal.

providers.name: Element Science
providers.description: Element Science is a San Francisco-based medical device and digital health company focused on high-risk cardiovascular patients. Its flagship product is the Jewel Patch-Wearable Cardioverter Defibrillator (P-WCD) — a low-profile, water-resistant wearable that continuously monitors for and treats life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias in patients at temporary elevated risk of sudden cardiac arrest. The Jewel received FDA Premarket Approval in 2025 and CE Mark / UKCA marking in January 2024. Element Science is a portfolio company of GV. Added to the API Evangelist network as a lead; no public developer API or machine-readable specification has been identified for this provider at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Alterego
providers.description: Alterego is a Boston-based startup, spun out of the MIT Media Lab in 2025, building a near-telepathic silent-speech interface: a minimal, non-invasive wearable that detects the faint neuromuscular signals produced when a person internally verbalizes words, letting them interact with AI and computers without typing, tapping, or speaking aloud. Its "Silent Sense" technology responds only to intentional internal speech, keeping private thoughts private while enabling hands-free, screen-free messaging, queries, and information access. The company is pre-launch, backed by investors including Canaan, Granite Ventures, Mayfield, Rembrandt Venture Partners, and Cisco Investments. As of this profile Alterego publishes no public API or developer platform.

providers.name: B2X
providers.description: B2X is a Munich-founded hardware lifecycle orchestration company that manages the complete service journey of electronic devices for global brands and operators — from warehousing, staging and onsite deployment through customer support, maintenance and repair, returns management, refurbishment and recycling. Its proprietary B2XONE platform combines ONE Connect (self-service customer portals with track & trace and appointment booking), ONE Service (operations management for repair, warehouse, inventory and logistics) and ONE Analytics (real-time KPIs and predictive insights), delivered through a network of 155+ certified service partners across 25+ countries. B2X serves mobile and consumer electronics, retail automation, B2B/enterprise and mission-critical segments. As of this profile, B2X does not publish a public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Fishbit
providers.description: Fishbit is a smart-aquarium management company whose platform pairs a mobile app (iOS/Android) with connected hardware — the Fishbit Monitor, which tracks water parameters such as pH, temperature, and salinity in real time, and the Fishbit Controller, which wirelessly automates aquarium equipment. Hobbyists and reef keepers use the system to remotely monitor tank conditions and automate lighting, pumps, and dosing. The company sells its monitoring and control hardware through an online store and ran a device-manufacturer partner program (e.g. RapidLED Corona integration). No public API, developer portal, or SDK is currently published; this API Evangelist profile tracks the company as a connected-hardware / IoT lead.

providers.name: houmo
providers.description: HOUMO.AI (后摩智能) is a Chinese fabless semiconductor company founded in 2020 that develops compute-in-memory (CIM / storage-and-computation integrated) edge AI chips for running large language models and other AI workloads on endpoint devices. Its products include the MOMAGIC (H30) series processors, LIQING M.2 modules, and Limou (LM 5050 / LM 5070 / LM 30) AI acceleration cards, paired with the Houmo Avenue software toolchain (PyTorch / TensorFlow / ONNX, CUDA-style front end) for model quantization, compilation, and deployment. The company targets edge inference, autonomous driving, embodied robotics, and intelligent mobile devices, and runs a developer community with documentation and downloads. This profile is a hardware / AI-chip vendor with a developer toolchain rather than a public web API provider; no REST/OpenAPI, OAuth, or hosted API surface was found.

providers.name: Inmarsat
providers.description: Inmarsat is a British satellite communications operator founded in 1979, originally as the International Maritime Satellite Organization, providing voice, data, broadband, and IoT services over a global L-band, Ka-band, and multi-band fleet of geostationary satellites. In May 2023 Viasat completed its acquisition of Inmarsat, and the combined company now operates Inmarsat's GX (Global Xpress), BGAN, IsatData Pro (IDP), and Fleet Xpress services alongside Viasat's ViaSat-3 constellation as a unified multi-orbit network. Inmarsat serves four core markets — Maritime (NexusWave, Fleet Xpress, Fleet One, FleetBroadband, Inmarsat C/GMDSS), Aviation (SwiftBroadband, GX Aviation, Jet ConneX, SB-S safety services), Government (L-TAC, GX, BGAN M2M), and Enterprise/IoT (BGAN M2M, IsatData Pro, IsatM2M, NB-NTN). Inmarsat operates a developer program at developer.inmarsat.com with documented APIs for BGAN network management, GSPS voice, Global Xpress, IsatData Pro messaging, Fleet Edge assurance, and Fleet Edge hardware replacement; access to interactive Swagger documentation is gated behind developer registration and approval, though the IsatData Pro Messaging API has an open-source Apache-2.0 Node.js client published on GitHub. Inmarsat is also one of the participating operators in the GSMA NB-NTN (Non-Terrestrial Network) standards work for satellite-extended cellular IoT, with Viasat-led proof-of-concept code for NIDD (Non-IP Data Delivery) published under the inmarsat-enterprise GitHub organization.

providers.name: Scout
providers.description: Scout (Scout Space) is a Techstars- and venture-backed space technology company founded in 2019 that builds next-generation orbital sensing and autonomy for Space Domain Awareness (SDA). Its in-space products, first launched in 2021, let spacecraft see and understand objects around them through electro-optical and infrared sensors (the Owl long-range SDA sensor line), edge processing hardware, mission autonomy software developed with the U.S. Space Force, and mission-design analysis. Scout supplies cross-orbit intelligence and dynamic space operations to government and commercial operators and has been awarded multiple AFWERX SBIR and USSF TACFI contracts. Scout does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its identity and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Auradine (Velaura AI)
providers.description: Auradine, Inc. is a Silicon Valley semiconductor and infrastructure company founded in 2022, in 2026 rebranded as Velaura AI, Inc. The company designs ultra-low-power compute solutions for data center, edge, and physical AI applications, anchored by its Titan Core silicon design and IP platform that reduces the power required for AI compute while maintaining performance. Its Teraflux product line delivers high-efficiency Bitcoin mining hardware (3nm ASICs, air- and hydro-cooled miners, containers, and fleet management software) deployed by leading Bitcoin data center operators. Auradine raised over $300 million across its funding rounds, including a $153M Series C, and is backed by investors including DCVC. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; Auradine/Velaura AI publishes no public developer API or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Code Metal
providers.description: Code Metal is a Boston-based AI company building a verifiable code translation and optimization platform for mission-critical, edge, and regulated industries including defense, automotive, semiconductor, robotics, and aerospace. The platform ingests high-level research and prototype code (Python, MATLAB, Julia) and produces optimized, edge-ready low-level code across C/C++, Rust, VHDL, Verilog, CUDA, HIP, and ONNX, using a divide-and-conquer pipeline that instruments and tests, translates and verifies functional equivalence, then optimizes and benchmarks against target CPU/GPU/FPGA runtimes. Code Metal was surfaced as a portfolio company of Accel and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer documentation, or specification surface; this profile carries verified company identity plus a probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Commsignia
providers.description: Commsignia is a Budapest-based V2X (Vehicle-to-Everything) technology company building connected vehicle and smart infrastructure solutions for the automotive and transportation industries. Its portfolio spans roadside units (RSUs) and onboard units (OBUs), a V2X software stack, and cloud services grouped into product suites: Roadway Intelligence, Emergency Safety, Fleet, Automotive, Smart Infrastructure, and Connected Vehicle. The company turns isolated roadway and vehicle data silos into real-world operational intelligence for safer roads and improved traffic flow. As of this enrichment pass Commsignia publishes no public developer API, REST/OpenAPI reference, SDK, or developer portal; technical integration is handled through direct engagement. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech.

providers.name: Hippo
providers.description: Hippo is a digital home insurance provider operating as Hippo Insurance Services, a subsidiary of Hippo Holdings Inc. (NYSE: HIPO). Headquartered in California and domiciled in Delaware, Hippo sells homeowners, Hippo+, auto, flood, pet, landlord, and fire insurance through a network of more than 70 carrier partners, including its in-house carrier Spinnaker Insurance Company. The company serves more than 500,000 homeowners across all 50 states and pairs policies with the Hippo Home app, which offers home maintenance checklists, seasonal guidance, and a home care score to encourage proactive home upkeep. Hippo Holdings also operates First Connect Insurance Services, an independent-agent platform, and Spinnaker Specialty Insurance Company and Mainsail Insurance Company. Hippo does not publish a public developer portal, partner API, or SDK; there is no documented public REST API, OpenAPI specification, or open-source GitHub presence (the `hippoinsurance` GitHub organization exists but is empty).

providers.name: INURU
providers.description: INURU (Inuru GmbH) is a Berlin-based printed-electronics company that manufactures ultra-thin, flexible printed OLED lighting for smart packaging, labels, apparel, and medical products. Its core product, the Elf (Embeddable Luminous Film), combines an inkjet-printed OLED, a power source, and a microchip into a paper-thin, waterproof film that can glow in any shape and respond to touch, motion, or sound. Founded in 2016, Inuru operates the automated "Dragon Factory" OLED production line in Wildau and works with brands such as Coca-Cola and Marvel on interactive, sustainable smart-packaging and medication-adherence labels. This is a company/provider record in the API Evangelist network; Inuru is a hardware and smart-packaging manufacturer and does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: AgroMatch
providers.description: AgroMatch is a Chilean agricultural technology (AgTech) platform, founded in 2018 and backed by 500 Global, that connects farmers, agricultural contractors, and machinery owners in a single collaborative marketplace. Often described as the "Airbnb of agricultural machinery," it lets machinery owners lease idle equipment (tractors, implements, portable bins) during low-use periods to farmers in regions whose seasons do not coincide, and lets farmers contract or offer agricultural services such as harvesting, soil preparation, and crop applications. The platform also supports buying and selling new and used machinery, operative leasing, and supplier networking, using artificial intelligence and IoT to match demand for machinery with available supply. AgroMatch reports more than 400 B2B customers across Chile and Perú with operations extending to the US, Colombia, and Mexico. The company operates as a web and mobile application at app.agromatch.cl; no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal is published as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Ethonai
providers.description: EthonAI AG is an ETH Zurich spin-off (founded 2021, Zurich, Switzerland) that builds an Industrial AI Platform — the Manufacturing Analytics System (MAS). It applies Causal AI through a no-code platform so manufacturing engineers can move from reactive dashboards to prescriptive quality and process analytics, deploying models to production in hours. The platform ships as Analyst, Inspector, and Operator modules, is cloud-agnostic (AWS, GCP, Azure), and is API-first: data flows in and out via a REST API, MQTT streaming, and a Python SDK for notebooks and custom applications. EthonAI is used by manufacturers including Siemens, Bosch, Roche, and Lindt & Sprüngli, is part of the Siemens Xcelerator ecosystem, and is backed by Index Ventures, General Catalyst, Earlybird, and Founderful. It does not publish a public API reference or developer portal; its API and SDK are documented inside the authenticated product.

providers.name: Bug Labs
providers.description: Bug Labs is a New York City enterprise software company founded in 2006, first as one of the earliest open-source modular hardware makers and later as an enterprise IoT platform provider serving Fortune 500 customers including Verizon, Comcast, VMware, Ford, Charter and Orange. Its current flagship product, Signalpattern, targets workflow fragmentation by mapping and connecting dispersed enterprise systems, automating cross-system tasks, and letting users interact with APIs directly without writing code. Bug Labs previously operated the well-known public IoT APIs dweet.io, dweetpro.io and freeboard.io; all three are decommissioned and the company publishes no developer portal, API documentation or public API today. Backed by Union Square Ventures, Spark Capital and Court Square Ventures.

providers.name: Philips
providers.description: A Dutch multinational health technology company focused on diagnostic imaging, patient monitoring, image-guided therapy, ultrasound, sleep and respiratory care, and connected care solutions. Philips transitioned from a diversified electronics conglomerate to a dedicated healthcare technology leader and operates the HealthSuite Digital Platform (HSDP) as its cloud-based platform for connected health applications. HSDP exposes Identity & Access Management, Provisioning, IoT/Connect, Foundation, Cognitive, Clinical Data, and Notification building blocks to enable consumer health and professional healthcare applications, but access is gated behind a customer portal at www.hsdp.io with developer documentation distributed to authenticated customers and partners rather than the open public web. Philips also operates vertical Connected Care offerings (Patient Monitoring, eICU/Capsule, Sleep & Respiratory Care/SimplyGo, IntelliSpace) layered on HSDP. The legacy Philips Hue lighting API is no longer a Philips offering - Hue has been spun off into Signify and is published at developers.meethue.com.

providers.name: xiaoyi
providers.description: Xiaoyi Technology (小蚁科技), operated by Shanghai Yunyi Zhilian Technology (上海云蚁智联) and best known for its YI-brand cameras, is a Shanghai-based smart-imaging company that emerged from the Xiaomi ecosystem. It builds action cameras, the M1 mirrorless camera, smart home/security cameras, dash cams and in-car rearview systems, VR cameras, and handheld gimbals, and now positions itself around computer vision, edge intelligence, and edge computing solutions for smart mobility, smart home, smart retail, smart parks, and smart communities, selling through JD and Tmall storefronts. Surfaced as a Qiming Venture Partners portfolio company. No public developer API surface was found during enrichment - the developer subdomain (dev.xiaoyi.com) returns 502, api.xiaoyi.com serves only a placeholder page, and no API documentation, OpenAPI specs, official GitHub organization, or first-party registry packages were located.

providers.name: Audi Connect / myAudi
providers.description: Audi Connect is the connected-vehicle services platform from Audi AG, the Ingolstadt, Germany-based luxury automaker and member of the Volkswagen Group. Delivered to drivers through the embedded MMI infotainment system and the myAudi companion app for iOS and Android, Audi Connect spans remote vehicle control (lock/unlock, remote start, climate pre-conditioning, EV charge management), safety and security (Emergency Call/eCall, Audi Service Request, stolen-vehicle locator, geofencing, speed alerts), and in-car infotainment (real-time traffic, satellite map imagery, parking and fuel information, weather, news, natural voice recognition, Amazon Alexa, Amazon Music, Wi-Fi hotspot, and an in-vehicle app store with Disney+ and passenger gaming on supported models). Services are packaged as Audi connect CARE (included for ten years on new U.S. Audis), Audi connect NAV (navigation and live traffic), and Audi connect PLUS (premium streaming and Wi-Fi). For EVs and PHEVs, Audi Connect adds charging-station search, remote charge monitoring, and cabin pre-conditioning. Audi does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specification, OAuth program, or partner SDK for myAudi/Audi Connect; programmatic access today is brokered by third-party connected-car aggregators (Smartcar, High Mobility, Enode, Mojio) under Audi's commercial agreements, and community projects reverse-engineer the mobile-app endpoints. Audi has publicly discussed an internal OpenAPI-driven API management strategy (with Nagarro) but the surface remains private to Audi, VW Group brands, and authorized partners.

providers.name: Omate
providers.description: Omate designs and manufactures Wearable-as-a-Service (WaaS) safety solutions built around cellular-connected smartwatches for people who need protection — seniors, children, and lone workers. Its devices (such as the O6L Pro line, marketed under the Omahome brand) combine GPS location tracking, SOS calling, fall detection, and two-way voice into a managed hardware-plus-service offering sold direct to consumers and through partners. Omate is a hardware and connected-device company; as of this profile it exposes no public developer program, API, or SDK. This entry was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio lead and enriched with an identity and domain-security pass.

providers.name: Tractive
providers.description: Tractive is an Austrian pet-technology company, founded in October 2012 in Pasching, Austria and led by CEO Michael Hurnaus, that builds GPS location and health-monitoring trackers for dogs and cats. Its collar-attached devices (such as the DOG and CAT GPS trackers) pair with a subscription mobile app to deliver real-time worldwide location, virtual fences, activity, sleep and, more recently, resting heart-rate and respiratory-rate health intelligence to more than 1.4 million active subscribers. Tractive was acquired by Italy's Bending Spoons in 2026. Tractive does NOT publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal — its backend HTTP API (api.tractive.com) is private to its own apps; the only clients are unofficial, community reverse-engineered libraries. This profile enriches the company's identity for the API Evangelist network; there is no official API surface to catalog.

providers.name: morewis
providers.description: Morewis (摩尔元数) is a Chinese industrial software company founded in 2017 and headquartered in Xiamen, Fujian, that develops cloud-based Manufacturing Execution System (MES) and Manufacturing Operations Management (MOM) software for the manufacturing sector. Its Morewis Cloud industrial internet platform, MoreDEV low-code development platform (including the WisIDE cloud IDE), and MoreAgent / N³ industrial AI large model let manufacturers build and run smart-factory applications with reduced hand coding. Reference clients include Haier, Hisense, Aisino, Inspur, and 3Trees Group. The company raised a ~100M yuan Series B led by Qiming Venture Partners. No public English-language REST API, OpenAPI, SDK, or GitHub organization was found; the developer surface is a China-hosted low-code industrial application platform.

providers.name: Securly
providers.description: Securly is a K-12 student safety company whose platform spans web filtering, device management (MDM), classroom management, and student wellness/self-harm and threat monitoring across the web, email, and cloud drives. Securly is deployed by school districts and integrates with the school technology stack - Google Workspace, Microsoft 365/Entra, Apple School Manager, and Student Information Systems via the OneRoster and rostering standards. Securly's public developer surface is limited and access-gated - it primarily CONSUMES rostering and identity APIs from external systems rather than exposing a documented public developer API. The one provider-exposed API is a credential-gated Securly MDM API used by third-party device/asset systems to pull device inventory and assign or unassign students to devices; its endpoints and base URL are provisioned per tenant and are not publicly documented as a reference.

providers.name: Cron Systems
providers.description: Cron Systems (now operating as Cron AI) builds deep-learning perception software for 3D sensor and LiDAR data. Its flagship platform, senseEDGE, performs real-time 3D object detection, classification, and tracking from point-cloud data at the edge, with multi-sensor fusion and adverse-weather resilience. The technology serves intelligent transportation systems, smart infrastructure, autonomous mobility, smart cities, and security and surveillance — powering use cases such as traffic management, autonomous tolling, crowd and queue management, smart parking, vehicle counting, and airport and aircraft-movement monitoring. Object output is emitted as JSON and Flatbuffers binary over WebSocket, with a web-based configuration and visualizer utility, VPN and PTP time-synchronization support, and a privacy-preserving, GDPR-compliant design. Cron AI was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; the company currently publishes no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface.

providers.name: DayOne
providers.description: DayOne is a hyperscale data center company delivering next-generation digital infrastructure for cloud, AI, and edge computing workloads. Spun out of the GDS International business and backed by SoftBank Vision Fund 2, DayOne develops and operates strategically located, interconnected data center campuses across Asia-Pacific — Singapore, Johor (Malaysia), Batam (Indonesia), Hong Kong, Tokyo, and Bangkok — and is expanding into Europe with a launch market in Finland. The company positions itself as a build-to-suit and hyperscale partner focused on power availability, connectivity, and sustainable operations rather than as a public API or developer-platform provider; there is no public developer portal, API, or SDK surface at this time.

providers.name: Evreka
providers.description: Evreka is a smart waste and recycling management technology company offering an end-to-end "Sustainability as a Service" platform that digitizes the entire waste management lifecycle. Its software suite spans operations, fleet, asset, MRF, and workforce management, route optimization, citizen engagement, and EPR/PRO management, complemented by IoT hardware such as fill-level sensors, vehicle and container trackers, and RFID readers. Evreka serves dumpster rental, recycling centers, medical, hazardous and liquid waste, construction and demolition, local authorities, and cross-border waste operators. Backed by 500 Global, it is tracked in the API Evangelist network; no public API or developer portal is currently published.

providers.name: TruckLabs
providers.description: TruckLabs built TruckWings, an automated tractor-mounted aerodynamic device that closes the gap between the tractor and trailer to reduce aerodynamic drag, cutting fuel consumption by a proven 3-6% and eliminating roughly 7-10 metric tons of CO2 per truck each year with an 18-24 month payback. The device deploys automatically at highway speed and retracts below it, reduces buffeting and trailer sway in crosswinds, and installs on both new builds and retrofits in about two hours. TruckLabs was acquired by ConMet, and trucklabs.com now redirects to the ConMet TruckWings product line. As a hardware fuel-efficiency company, TruckLabs exposes no public developer API, SDK, or well-known discovery surface; this profile captures its identity and probed domain-security posture. Backed by Uncork Capital.

providers.name: Valinor
providers.description: Valinor Enterprises is a defense and government technology operational holding company — a "company of companies" that builds and buys mission-critical technologies to fill the gaps others ignore. It centralizes go-to-market, compliance, security, and operations while decentralizing engineering across lean Product Companies including Condor (attritable aerial systems), Dispatch (drone charging infrastructure, selected by DIU for the CADDS program), Harbor (expeditionary medical systems for the Marine Corps), Reflex (smart optics with onboard vision models), and Streamline (AI-enabled data collection with structured ontology write-back). Backed by General Catalyst; raised a $54M Series A led by Friends & Family Capital. Valinor publishes no public API or developer portal; its developer footprint is a GitHub organization and the @valinor-enterprises npm scope.

providers.name: Vitesse
providers.description: Vitesse is a universal physical-AI platform for industrial machines, founded by the team behind Tesla's "Model 3 automation hell" fix alongside leaders from SpaceX, Siemens, and Safran. It connects any machine - Siemens, Allen-Bradley, Fanuc, KUKA, ABB, and legacy PLCs - through 135 native OT connectors, generates control logic from a natural-language description of a process (up to 15x faster than traditional PLC programming), and runs the full stack at the edge on purpose-built industrial controllers with no cloud required. The platform layers hardware, live data dashboards and SCADA views, interoperability, physical AI, and zero-trust OT/IT cybersecurity (NIS2 and NIST aligned) into one stack, with real-time browser-based monitoring across 800,000+ machine hours. Vitesse exposes a marketing website and a login-gated product application; it does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer documentation.

providers.name: SiLC
providers.description: SiLC Technologies is a silicon photonics company headquartered in Monrovia, California that builds integrated single-chip FMCW (frequency-modulated continuous-wave) LiDAR — coherent 4D vision systems that capture depth, instantaneous velocity via micro-Doppler, and dual-polarization intensity from one photonic chip. Its Eyeonic product family spans Eyeonic Trace Ultra (a Class 1 laser line scanner for industrial automation and inspection), Eyeonic Vista (an ultra-long-range perimeter security and counter-UAS vision system with detection beyond 2 km), and Eyeonic Edge (high-precision 4D inspection of large objects). The company sells sensors, modules and vision chips to industrial and AI robotics, perimeter security, and mobility customers. It was founded by Dr. Mehdi Asghari and is backed in part by Honda. SiLC ships hardware, not software services: as of this profile it publishes no public developer program, API, SDK, documentation portal, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Apex.AI
providers.description: Apex.AI is an embedded and autonomous software company whose tagline is "software that moves," focused on safe, real-time, software-defined systems (SDx) for automotive, robotics, and other safety-critical embedded platforms. Its product line includes Apex.Grace (deterministic embedded execution framework, an automotive-grade evolution of ROS 2), Apex.Ida (high-speed fault-tolerant middleware for sensor, compute, and cloud connectivity), Apex.OS for V&V (data recording and replay for validating autonomous systems), and Apex.Alan (automated tooling and CI/CD workflows for safe software development at scale). Apex.AI also provides technical assessment, architecture, embedded and cloud software development, CI/CD pipeline, and ROS 1 to ROS 2 migration services. The company is a maintainer of substantial ROS 2 and embedded middleware open source. It is backed by Canaan Partners and Lightspeed Venture Partners. This profile was enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; Apex.AI publishes no public developer REST API at this time.

providers.name: ISAAC Instruments
providers.description: ISAAC Instruments is a Canadian provider of in-cab technology and fleet management for the trucking industry - electronic logging devices (ELD), telematics, hours-of-service (HOS) compliance, driver workflow, messaging, and fuel/performance analytics, delivered as a fully managed hardware-plus-software platform. ISAAC runs an "Open Platform" with a documented API that lets fleets and 80+ integration partners (TMS/dispatch, maintenance, fuel tax, visibility, safety/compliance) share ISAAC data with their chosen vendors. API access is partner-gated - vendors apply through the ISAAC partner program and the full API Guide and reference live behind the ISAAC InRealTime portal and Client Center rather than on a public developer site. The API surface documented here is modeled from ISAAC's public platform and partner materials; exact endpoints, base URLs, and authentication are provisioned to approved partners.

providers.name: OpenEyes Insurance
providers.description: OpenEyes Insurance (OpenEyes Insurance Agency, Inc.) is an Austin, Texas-based insurtech startup, with an additional New York office, that provides commercial auto insurance for truck and bus fleet operators bundled with proprietary risk-prevention technology. Its offering pairs fleet coverage with real-time driver monitoring, AI dashcams, safety analytics, customized driver training, and 24/7 claims management, serving both insurance agents (For Agents) and fleet operators directly (For Fleets). Founded by Yoav Oron (CEO), Dr. Omry Sendik (CTO), and Dan Charash (Chairman), OpenEyes emerged from stealth in February 2023 with a $23M Series A led by Insight Partners with Pitango First. The company operates a customer-facing fleet dashboard but does not publish a public developer API, portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Swiftlane
providers.description: Swiftlane is a San Francisco-based physical security company providing cloud-based access control and video intercom systems for multifamily residential and commercial buildings. Its touchless, mobile-first platform combines face recognition, mobile and key-card credentials, visitor PIN access, vehicle readers, smart locks, and a centralized cloud management dashboard with access logs, user management, and remote unlock. Swiftlane publishes a customer product site, a large blog, and an Intercom-hosted help center, but exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDKs, or webhooks; integrations are delivered through partners such as Okta, Azure, Google Workspace, and Eagle Eye.

providers.name: EQUIPTAL HOLDING LTD
providers.description: EQUIPTAL HOLDING LTD operates Moedatech (معداتك), Saudi Arabia's first digital procurement and rental marketplace for heavy construction equipment, connecting contractors with verified suppliers of excavators, cranes, and trucks through RFQs, real-time bidding, and audit-ready digital contracts. Founded in Riyadh in 2020 by Ali Merie and Mansour Hmaid, the company pairs the marketplace with a telematics/fleet layer (built on Traccar GPS tracking) so equipment owners can monitor real-time asset performance. The product ships as iOS and Android apps plus a web app; there is no publicly documented developer API at this time. The company is backed by 500 Global and Plug and Play Middle East. This profile was surfaced from the 500 Global portfolio and enriched from the company's public web, brand (moedatech.net), and GitHub presence.

providers.name: Hyundai Bluelink
providers.description: Hyundai Bluelink is Hyundai Motor America's connected vehicle service for Hyundai owners, providing remote vehicle control, vehicle status and diagnostics, navigation and route services, safety and security features, and EV-specific charging and climate management. Bluelink is delivered to owners through the MyHyundai with Bluelink mobile app (iOS and Android), the in-vehicle infotainment head unit, the owner web portal at owners.hyundaiusa.com, and connected smart-home and voice integrations (Amazon Alexa, Google Assistant, smartwatch apps). Feature sets vary by model year and subscription tier — typically Bluelink, Bluelink+, and Bluelink Connected Care / Remote / Guidance bundles — and include remote start with climate, remote door lock/unlock, remote horn and lights, vehicle finder, stolen vehicle recovery and SVI, automatic collision notification, SOS emergency assistance, monthly vehicle health reports, destination search (powered by Google), in-vehicle Wi-Fi hotspot (via AT&T on supported models), and EV-specific remote charge start/stop, charge schedule, charge-level monitoring, and pre-conditioning. Bluelink is a consumer-facing, owner-authenticated service. Hyundai does not publish a public developer portal, public OpenAPI specification, or self-serve API keys for third-party integration with Bluelink vehicle endpoints; access is limited to authenticated owners through Hyundai's first-party apps and to enterprise partners under contract (fleet, insurance telematics, charging networks, smart-home platforms). A community ecosystem of reverse-engineered, unofficial Python and Node.js clients (Hyundai-Kia-Connect/hyundai_kia_connect_api, Home Assistant integrations, Bluelinky) is used by enthusiasts and home automation users, but these are not endorsed, supported, or governed by Hyundai and may break at any time.

providers.name: Sandbar
providers.description: Sandbar is a consumer hardware and AI company behind Stream, a private voice ring and conversational notes app. Worn on the finger, Stream pairs a discreet private microphone, a glass touchpad, and silent haptics with an on-device "Inner Voice" assistant so people can capture notes, reminders, and todos, dictate speech-to-text across any iOS or Mac app, and think aloud without reaching for a phone. Backed by Kindred Ventures and True Ventures, Sandbar is a preorder-stage consumer product; it publishes a marketing site, an About/Us page, and a Careers page, but no public developer portal, API, or SDK surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: INDOS
providers.description: INDOS (Garment IO) is an AI-powered manufacturing operations platform built for labor-intensive garment and apparel production facilities. Its cloud-based system unifies Manufacturing Execution (MES), Quality Management (QMS), Maintenance Management (MMS), and Warehouse Management (WMS) into a single real-time view of the factory floor. A shop-floor hardware device captures operator and production-line data, and the platform surfaces operator efficiency, AI anomaly detection, performance scorecards, and end-to-end control from cutting through packing. Founded by Ahmed Nounou and Mahmoud Sabae and backed by 500 Global, it serves garment manufacturers across the Middle East, North Africa, and South Asia. INDOS does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation; this profile captures its identity, web properties, and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Nothing
providers.description: Nothing is a London-based consumer technology company designing smartphones (Phone series), wireless earbuds (Ear series), and other consumer hardware under the Nothing and CMF by Nothing brands, backed by EQT Ventures and GV. Surfaced as a portfolio-company lead in the API Evangelist network. An enrichment pass confirmed Nothing publishes a consumer web presence (support centre, community, careers, playground) but no public developer API, API documentation, developer portal, SDK, or webhook surface as of this pass.

providers.name: Wisear
providers.description: Wisear is a Paris-based neurotechnology company building an AI-powered neural interface that lets people control devices through voiceless and touchless commands. Its technology reads biosignals captured by everyday wearables such as wireless earphones, AR/VR headsets and smartglasses, turning subtle facial and neural gestures into hands-free device controls. Wisear targets use cases across consumer audio, industrial augmented reality, walkie-talkie and emergency communications, gaming headsets, the metaverse and accessibility. Surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; as of this enrichment pass Wisear publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation portal — this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Sensome
providers.description: Sensome is a clinical-stage medical technology company developing tissue-sensing microchip technology and proprietary integration processes that embed real-time bio-impedance sensing into minimally invasive medical devices. Its lead product, the Clotild Smart Guidewire System (manufactured with Asahi Intecc), is the first tissue-sensing neurovascular guidewire, providing physicians real-time blood clot characterization to guide Acute Ischemic Stroke treatment; additional indications include lung cancer biopsy guidance. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Partech, Sensome is a medical-device hardware company with no public API, SDK, or developer platform at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Theta EdgeCloud
providers.description: Theta EdgeCloud is a distributed, hybrid AI and video cloud built on the Theta Network blockchain, offering on-demand GPU compute for AI model training, fine-tuning, inference, video transcoding, and live streaming. EdgeCloud aggregates GPU capacity from data-center hyperscaler partners and a global community of Edge Nodes (consumer and enterprise GPUs) into a single dispatchable compute layer addressable via REST, JSON-RPC, and SDK clients. Core services include EdgeCloud AI Services (on-demand model inference APIs for LLMs, image, audio, and multimodal models such as Llama, Stable Diffusion, FLUX, and Whisper; agentic RAG chatbots; GPU-backed Jupyter notebooks; dedicated GPU pod deployments; and AI training with GPU clusters), EdgeCloud Video Services (the Theta Video API for upload, transcoding, livestream ingestion, DRM, NFT-gated playback, and webhooks), EdgeStore (decentralized object storage), and the EdgeCloud Client (an installable node that earns TFUEL for contributing GPU and bandwidth). Developers authenticate with x-api-key tokens issued from the EdgeCloud dashboard, manage deployments programmatically through api.thetaedgecloud.com and the Node.js SDK @thetalabs/theta-edgecloud, and access on-demand model endpoints (also distributed through RapidAPI). The Theta blockchain layer is EVM-compatible with an Ethereum RPC adaptor, supports TNT-20 tokens and NFTs, and underwrites EdgeCloud's payment, rewards, and staking economy through the THETA governance token and TFUEL gas token. Theta operates as Theta Labs, headquartered in San Jose, California.

providers.name: Open mHealth
providers.description: Open mHealth is a nonprofit, community-driven initiative that develops open standards and open-source software for making patient-generated health data interoperable across mobile apps, wearables, clinical systems, and electronic health records. Its core contribution is a library of clinically validated JSON Schema data point schemas — covering physical activity, sleep, heart rate, blood pressure, body weight, blood glucose, and other vital signs — with the sleep, physical-activity, and metadata schemas now superseded by IEEE 1752.1, the IEEE standard for Mobile Health Data co-shepherded by the Open mHealth community. Around the schemas Open mHealth ships a stack of Apache-2.0 reference implementations: Shimmer (a Java/Spring server that pulls health data from Fitbit, Google Fit, iHealth, Misfit, RunKeeper, and Withings APIs and normalizes it into Open mHealth or IEEE 1752.1 data points), omh-dsu-ri (a Data Storage Unit reference implementation exposing an OAuth 2.0-secured Data Point REST API on top of MongoDB and PostgreSQL), Granola (an Objective-C library that serializes Apple HealthKit samples into Open mHealth JSON), a web visualizations library built on D3 and Plottable.js, the OMH-on-FHIR mapping that aligns Open mHealth data points to HL7 FHIR resources, and a sample-data-generator. Open mHealth operates as the steward of the standard, the schema and unit registry at registry.openmhealth.org, and a developer community of thousands of developers and health organizations including Cornell Tech, Kaiser Permanente, Stanford School of Medicine, UC Davis, and UCSF. The project has no commercial API, no paid tier, and no hosted SaaS — all artifacts are open source under Apache 2.0 and the standard itself is openly published.

providers.name: Praan
providers.description: Praan (Praan Climate Technologies) is a deep-tech climate startup working to democratize access to clean, healthy air and to rebuild the atmosphere by capturing air pollution and greenhouse gases with novel filterless technology. Its products include HIVE, an air-purification device for homes and commercial spaces paired with a companion mobile application, and MK II, an air-purification system for industrial environments. Praan is backed by Prosus Ventures. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and enriched through the API Evangelist pipeline; as of this pass Praan publishes a consumer hardware and mobile-app surface but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation.

providers.name: DNOW
providers.description: DNOW Inc. (NYSE: DNOW), formerly NOW Inc. and operating as DistributionNOW, is a Houston-headquartered Fortune 1000 distributor of pipe, valves, fittings (PVF), pumps and packaged, engineered process and production equipment serving the upstream, midstream, downstream energy, and industrial sectors. Spun off from National Oilwell Varco in 2014 and built on a heritage that spans more than 160 years, DNOW combines a global network of distribution branches and engineering facilities with the DigitalNOW platform — shop.dnow.com B2B eCommerce, cXML/OCI ERP punchout integrations, the eSpec product configurator, the AccessNOW automated inventory control system, and a library of customer-facing mobile applications. DNOW does not publish a public developer portal, OpenAPI specifications, or a self-serve API program; customer integrations are delivered through configured cXML/OCI punchout sessions tied to enterprise ERP systems. In June 2025 DNOW announced a definitive merger agreement to acquire MRC Global in an all-stock transaction valued at approximately $1.5 billion.

providers.name: HUM Industries
providers.description: HUM Industries is a consumer hardware company building a wearable AI assistant designed to enhance social presence. The device records conversations locally, maintains a rolling buffer of recent audio, and surfaces contextual information such as names, personal details, and commitments back to the wearer through subtle audio cues. The company frames the product as giving people "the freedom to forget" by offloading memory to the device so they can stay present in the moment. At the time of profiling the product is pre-launch, offered through a preorder waitlist, with no public API, developer portal, or third-party integration surface. Backed by a16z; added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead.

providers.name: Skyfri
providers.description: Skyfri is a cleantech software and hardware company headquartered in Oslo, Norway that builds an operating platform for owners and operators of solar and battery energy assets. Founded in 2021, Skyfri combines an edge-native monitoring and control device (the SSI hardware, which speaks Modbus and SCADA over isolated RS-485 ports to inverters, meters, and sensors) with a cloud platform that automates operations, maintenance, and asset performance management. The software delivers real-time data processing, operational management, weather forecasting, dynamic benchmarking, plant insights, and fault detection to monitor generation and address underperformance and equipment failure across a global portfolio of solar and battery assets. The company has offices in Denver, London, Oslo, Singapore, and Bangalore and is backed by Speedinvest. Skyfri exposes no public developer API, documentation, or SDKs at this time; its platform is delivered as a customer application at app.skyfri.com.

providers.name: Anoria
providers.description: Anoria is a Y Combinator (Spring 2026) human-interaction company building a wearable bracelet for the EQ era that measures and tracks emotional states in real time. The device uses the company's proprietary SOMI (state-of-mind inference) model to correlate roughly 150 audio and biometric signals into a "Flow Score" that reflects a user's energy, mood, and focus, then explains why the user feels that way and what they can do about it. Anoria targets founders and creatives who treat their mental state as a performance asset, with the goal of making emotional intelligence trainable. As of mid-2026 the company is an early-stage prototype running an early-access waitlist; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation yet, so this API Evangelist profile captures verified company identity only.

providers.name: KDDI
providers.description: KDDI Corporation is a Japanese multinational telecommunications operator headquartered in Tokyo, providing mobile, fixed-line, broadband, and enterprise ICT services. KDDI markets its consumer mobile services under the au brand, alongside UQ mobile and povo, and serves enterprise customers globally through KDDI Global and KDDI America. The company operates the KDDI Open API for Developers portal exposing inquiry-gated product APIs including the au PAY Mini App platform, an XR/MEC low-latency application API, a PPM consent management API, and an au mobile Identification Support Service for KYC/identity verification. KDDI also runs the au OPEN DEVICE DEVELOPER SITE for cellular module device certification, and a KDDI Cloud Platform Service knowledge site with developer API references for cloud infrastructure.
