In 2025 KDDI became an equity partner in Aduna, the GSMA/Ericsson-backed network API venture aggregating CAMARA-aligned carrier APIs (Number Verify, SIM Swap, Quality on Demand, Device Location) across global operators. Public OpenAPI specifications are not openly published; API access is provided through contact/inquiry workflows after partner onboarding.

providers.name: Service Max
providers.description: ServiceMax is a cloud-based field service management (FSM) platform that helps asset-centric and equipment-dependent businesses improve technician productivity, streamline service operations, and maximize equipment uptime. Its product suite spans work order management, scheduling and dispatch, mobile field-technician apps, installed-base and asset management, entitlements and contracts, inventory and parts, and service analytics. Founded in 2007 and an early Mayfield portfolio company, ServiceMax was acquired by GE Digital in 2016, sold to Silver Lake in 2018, and acquired by PTC in early 2023, where it is now offered as PTC ServiceMax. This profile tracks the company within the API Evangelist network; its developer and API surface is folded into PTC.

providers.name: Bsquare
providers.description: Bsquare is an IoT and edge-software company known for Windows IoT device licensing, OS consulting (Windows, Linux, Android), device management, and its DataV IoT analytics and SquareOne data platform. Bsquare was acquired by Kontron; the bsquare.com domain now 301-redirects to www.kontron-americas.com, and the Bsquare brand operates as part of Kontron's connected-device software portfolio serving healthcare, avionics, energy, manufacturing, logistics, transportation, and hospitality. No independent public developer API or documentation surface is currently published; this profile carries the honest enrichment of the domain's live security and DNS posture.

providers.name: iTAC Software
providers.description: iTAC Software AG is an independent company of the Duerr Group and a leading provider of Manufacturing Execution System (MES) and Manufacturing Operations Management (MOM) software for discrete manufacturing. Its iTAC.MOM.Suite delivers production control, end-to-end traceability, quality management, and AI-supported analytics that help automotive, electronics, and medical-technology manufacturers implement Industry 4.0 and smart-factory operations. iTAC does not publish a public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs; system integration is delivered through the MOM platform's IoT and connectivity layers as part of a project engagement.

providers.name: Lynq
providers.description: Lynq Networks develops infrastructure-free, long-range wireless connectivity for enterprise and OEM devices, bridging the gap between short-range Bluetooth and infrastructure-dependent cellular/5G. Its technology lets original equipment manufacturers build large-area device networks without deploying traditional network infrastructure, targeting construction, agriculture, military, and public-safety use cases. Lynq is a Techstars-backed portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or machine-readable API documentation; this profile captures its identity and a domain-security probe for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Tile
providers.description: Tile is a consumer-electronics company known for its Bluetooth tracker devices, used to locate everyday items such as keys, wallets, bags, and phones through a companion mobile app and a crowd-sourced Find network. Tile was acquired by Life360 in 2021; its former site thetileapp.com now 301-redirects to life360.com. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners, Tile publishes no public developer API — this profile captures its security posture (security.txt, a HackerOne responsible-disclosure program, and probed domain security).

providers.name: Nofence
providers.description: Nofence is a Norwegian agritech company (founded 2011, headquartered in Batnfjordsøra, Norway) that produces the world's first commercial virtual fencing system for livestock. Solar-powered GPS collars worn by cattle, sheep and goats keep animals inside virtual pastures that farmers draw on a map, with the collar teaching animals boundaries through audio cues before a mild electric pulse. The system is operated entirely from a mobile app (iOS and Android) and a web portal, communicating over GPS and the cellular network with no base stations or buried wire. Farmers get real-time animal location, boundary/escape push notifications, herd replay, grazing-history and multi-species management. Nofence is a consumer/farmer-facing product: as of this profile it publishes a mobile app and web portal but no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface. It is a portfolio company of Speedinvest, added to the API Evangelist network for tracking.

providers.name: LINSOL Co.,Ltd.
providers.description: LINSOL Co.,Ltd. (린솔) is a safety-technology company headquartered in Daejeon, South Korea, founded as an in-house venture spun out of Hanwha Aerospace. LINSOL adapts acoustic detection techniques originally developed for defense landmine applications into commercial real-time hazard, accident, and environmental detection. Its product line includes Karang F (driving-environment detection), Karang S (precision acoustic signal transmission), SkyShield (fall detection), BR, Acoustic Eye (aerial security), and Safety Nova (smart integrated safety platform), sold into industrial safety, ESG, and defense security use cases. The company operates a Daejeon headquarters and research center plus a Goheung branch. LINSOL ships hardware and integrated platforms; as of a 2026-07-19 probe it publishes no public developer API, portal, SDK, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Getaround
providers.description: Getaround is a peer-to-peer car-sharing marketplace and connected-car technology company founded in 2009 and headquartered in San Francisco, California, with significant European operations across France, Germany, Spain, Belgium, Norway, and the United Kingdom. The platform pairs private and professional vehicle owners with renters who book cars by the hour or day, unlocking and starting vehicles from a mobile app rather than meeting the owner to exchange keys. The keyless experience is enabled by Getaround Connect, a proprietary in-car telematics device that the company designs and installs in shared vehicles to handle remote lock/unlock, ignition, GPS tracking, mileage reporting, fuel level monitoring, and trip event recording. Getaround acquired Drivy in 2019 to consolidate the European car-sharing market and acquired the HyreCar rideshare-driver rental marketplace in 2022. The company went public on the NYSE via a SPAC merger in December 2022 at a valuation of roughly $1.2 billion, was delisted from the NYSE in July 2024 and transferred to OTC Pink under the ticker GETR after its market capitalization collapsed to roughly $24 million. On February 11, 2025, Getaround announced it was ceasing all United States operations — including HyreCar — while preserving its European business, which continues to operate in major EU cities under the same Getaround Connect platform. Getaround has never published a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or developer portal; partner integrations with insurers, fleet operators, and automotive OEMs have historically been delivered through private, contract-bound APIs rather than a self-service developer surface. The company's GitHub organization hosts primarily forks of generic open-source libraries (Braintree SDKs, iOS testing frameworks, logging libraries) rather than first-party API artifacts.

providers.name: iRobot
providers.description: iRobot Corporation is a Bedford, Massachusetts consumer robotics company best known for the Roomba robot vacuum and the Braava and Braava jet robot mop product lines. Founded in 1990 by MIT roboticists, iRobot pioneered the home cleaning robot category and has sold tens of millions of units worldwide. Its current portfolio includes the Roomba Max, Roomba Plus, and Roomba 100/200 series vacuums and combo (vacuum + mop) models, along with AutoWash and AutoEmpty docks, the iRobot Home App for scheduling and mapping, and a cleaning accessories and trade-in program. The proposed acquisition by Amazon was abandoned in January 2024 after regulatory pushback from the European Commission, after which iRobot underwent a major restructuring and layoffs. iRobot's revenue model is direct robot and accessory sales plus recurring consumables; it does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI specification, and its homesupport documentation explicitly notes that Wi-Fi connected Roombas do not have an open API. A community of unofficial reverse-engineered libraries (dorita980, rest980, pyirobot) exists but is not endorsed by iRobot.

providers.name: Source.dev
providers.description: Source.dev builds AI-native software tooling that helps device manufacturers develop, build, and update the operating systems that run intelligent devices such as smartphones and electric vehicles. Its platform virtualizes source access (SourceFS) to cut Android checkout-and-build times from hours to minutes, replays build steps across languages and systems for faster CI, and uses LLM-driven merging (Harmony AI / Continuous Merges) to automatically resolve conflicts when applying security patches and OS upgrades to large, long-lived codebases like AOSP. The company is a sales/demo-led platform for device makers and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or self-serve documentation surface.

providers.name: Vayu Robotics
providers.description: Vayu Robotics is a Palo Alto, California robotics company building AI foundation models and sensing for autonomous mobile robots. Its stack spans Vayu Drive, an end-to-end learned, sim-first foundation model for mobility; Vayu Sense, a plenoptic sensor with embodied AI for high-resolution depth perception; a Vayu Sense Development Kit bundled with NVIDIA Orin; and Vayu One, a low-cost autonomous delivery robot for last- and middle-mile delivery. Backed by Khosla Ventures, the company was acquired by Serve Robotics in September 2025. Enrichment probing found no public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or event surface.

providers.name: AgZen
providers.description: AgZen is an MIT spinout building RealCoverage, a sensor- and AI-based system that measures and controls how many droplets of crop-protection product land on every leaf during agricultural spraying. A boom-mounted computer-vision sensor analyzes spray coverage and droplet quality in real time and displays actionable data on an in-cab tablet, automatically optimizing foliar sprays on any sprayer as the operator drives. Growers use RealCoverage to cut chemical and water use by up to 50% while maintaining or improving efficacy and yield, with a typical payback in under a year. RealCoverage retrofits onto any generation of sprayer and won Crop Protection Solution of the Year in 2025. AgZen is headquartered at Greentown Labs in Somerville, Massachusetts and is backed by DCVC Bio, Material Impact, Astanor Ventures, and Syngenta Group Ventures.

providers.name: Carnival Corporation
providers.description: Carnival Corporation & plc is the world's largest cruise company operating eight cruise line brands (Carnival Cruise Line, Princess Cruises, Holland America Line, Seabourn, Cunard, P&O Cruises, Costa Cruises, AIDA Cruises), plus the White Pass and Yukon Route. Carnival operates the OceanMedallion wearable IoT technology and mobile experience platform, the Carnival HUB app, the Princess MedallionClass app, and a portfolio of guest-facing digital experiences across its fleet of over 90 ships.

providers.name: Raytheon
providers.description: Raytheon is an American aerospace and defense manufacturer operating as a business of RTX Corporation, the world's largest aerospace and defense company. Raytheon designs, develops, and produces advanced defense systems including precision weapons, air and missile defense systems, sensors, radar, electronic warfare, command-and-control solutions, and cyber capabilities for the U.S. military and allied governments worldwide. Key products include the Patriot missile defense system, StormBreaker smart weapons, RAIVEN electro-optical/infrared sensor suites, and advanced electronic attack systems. Raytheon also develops world-class logistics software through the EAGLE team supporting production management, technical manual development, and product support data. No public developer API or machine-readable specification is available at this time; Raytheon's software solutions are deployed within government program contracts.

providers.name: Jewelbots
providers.description: Jewelbots makes smart, codable friendship bracelets designed to teach kids (primarily tween girls) to code. The wearable is an Arduino-compatible, Bluetooth Low Energy device built on a Nordic nRF chipset that friends can program with an Arduino IDE library and firmware, with a companion iOS/Android app for pairing and messaging. The project is largely open source: the Jewelbots GitHub organization publishes the Arduino library, firmware, companion app, and hardware/toolchain repositories. Jewelbots was a 500 Global (500 Startups) portfolio company; jewelbots.com now runs as a Shopify storefront. It is a hardware/firmware and education company rather than a web API provider, and exposes no first-party public HTTP/OpenAPI API.

providers.name: Kumu Networks
providers.description: Kumu Networks, Inc. is a Sunnyvale, California semiconductor and RF technology company founded in 2011 to commercialize Stanford University research into full-duplex wireless and self-interference cancellation (SIC). Its silicon and module products — RF integrated circuits, cancellers such as the K8 canceller prototype, and self-interference-cancelling smart repeaters — let a radio transmit and receive on the same or an adjacent channel at the same time, across roughly 200 MHz to 60 GHz, targeting 4G/5G/6G infrastructure, Wi-Fi, IoT, satellite, and defense and aerospace programs including US Army demonstrations and Department of Defense dynamic spectrum-sharing work. The company raised roughly $45M from investors including Khosla Ventures, New Enterprise Associates, Cisco Investments, Deutsche Telekom, Verizon Ventures, Swisscom, Singtel Innov8 and Third Point, and its shares trade on secondary marketplaces. Kumu Networks licenses hardware IP and sells modules to wireless equipment manufacturers rather than operating a public developer platform: as of August 2026 it publishes no developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDKs, CLI or public code repositories, and its own website at kumunetworks.com returns HTTP 404 from its WP Engine host (last successful Internet Archive capture 2024-08-10).

providers.name: SmartRent
providers.description: SmartRent, Inc. (NYSE: SMRT), founded in 2017 and headquartered in Scottsdale, Arizona, is a leading provider of smart home and smart property technology for the multifamily and single-family rental industries. Its platform pairs smart hardware — smart locks, thermostats, water/leak sensors, access control and hubs (Alloy, Fusion) — with cloud-based SaaS for property operators to manage connected devices at scale. Products span smart apartments, building and common-area access control, asset protection and leak monitoring, parking management, self-guided tours, Virtual Intercom (browser-based WebRTC entry), and community/resident WiFi. SmartRent exposes a partner-gated REST API and a Phoenix Sockets real-time API for integrations, but publishes no public developer portal or OpenAPI; API credentials are provisioned on request via api@smartrent.com. This profile was surfaced as a VC portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Aerohive
providers.description: Aerohive Networks was a cloud-managed networking company founded in 2006 by Changming Liu and headquartered in Milpitas, California. It pioneered controller-less, cloud-managed Wi-Fi and edge networking, managed through its HiveManager NG (later ExtremeCloud IQ) platform and access points. Aerohive went public on the NYSE under the ticker HIVE and was acquired by Extreme Networks in a deal that closed on 2019-08-09 for approximately $272 million. The company operated an Aerohive Developer Program with a public developer portal (developer.aerohive.com) and REST APIs for the HiveManager NG / ACS platform, plus a GitHub organization of reference applications. Following the acquisition the products were folded into ExtremeCloud IQ, and the legacy Aerohive API and its developer portal were retired (shutdown dated 2026-07-12), with integrators directed to migrate to the Extreme Platform ONE Developer Portal. This profile enriches the historical Aerohive API surface; it is a retired/acquired provider.

providers.name: AltoTech Global
providers.description: AltoTech Global is a Bangkok-based energy-management technology company building an AI and IoT (AIoT) platform that optimizes energy consumption and reduces carbon emissions across smart buildings. Its Alto CERO air-side and water-side products autonomously tune HVAC, VRF, and chiller-plant systems based on real-time occupancy and conditions, while Alto Digital Twin, Alto Multi-Property, and AltoACE deliver spatial building intelligence, centralized multi-site energy tracking, and AI-assisted facility engineering. Backed by 500 Global, AltoTech serves offices, malls, hotels, banks, and government facilities across Southeast Asia to help accelerate the net-zero economy.

providers.name: Tibo Energy
providers.description: Tibo Energy is an Eindhoven-based energy software company building an AI-driven Energy Management System (EMS) for commercial and industrial customers. Its SaaS platform simulates, monitors, and autonomously controls on-site energy hubs and smart grids, coordinating distributed assets such as heat pumps, EV charging stations, and battery storage to cut energy costs and emissions and to unlock additional capacity from existing infrastructure without waiting for grid upgrades. Tibo connects hardware through standard protocols such as MODBUS and OCPP via the Tibo Gateway and exchanges data with BMS, SCADA, and ERP systems through open APIs. Since launching in late 2023 it has deployed its EMS across more than 30 industrial sites and is backed by KOMPAS VC, Hitachi Ventures, SET Ventures, WEPA Ventures, and Speedinvest.

providers.name: Avery Dennison
providers.description: Avery Dennison is a global materials science and manufacturing company specializing in the design and manufacture of labeling and functional materials, packaging, and intelligent labels.

providers.name: Avnet
providers.description: Avnet is a global technology distributor and solutions provider that delivers electronic components, embedded solutions, and design and supply chain services to industrial and commercial customers.

providers.name: IKEA U.S.
providers.description: IKEA U.S. is the United States retail operation of IKEA, run by Ingka Group, the largest IKEA franchisee. The U.S. business operates ~50+ full-service stores, ~40+ Plan & Order Points, and ~80+ pick-up locations across the country, alongside the ikea.com/us e-commerce site and the IKEA mobile app. Inter IKEA Systems B.V. separately owns the IKEA Concept and brand. IKEA U.S. offers home furnishings, kitchens, appliances, lighting, the IKEA Family loyalty program, the IKEA Business Network for B2B customers, home delivery and Click & Collect, design and planning services, the Buy Back & Resell program, and IKEA Home smart products controlled via the IKEA Home smart and IKEA Home smart 1 apps. IKEA U.S. does not publish a public developer API; supplier and trading-partner integrations are handled through IKEA's vendor systems and Ingka Group's internal digital platforms.

providers.name: Lexmark International
providers.description: Lexmark International is a global imaging and IoT solutions leader that helps customers worldwide realize the full potential of their information through printers, multifunction devices, and managed print services. As of 2024, Lexmark was acquired by Xerox Holdings Corporation. Public developer APIs are not currently advertised through an open developer portal.

providers.name: Automatic
providers.description: Automatic (Automatic Labs, Inc.) was a San Francisco connected-car company founded in 2011 by Thejo Kote and Jerry Jariyasunant. Its OBD-II adapter and companion mobile app turned almost any car built since 1996 into a connected car, adding trip logging, fuel and MPG tracking, engine-light diagnostics, parking recall, and automatic crash alerts. Automatic ran a public developer platform at developer.automatic.com built around three surfaces: a REST API exposing trip, user, and vehicle data; an Events API delivering real-time driving events such as ignition on/off, hard braking, acceleration, speeding, and location changes over webhooks and websockets; and a private-beta Streaming SDK that read raw OBD-II data from the second-generation adapter over Bluetooth. SiriusXM acquired the company on 2017-04-27 for approximately $115 million, and all operations were shut down on 2020-05-28. THIS COMPANY IS DEFUNCT — no API, developer portal, or documentation remains online, and the automatic.com domain now belongs to the unrelated company Automattic. This profile is retained as a historical record of a notable connected-car API platform.

providers.name: AliciaBots
providers.description: AliciaBots is a maritime robotics company, backed by Techstars, that builds autonomous robot teams for cleaning and inspecting ship hulls. Its flagship Roverclean robot operates independently to remove marine growth and monitor hull condition in real time without interrupting a vessel's voyage, using self-learning adaptive systems, precision cleaning, and remote monitoring and control to improve fuel efficiency and help operators meet IMO regulatory standards. AliciaBots does not currently publish a public API or developer program; this profile tracks the company as a network lead.

providers.name: Atom Semiconductor
providers.description: Atom Semiconductor (Atom Semiconductor Technologies Limited) is a fabless mixed-signal chip design company founded in Hong Kong in October 2020, with offices in Shenzhen and Shanghai. It designs high-performance analog and mixed-signal semiconductors for consumer and industrial IoT systems across three product lines: digital sensor chips (temperature/humidity, pressure, optical), analog-to-digital converters (24-bit Sigma-Delta, high-precision SAR, and high-speed GSPS ADCs), and microprocessors. Its first product, the AS1412 24-bit Sigma-Delta ADC, shipped for customer trials in late 2021. The company raised roughly 100M yuan in a pre-A round led by Qiming Venture Partners (with Venus Medtech and Alibaba Entrepreneurs Fund) and was named to the Forbes Asia 100 To Watch 2022. It is a hardware chip designer and does not publish a developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Axera Tech
providers.description: Axera Intelligence (爱芯元智), operating as Axera Tech, is a Chinese fabless semiconductor company building AI-inference SoCs for edge and endpoint computing. Its chips pair the Axera Tongyuan mixed-precision NPU with the Axera Zhimu AI-ISP to power on-device vision perception, smart-vehicle autonomous-driving and intelligent-cabin platforms, and multi-tier edge-AI inference across IoT and industrial scenarios. Axera Tech was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners; it is a hardware/silicon provider and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Borqs
providers.description: Borqs Technologies Inc. is a global Internet of Things (IoT) platform solution provider delivering customizable, differentiated and scalable smart-connected IoT software, hardware and cloud-service platforms. Founded in 2007, Borqs is a Google-licensed Android and Android Wear partner with R&D centers in the U.S., India and China, and debuted publicly on Nasdaq (BRQS) in August 2017. Its BorqsWare platform powers smartphones, tablets, wearables, in-vehicle infotainment (IVI), M2M and smart-appliance solutions, and in 2021 it expanded into solar and energy storage systems (ESS) via its Holu Hou Energy acquisition. Borqs is now a Sasken Group company. No public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal is published; this profile carries company identity and a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: CIX Technology
providers.description: CIX Technology (此芯科技) is a Chinese fabless semiconductor company founded in 2021 that designs high-performance, general-purpose heterogeneous intelligent CPU chips for AI computing. The company builds low-power, high-efficiency compute platforms spanning personal computing (PC), vehicle/automotive computing, and edge computing, and partners across the Arm ecosystem (Arm, Arm China, Lenovo and others). It was surfaced as a portfolio company of the venture firm qiming and added to the API Evangelist network. CIX is a silicon/hardware company and publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal at this time; this profile captures its verifiable public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Coolso
providers.description: Coolso develops wearable gesture-recognition technology. Using patented sensing that detects muscle-vibration signals processed through its own AI model, Coolso recognizes individual finger movements and strength levels with low-latency response, from a wrist-worn device or an ordinary smartwatch's accelerometer and gyroscope without dedicated hardware. Founded by Sheng-Kuei Hsu, Wei-Lin Lee, and Jack Wu and based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, the seed-stage company is backed by 500 Global and Alchemist Accelerator and targets AR/VR interaction, with potential expansion into medical rehabilitation and sports equipment. Coolso publishes no public API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: emergen
providers.description: emergen (智昌科技集团股份有限公司, Zhichang Technology Group) is a Chinese industrial intelligence company founded by Dr. Gan Zhongxue, an expert in intelligent manufacturing. Built around its proprietary "ternary control" technology and cluster (swarm) robotics, the company positions itself as "AI + Control," delivering integrated "industrial agent" solutions that install a control "brain" into individual machines, production lines, and whole factories. Its portfolio spans robot controllers, ubiquitous controllers, industrial and collaborative robots, life-science robots, GVision 2D/3D machine vision, the GSC-AI100 sense-compute-control AI controller, a swarm-intelligence network controller, a micro-control cloud platform, and the "Jiangxin" family of industrial large models (design, production, service, and management). emergen serves automotive, electronics, equipment manufacturing, steel, metallurgy, textile, furniture, and shipbuilding sectors, plus Robotics-as-a-Service. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of qiming and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this pass no public developer/API surface was found.

providers.name: Fluent.ai
providers.description: Fluent.ai is a Montreal-based speech recognition software company, founded in 2015, that voice-enables the world's devices with embedded, offline voice AI. Its patented "speech-to-intent" technology maps a user's speech directly to their intended action using acoustic deep neural networks, with no speech-to-text transcription and no cloud connection required. The result is a small-footprint, private-by-design engine that runs fully on-device, is robust to noise, and works across languages and accents. Fluent.ai licenses two core products to OEMs and ODMs: Fluent.ai Air (Automatic Intent Recognition), an on-device command-recognition engine, and Fluent.ai Wakeword, a small-footprint wake-word / keyword-spotting solution. Target markets include smart-home devices, wearables and hearables (including True Wireless Stereo), and industrial IoT and robotics. The company distributes its technology as embedded SDKs and reference designs through hardware partnerships (e.g. Arm, Cadence Tensilica, Knowles) rather than a public cloud API. It is a portfolio company of 500 Global.

providers.name: GeoGrid
providers.description: Geogrid Co., Ltd. is a South Korean smart-building water technology company behind BLOS ("Building Oasis"), an integrated building-level water purification and monitoring system. BLOS delivers drinkable water from every tap using chemical-free ionization to eliminate rust, scale, and biofilm, and pairs it with real-time monitoring of water quality, usage, carbon emissions, and consumption plus predictive analytics for pipe condition, contamination risk, and filter replacement. Geogrid targets schools, hotels and resorts, public institutions, and healthcare facilities, and offers a BLOS Care membership service. The company is based at Seoul Startup Hub Seongsu, holds 21 registered patents, and has been recognized with venture certification, ESG awards, and selection as a Korean representative for WSA 2026. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio lead and enriched from the company's public website.

providers.name: GreenQ
providers.description: GreenQ is an Israeli smart waste-management technology company (founded 2015, Jerusalem) promoting the "Internet of Garbage" — turning ordinary garbage trucks into smart trucks. Its GreenTrack device installs on any collection vehicle to weigh incoming waste and track route, mileage, capacity, time and per-bin (single-can-level) pickup data without requiring sensors on the bins, using a patent-pending visual-recognition algorithm. A recommendations engine then suggests route-optimization and scheduling improvements, surfaced through the GreenQ dashboard of reports and analytics. Collected data can be integrated with a municipality's local-authority systems through a private integration API; the company publishes no public developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or specification. GreenQ was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global (also backed by URBAN-X) and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Ruedata
providers.description: Ruedata (RueData AI) is an AI predictive tire-management software platform for commercial fleet operators. It combines a smart digital inspection app, the TLGX precision tire-measurement device (tread depth to +/-1/32nd and pressure to +/-0.25 percent), and a centralized web platform to help fleets prevent tire blowouts, cut maintenance costs, extend tire lifecycle, and improve road safety. Its business-intelligence layer applies predictive analytics for tire wear and route optimization, and it integrates with major telematics providers such as Samsara, Geotab, Netfleet, and Traffilog plus ERP systems via direct API connections. Ruedata is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass it publishes a marketing and product site but no public developer API, API reference, SDKs, or developer portal.

providers.name: Flock
providers.description: Flock is a London-based commercial motor and fleet insurtech that provides usage-based, data-driven insurance for businesses operating vehicle fleets. Using real-time telematics and data science, Flock prices risk dynamically and rewards safer driving with lower premiums, delivering connected fleet insurance through a digital platform and partner integrations. The company is backed by Anthemis and other investors and operates primarily in the United Kingdom. This API Evangelist profile tracks Flock's public developer and company surface; as of this enrichment pass Flock publishes no public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification.

providers.name: Inviscid AI
providers.description: Inviscid AI is a San Francisco-based startup (Y Combinator W2026) building physics-informed AI for real-time cooling and airflow simulation of buildings and industrial facilities. Its platform combines computational fluid dynamics (CFD) with physics-informed neural networks to run thermal digital twins up to 1000x faster than traditional CFD, ingesting live data from building management systems, meters, and IoT sensors to autonomously recommend HVAC setpoints and optimize airflow. Target facilities include data centers, offices, hospitals, and cold storage, where the company claims 30%+ energy savings and sub-90-day ROI. As of mid-2026 Inviscid AI is a pre-product-launch company with no public developer portal, API, SDKs, or OpenAPI surface; this profile tracks it as an API Evangelist network lead pending an external API.

providers.name: Sense
providers.description: Sense is a Cambridge, Massachusetts energy-intelligence company that builds a residential energy monitor and machine-learning platform for real-time whole-home electricity disaggregation. The Sense Monitor installs in a home electrical panel, samples voltage and current at one million times per second, and uses signature-based machine-learning models to identify individual appliances and loads behind a single point of measurement. The Sense iOS, Android, and web apps surface device-level usage, always-on load, solar production, time-of-use cost, and goal tracking to homeowners. For utilities and grid operators, Sense embeds its disaggregation software into next-generation AMI 2.0 smart meters through partnerships with meter manufacturers such as Landis+Gyr, providing grid-edge visibility, fault detection, load-management, demand-response, and virtual-power-plant enablement. Sense also runs a partner program for smart-device integration with thermostats, EV chargers, heat pumps, and home-service providers. Sense has not released an official public developer API; community developers maintain reverse-engineered, unofficial clients in Python, Node.js, and Home Assistant against an undocumented and unsupported endpoint. Sense's revenue model is hardware sales of the consumer monitor and licensing of its disaggregation software to utilities and meter OEMs.

providers.name: Datost
providers.description: Datost Inc. is a New York applied research lab building hardware and intelligent systems that operate in your environment without demanding constant attention — "computers that come after the screen." Its first public product is ED1TH, a 25-gram pair of AI augmented-reality smart glasses with a 640x480 green Micro-LED in-lens display readable in direct sunlight, hot-swap battery cells, a companion steel smart ring for gesture control, and a privacy-first design with zero cameras and a single hardware-mutable microphone. ED1TH runs ED1TH-OS and handles email, calendar, turn-by-turn navigation, live translation, and meeting transcription in the wearer's field of view. Datost is backed by Y Combinator (Spring 2026) and OpenAI. As a consumer hardware and applied-research company, Datost does not currently publish a public web API, OpenAPI, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: GM OnStar
providers.description: GM OnStar is General Motors' connected vehicle services platform, originally launched in 1996 as an in-vehicle safety, security, and concierge service and since extended into a commercial data platform under OnStar Business Solutions. The OnStar Business Solutions API and Data Services product delivers near-real-time embedded telematics straight from properly equipped 2015-model-year-or-newer GM vehicles — Chevrolet, Buick, GMC, and Cadillac — without aftermarket hardware, exposing vehicle location, speed, ignition status, odometer, fuel level, EV state-of-charge and charging status, tire pressure, seatbelt status, diagnostic trouble codes, and driver-behavior events such as hard brake and hard acceleration. The product is packaged into tiered plans (commonly referenced as API Starter and API Pro) and is distributed primarily through OnStar's enterprise channel under the GM Envolve commercial brand, plus integrations with fleet management providers including Samsara, Geotab, Wheels, Verizon Connect, and other approved telematic service providers. There is no public self-serve developer portal or published OpenAPI specification — access is gated through GM/OnStar sales (developer.gm.com is a request-access endpoint) or via an authorized integration partner. Consumer-facing OnStar mobile features (remote start, remote lock, vehicle locate, in-vehicle Wi-Fi, Super Cruise telemetry) are delivered through GM's myChevrolet, myBuick, myGMC, and myCadillac apps and are not part of the published API surface.

providers.name: Hexing Electrical Co., Ltd.
providers.description: Hexing Electrical Co., Ltd. (海兴电力 / Hexing) is a Chinese energy-technology company focused on smart power distribution and utilization, new energy, smart water and gas, water treatment and clean water, and marine electrification. Beyond hardware, Hexing delivers integrated solutions and project delivery spanning metering devices, communication networks (RF, PLC, cellular, NB-IoT), MDC / MDM / AMI platforms, billing systems, distribution automation, energy storage (BESS), EV charging, water metering, seawater desalination and electric marine propulsion. The company reports 34 years of industry experience, operations across 110+ countries and 17 global manufacturing hubs. Surfaced as a portfolio company of qiming and profiled in the API Evangelist network; Hexing publishes no public developer/API surface today, so this profile captures corporate identity plus the AI knowledge file (llms.txt) the company publishes for AI search / RAG.

providers.name: Ion Mobility
providers.description: ION Mobility is a Singapore-headquartered technology and automotive company that designs and builds affordable, zero-emission smart electric motorcycles for riders across Southeast Asia, with its flagship M1-S model and a companion rider mobile app. The company combines advanced hardware and software with human-centred design, spanning electric two-wheelers and energy charging and storage solutions, with additional offices in Jakarta and Shenzhen and backing from investors including 500 Global. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company's public developer and identity surface; ION Mobility currently publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or OpenAPI specification, operating a consumer waitlist/test-ride site and an internal open-source tooling estate on GitHub.

providers.name: petkit
providers.description: PetKit is a consumer smart pet-technology company that designs and sells connected pet-care hardware — automated feeders, smart water fountains, self-cleaning litter boxes, cameras, and health-monitoring accessories — paired with the PetKit mobile app that controls the devices over the cloud. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of the venture firm qiming and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass, PetKit publishes no dedicated first-party developer portal or public API; petkit.com is operated as a Shopify storefront, so the only machine discoverable surface on the domain is Shopify's Customer Account OAuth/OIDC discovery documents. Third-party (community, reverse-engineered) integrations exist for the mobile-app backend but there is no officially documented API.

providers.name: Tri Pointe Homes
providers.description: Tri Pointe Homes (NYSE: TPH) is a US homebuilder headquartered in Orange County, California. Founded in 2009, it builds single-family and multifamily new homes across 13 states plus the District of Columbia under a unified Tri Pointe Homes brand that consolidated legacy regional brands including Pardee Homes, Maracay, Quadrant Homes, Winchester Homes, and Trendmaker Homes. The company also offers ancillary services through Tri Pointe Connect (mortgage), Tri Pointe Assurance (title and escrow), and Tri Pointe Advantage (insurance). Tri Pointe operates no public developer program, no documented API, and no GitHub presence; its digital surface is limited to a marketing site (tripointehomes.com), an investor portal, a blog, and a careers portal.

providers.name: Mauna Kea Semiconductors
providers.description: Mauna Kea Semiconductors (mk-semi.com) is a Silicon Valley-based fabless semiconductor company founded by industry veterans to develop what it describes as the world's lowest-power Ultra-Wideband (UWB) solution for high precision location and direction-finding applications. Its UWB chips, modules, and integrated System-on-Chip solutions target smartphones, wearables, IoT devices, and automotive use cases, combining digital and analog/mixed-signal design expertise. Headquartered in Cupertino, California, with engineering operations in Shanghai, Beijing, and Shenzhen, the company is led by CEO Dr. Yifeng Zhang and is backed by Qiming. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Qiming; it is a hardware/silicon vendor with no public API or developer surface at this time (documentation, blog, and careers pages are marked "Coming Soon").

providers.name: Misfit
providers.description: Misfit is a consumer wearables brand — fitness trackers and smartwatches such as the Misfit Shine, Flash, Ray and Vapor — founded in 2011 by Sonny Vu, John Sculley and Sridhar Iyengar and backed by Norwest Venture Partners, Khosla Ventures, Founders Fund, GGV Capital and Xiaomi before being acquired by Fossil Group in 2015. Misfit ran a developer program (the Misfit Cloud API, Device SDK and Scientific Library) at build.misfit.com with 30+ launch partners. Fossil discontinued the Misfit backend, Cloud API and companion app in spring 2023, so the hosted API and all misfit.com domains are now unreachable. The only surviving developer surface is the official Misfit-Developers GitHub organization and its unmaintained iOS SDKs on CocoaPods.

providers.name: I Flow
providers.description: iFlow Inc. is an energy and water solutions provider headquartered in Santa Ana, California, offering products and services for the sustainable use of vital resources including water metering and leak detection, wastewater management, gas measurement and control, thermal energy/BTU metering, and data connectivity solutions. No public developer APIs are documented at this time.

providers.name: Bouffalo Lab
providers.description: Bouffalo Lab (博流智能) is a fabless chip design company founded in 2016 and headquartered in Nanjing, China, focused on ultra-low-power AIoT (AI + IoT) and edge-computing system chips. Its product line centers on RISC-V based microcontrollers with integrated wireless connectivity — the BL602/BL604 (Wi-Fi 2.4G + BLE 5.0), BL702/BL704/BL706 (Zigbee 3.0 + BLE 5.0), BL606P (quad-mode dual-core Wi-Fi/BT/BLE/Zigbee), and the BL616/BL618 and BL808 families — combining wireless radios, audio/video processing, and on-device AI algorithms. The company ships the open-source BouffaloSDK (a merge of bl_mcu_sdk and bl_iot_sdk) under Apache 2.0 through its public GitHub organization, along with hardware abstraction drivers, Matter/Thread support, and NuttX RTOS ports. Bouffalo Lab is a hardware/firmware provider rather than a web-API provider; it exposes no public HTTP/REST developer API, so the enrichment pipeline captures its developer surface (GitHub SDK org) and domain security posture. It is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners.

providers.name: CTRL-labs *
providers.description: CTRL-labs was a neurotechnology company founded in 2015 in New York City (originally Cognescent) by Thomas Reardon, Patrick Kaifosh, and Tim Machado, building a non-invasive neural interface: a wrist-worn band that reads surface electromyography (sEMG) signals from motor neurons to decode intended hand and finger movements for human-computer interaction. Its developer hardware was the CTRL-kit, and it acquired the Myo armband patents from North. In fall 2019 CTRL-labs was acquired by Facebook and folded into Facebook (now Meta) Reality Labs, where the technology became the basis of Meta's neuromotor wristband for AR glasses (detailed in a July 2025 Nature paper). The company no longer operates as an independent entity and publishes no public API, SDK, or developer platform; this record is retained as an acquired-company lead.

providers.name: Cypress
providers.description: Cypress Semiconductor Corporation was a San Jose, California semiconductor company founded in 1982, and an early Mayfield venture investment. It designed and manufactured mixed-signal, embedded, and connectivity silicon — most notably the PSoC programmable system-on-chip microcontrollers, WICED Wi-Fi and Bluetooth wireless combos, USB controllers (EZ-USB), NOR flash and SRAM memory, and automotive Traveo microcontrollers — supported by the ModusToolbox and PSoC Creator developer tooling and the Cypress Developer Community. Infineon Technologies AG acquired Cypress in April 2020 for approximately 9.4 billion dollars; the business, its developer community, and its GitHub repositories have since been folded into Infineon. cypress.com now redirects to infineon.com and the developer resources live at community.infineon.com. Cypress shipped hardware SDKs and embedded toolchains rather than a public web/REST API, so there is no independent HTTP API surface to catalog for this entity — this profile documents it as a historical, acquired provider.

providers.name: eFishery
providers.description: eFishery is an Indonesian aquaculture technology ("fishtech") company founded in 2013 in Bandung by Gibran Huzaifah and Chrisna Aditya. Its platform combined an IoT smart auto-feeder (eFeeder) that dispenses feed to fish and shrimp ponds and streams pond telemetry to a smartphone app, with an integrated services layer: eFisheryKu / eFarm farm-management software, eFund (including the Kabayan "pay later" financing product) linking smallholder farmers to lenders, and eFresh / eMart marketplaces connecting farmers to feed suppliers and downstream buyers. The company raised a $90M Series C (2022) and a $200M Series D (2023) at a unicorn valuation, backed by investors including 500 Global, Aqua-Spark, SoftBank Vision Fund 2, Temasek, and Northstar. In late 2024 an audit alleged large-scale financial-statement fraud dating to 2018; both founders resigned and the company underwent multiple rounds of layoffs and restructuring through 2025. This record was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; eFishery exposes no public developer API or developer portal, and its primary efishery.com domain currently resolves to a parked/forwarding host.

providers.name: Metis Labs
providers.description: Metis Labs Limited is a London-based industrial AI company founded in 2017 by Alex Appelbe and Bashir Beikzadeh (an Entrepreneur First EF8 alumnus and a Speedinvest portfolio company). Its product, Kelvin Analytics, is an intelligent factory-optimization platform that applies reinforcement machine-learning to real-time monitoring and predictive analysis, helping process manufacturers in consumer-packaged chemicals, food and beverage, and construction materials cut production-line waste, raise product quality, and improve throughput. Metis Labs was acquired by Ascalia in September 2024. No public API, developer portal, or documentation surface is currently published.

providers.name: NVE Corporation
providers.description: NVE Corporation (nve.com, NASDAQ: NVEC) is a leader in the practical commercialization of spintronics, a nanotechnology that relies on electron spin rather than electron charge to acquire, store, and transmit information. NVE designs and manufactures spintronic GMR and TMR magnetic sensors (analog, angle/rotation, current, gear-tooth, and medical sensors), digital signal isolators (CAN, RS-422/485, PLC, battery-management, and power interfaces), and power-management ICs. Its developer surface is hardware-oriented: PDF datasheets, application notes, reference designs, magnetic-field calculators/web apps, a YouTube channel, and Arduino/embedded sample code on GitHub. NVE publishes no software/web API, OpenAPI or AsyncAPI specification, SDK, or developer API platform.

providers.name: View
providers.description: View, Inc. is a smart-glass and smart-building technology company founded in 2007 and headquartered in Milpitas, California, with manufacturing in Olive Branch, Mississippi. View makes View Dynamic Glass, electrochromic architectural windows whose tint adjusts automatically to sunlight, glare, and heat, alongside a connected Smart Building Platform in which each pane is individually IP-addressable and app-controllable and layered with sensors and services such as SmartProtect (an Azure IoT integration that alerts building managers when glass breaks). Backed by the SoftBank Vision Fund, View went public via SPAC in 2021 and filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2024, transitioning back to private ownership under its lenders. View exposes no public developer API surface; its GitHub organization (viewinc) mirrors third-party C/C++ and IoT firmware libraries used internally rather than first-party SDKs.

providers.name: Amodo
providers.description: Amodo was a European connected-insurance and telematics company founded in Zagreb, Croatia, that helped insurers and brokers build and distribute personalized usage-based insurance (UBI) products. Its Connected Insurance Platform combined a mobile telematics SDK, driver-behavior scoring, customer segmentation, and profiling analytics to power models ranging from try-before-you-buy to pay-as-you-drive and pay-per-mile. Over roughly nine years Amodo ran nearly 50 telematics programs worldwide with insurers including AIG, Porsche Versicherungs, Tower Insurance, and P&V, and was named one of the Financial Times' top five insurtech companies. Backed by Speedinvest, Amodo was acquired by Cambridge Mobile Telematics (CMT) in March 2023 and folded into CMT's European operations; the amodo.eu domain now redirects to CMT, and the company no longer maintains an independent public developer or API surface.

providers.name: Envision Energy
providers.description: Envision Energy is a Chinese green-technology company founded in 2007 by Lei Zhang and headquartered in Shanghai. It designs and manufactures smart wind turbines, operates one of the world's largest fleets of connected wind and solar assets, and builds net-zero industrial parks. Its business spans energy storage and batteries (through Envision AESC), green hydrogen and green ammonia, and the EnOS AIoT operating system delivered by its Envision Digital arm, which connects and manages energy and IoT devices at scale. Envision was surfaced as a portfolio company of Hongshan (formerly Sequoia China) and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; its public digital surface is a marketing site and the EnOS platform, which is documented on region-restricted hosts not reachable for spec discovery in this pass.

providers.name: Wi Charge
providers.description: Wi-Charge is a long-range wireless power company that transmits electricity over the air using infrared light, delivering safe, automatic charging to smart devices from thirty or more feet away without cables, batteries, or charging pads. The company sells consumer products such as the Encode Wireless Power Kit for smart locks and licenses its transmitter platform and compact receiver modules to OEMs building smart-home, commercial, IoT, retail, and consumer-electronics devices. Wi-Charge is venture-backed, including by Lightspeed Venture Partners. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; as of this pass Wi-Charge publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal — it is a hardware and OEM-licensing business rather than an API-first provider.

providers.name: Aethero
providers.description: Aethero designs and manufactures radiation-hardened, space-rated edge computing systems and AI/ML software for satellites, space stations, and orbital data centers, enabling autonomous on-orbit processing of imagery and sensor data rather than downlinking raw feeds. Its NVIDIA Jetson Orin/Thor-based NxN-ECM and NxA-ECM edge computing modules, Titan and Phobos platforms, the Aether fleet-management software framework, and the AMATDT model annotation/training/deployment tool let spacecraft run AI inference in orbit. Founded in 2023 and headquartered in San Francisco, Aethero raised an $8.4M seed round led by Kindred Ventures in June 2025. Aethero exposes no public web API today; this profile captures the company's identity and its live domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: AI-Prime (Paidao Intelligence)
providers.description: AI-Prime (Paidao Intelligence / 湃道智能) is a Shanghai-based industrial-safety AI company founded in 2017 that builds computer-vision, deep-learning, and knowledge-graph platforms for high-hazard industries. Its full-stack products span an AI industrial-safety monitoring cloud platform, 40+ safety-scenario models (PPE detection, unsafe behavior, equipment leaks, fire/smoke, work-process compliance), a self-learning AI model-development platform, and Prime-Edge smart hardware (edge-computing boxes, inspection robots, AR work mirrors, and edge cameras) serving the chemical, steel, coal, oil & gas, energy, and mining sectors. AI-Prime is a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners. It is an enterprise B2B provider with no public developer API program; this profile captures its identity and web presence.

providers.name: Arcstone
providers.description: Arcstone is a Singapore-based digital manufacturing technology company (founded 2013) that helps enterprises digitalize and gain real-time transparency across their shop floors and supply chains. Its product family spans arc.essentials (a lightweight Manufacturing Execution System for SMEs), arc.ops (a modular, next-generation MES for large enterprises), arc.net (multi-tier supply chain visibility), arc.studio (a low-code enterprise app and integration platform), arc.green (sustainability tracking), and arc.ai (an AI control tower for managed AI workforce deployment). Arcstone serves precision engineering, FMCG, mining, semiconductor, plastics, and biomedical manufacturers, and was named a Gartner Cool Vendor in Manufacturing Operations in 2022. The company is backed by 500 Global. No public API, developer portal, or SDKs are published at this time; this profile carries the identity and infrastructure signals harvested by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Aspinity
providers.description: Aspinity is a Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania semiconductor company that develops analog machine learning (AnalogML) technology combining ultra-low-power analog signal processing with machine learning for always-on, battery-operated edge AI event detection and classification. Its analogML processors the AML100 and next-generation AML200 deliver TOPS-level inference in a microwatt power footprint, targeting automotive vehicle-security monitoring, smart-home sensing such as glass-break and water-leak detection, and IoT applications including voice and keyword detection and vibration monitoring. Aspinity is a hardware and semiconductor provider and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile tracks its public web and security posture in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Bellabeat
providers.description: Bellabeat is a femtech and women's wellness technology company founded in 2014 by Urska Srsen and Sandro Mur, headquartered in San Francisco, California. It designs health-tracking wearables and connected devices aimed at women, including the Leaf and Ivy wellness jewelry trackers, the Time hybrid smartwatch, and the Spring smart water bottle, paired with the Bellabeat mobile app that tracks activity, sleep, stress, meditation, menstrual cycle, and overall wellness. Bellabeat operates as a direct-to-consumer wellness brand; it does not currently publish a public developer API, so this profile captures company identity and network provenance rather than API artifacts. Added to the API Evangelist network as a Y Combinator portfolio lead and enriched here.

providers.name: Cardiogram
providers.description: Cardiogram is a digital-health company whose consumer app analyzes heart-rate and activity data from wearables such as the Apple Watch, Wear OS, Garmin, and Fitbit to help people understand their cardiovascular health. Its DeepHeart deep-neural-network technology was developed to screen heart-rate patterns for signs of conditions including atrial fibrillation, sleep apnea, diabetes, and hypertension, work studied in collaboration with academic health researchers. The company is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a venture-portfolio lead; as of this pass Cardiogram exposes no public developer or API surface and its primary website (cardiogram.com) does not complete an HTTPS/TLS handshake.

providers.name: Colony Capital (DigitalBridge Group)
providers.description: Colony Capital was a diversified real estate and hospitality investment firm founded by Tom Barrack in 1991. In June 2021 the company rebranded as DigitalBridge Group, Inc. (NYSE: DBRG) — completing a multi-year pivot from traditional real estate to pure-play digital infrastructure investing. The Boca Raton, FL-based alternative asset manager now operates exclusively across five digital infrastructure categories: data centers, macro cell towers, fiber networks, small cells, and edge infrastructure. DigitalBridge manages approximately $119B in assets across 45+ portfolio companies including Vantage Data Centers, DataBank, Switch, Vertical Bridge, Zayo Group, GD Towers, Boingo Wireless, AtlasEdge, Scala Data Centers, Yondr Group, and ExteNet Systems. In December 2025 SoftBank Group announced a definitive agreement to acquire DigitalBridge for approximately $4 billion, with the deal expected to close in the second half of 2026. DigitalBridge itself publishes no developer API, SDK, or public OpenAPI surface — it is a holding company whose programmable surface lives inside its individual portfolio companies (e.g., Zayo, DataBank, Switch), each of which is profiled separately in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Fox-Tech
providers.description: FOX-TECH CO. is a New Taipei City, Taiwan IoT company (founded 2016, backed by 500 Global and SparkLabs Taipei) that digitally transforms farming, logistics, cold-chain, and manufacturing operations. Its TempHawk platform pairs wireless temperature, humidity, CO2, light-intensity and soil-EC sensors over Sigfox LPWAN with web and mobile apps and cloud data analytics, helping the perishable-goods value chain monitor conditions, manage risk, and meet policy compliance. Recognized on the Forward Fooding FoodTech 500. No public API, developer portal, or SDK is currently published.

providers.name: Illume Labs
providers.description: Illume Labs is a Y Combinator (Summer 2026) startup building a 24/7 AI personal health and longevity companion. Its platform is designed to connect a user's wearables, blood panels, and genomic data, then text them personalized, actionable insights — detecting patterns across data sources, answering health questions conversationally, and offering an interactive surface for deeper exploration of longevity signals. As of mid-2026 the company is pre-launch and operates a single marketing landing page ("A new lens on longevity") on Vercel with no public API, developer portal, SDK, or documentation surface yet published. This profile remains a network lead pending a public developer surface to enrich.

providers.name: Livongo
providers.description: Livongo Health is a digital chronic-condition management platform for diabetes, hypertension, weight, and prehypertension prevention, pairing connected devices (blood-glucose meters, blood-pressure cuffs, connected scales) with a mobile app, real-time monitoring, and certified health coaching delivered at no cost through employers and health plans. Founded in 2008 and taken public in 2019, Livongo was acquired by Teladoc Health in 2020; the standalone www.livongo.com site now 301-redirects to teladochealth.com/livongo, where Livongo operates as a consumer-facing product line. It is a patient/member health product, not a developer platform: no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or API documentation surface exists. Backed by Kleiner Perkins, Sapphire Ventures, and Threshold Ventures.

providers.name: Mantis
providers.description: Mantis (Mantis Biotech) builds predictive digital twins of individual people, aggregating personal data streams — wearables, digital activity, and clinical records — into high-fidelity models by combining large language models with physics-based simulation. The company positions itself as a neutral intermediary for personal predictive models — an "OAuth for identity" or "Plaid for banking" layer — letting individuals grant scoped, revocable access to their twin to healthcare providers and third-party builders. Applications include pre-symptomatic infection detection, cognitive baseline monitoring, heart-failure decompensation forecasting, medication-adherence prediction, post-operative recovery trajectories, psychiatric relapse early warning, and running trials on twins. Mantis is a Y Combinator (Winter 2026) company; as of this profile it publishes a marketing site and manifesto but no public API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: OMsignal
providers.description: OMsignal was a Montreal-based biometric smart-apparel startup, backed by Bessemer Venture Partners, that built compression shirts and the OMbra sports bra with embedded textile sensors streaming heart-rate, breathing, and activity data to a companion mobile app. The brand no longer operates independently: the omsignal.com domain now 301-redirects to hexoskin.com (Carre Technologies / Hexoskin), the biometric smart-clothing company that absorbed the product line. As of this enrichment pass OMsignal publishes no independent developer portal, API, or documentation of its own, and omsignal.com itself serves no API artifacts or well-known metadata.

providers.name: Petcube
providers.description: Petcube is a pet-technology company (a Y Combinator alum) that makes interactive Wi-Fi pet cameras and a companion mobile app for remote pet care. Its consumer hardware line includes the Petcube Cam, Bites treat-dispensing camera, and Play laser camera, offering HD video, night vision, two-way audio, motion and sound alerts, and app-controlled treat tossing and play. Petcube also sells the Care subscription (cloud video history, extended alerts) and Online Vet / Emergency Fund telehealth services. As of this enrichment pass Petcube exposes no public developer API, developer portal, or documented integration surface — the primary interface is the consumer iOS/Android app tied to its private cloud backend. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company record.

providers.name: Reach Labs
providers.description: Reach Labs (operating as Reach Power Inc.) is a wireless power transmission company that delivers electrical energy through the air without physical connections, describing its mission as "doing for power what Wi-Fi did for data." Its patented approach combines energy-transmission hardware, a custom delivery algorithm, and adaptive software controls to beam power to devices across varying distances and conditions. The company targets three primary sectors: defense and intelligence (powering sensors, autonomous vehicles, and drones in remote environments), manufacturing and logistics (energizing robotics and IoT devices in industrial settings), and public safety (enabling continuous drone operations for first responders). Reach was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCVC and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or machine-readable metadata surface.

providers.name: Theranica
providers.description: Theranica Bio-Electronics is a digital therapeutics company developing prescription-grade wearable neuromodulation devices for prevalent neurological pain conditions. Its flagship product, Nerivio, is an FDA-authorized wireless Remote Electrical Neuromodulation (REM) device worn on the upper arm for the acute and preventive treatment of migraine, with or without aura, in patients ages 12 and up. Nerivio is controlled by a companion iOS and Android smartphone app that lets patients start treatments, adjust stimulation intensity, monitor session duration, and keep a shareable migraine diary. Theranica is a venture-backed medical device company; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Lightspeed Venture Partners and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: 6thSense
providers.description: 6thSense is a physical-AI hardware company building the touch layer for dexterous robots. It designs and manufactures wearable tactile-sensing data gloves that capture how human hands interact with the world — pressure, contact, grip, and 3D hand pose — alongside custom tactile skin molded to robot hands. Its capture stack synchronizes eight aligned modalities (tactile and pressure proxies, egocentric video, depth/RGB-D, hand pose, motion and IMU dynamics, wrist and scene cameras, dense labels and commentary, and success/failure outcomes) into model-ready demonstration datasets used to train the next generation of dexterous, manipulation-capable robots. Founded in 2026 in San Francisco and backed by Y Combinator (S26).

providers.name: airquality
providers.description: AirQuality (爱优特) is a Shanghai-based manufacturer of high-efficiency electrostatic air purification and disinfection products, including central air filtration systems, commercial kitchen exhaust (hood) cleaners, odor-elimination units, and smart air-quality detection systems for schools, hospitals, offices, shopping malls, and hotels. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. It is a hardware/manufacturing business that publishes a consumer website and online shop but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time, so most enrichment artifacts are not applicable.

providers.name: American Aerospace Advisors
providers.description: American Aerospace Technologies, Inc., doing business as American Aerospace Advisors, is a defense and critical-infrastructure monitoring company based in Conshohocken, Pennsylvania. It provides end-to-end airborne intelligence systems that combine unmanned aircraft systems (UAS), airborne sensors, analytics, and communications to deliver near-real-time data through a cloud-based intelligence gateway. Its flagship AiRanger medium-altitude long-endurance unmanned aircraft and InstiMaps sensor technology support pipeline and linear-asset patrol, beyond-visual-line-of-sight (BVLOS) flight services, sensor integration, and aviation policy consulting. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs.

providers.name: Apigy
providers.description: Apigy, Inc. is the company behind Lockitron, an early keyless smart-lock startup that let people lock, unlock, and share access to their doors from a smartphone. Backed by 500 Startups (now 500 Global) and known for a large 2012 crowdfunding campaign, Apigy built connected door-lock hardware and companion mobile apps before the Lockitron product line was wound down. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; its public website (lockitron.com) is currently unreachable and no active developer or API surface could be located.

providers.name: AquaShield
providers.description: AquaShield is a Y Combinator-backed (Spring 2026 / P26 batch) startup building AI-driven water leak detection for buildings and large real estate portfolios. Non-invasive sensors clamp onto existing pipes in minutes with no pipe cutting, retrofits, or downtime; the platform learns each building's normal water-flow patterns and flags anomalies in real time before they escalate into costly damage. Water damage is the largest preventable loss in real estate — more than fire and theft combined. Founded by former MIT and Harvard/EPFL robotics researchers Paul Beckers (CEO) and Marguerite Benoist (CTO), the company is based in San Francisco and works with some of the largest residential portfolios in the world. This profile was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; AquaShield currently publishes a marketing site only and does not yet expose a public API or developer program.

providers.name: Arilinc
providers.description: Aril Inc. (Arilinc) is a fabless semiconductor company in Los Gatos, California designing efficient AI processors and memory technology for edge inference. Its two core products are the Aril Standard Cell Memory, a patented on-chip memory offering roughly 40% lower active power and 3.6x smaller area, and a scalable RISC-V-based AI Processor Engine delivering hundreds of TOPS of inference per block with integrated vector and matrix engines. The company targets robotics, industrial automation, drones, defense and aerospace, autonomous vehicles, and edge vision systems where power efficiency is critical. Founded by a team of engineers who have collectively shipped 20M+ processors and worked on silicon for Cisco, Intel, AMD, and Google. Arilinc sells custom silicon and IP to hardware makers rather than a public developer API; it publishes no API, SDK, developer portal, or programmatic surface at this time.

providers.name: Automatic Labs
providers.description: Automatic Labs was a connected-car company (the Automatic OBD-II adapter and companion app plus a developer platform / REST API for trip, vehicle, and driving-behavior data), founded circa 2011 and backed by a16z. It was acquired by SiriusXM in 2017 and wound down: the service and its developer API were discontinued around May 2020. As of this enrichment pass the automatic.com domain (and its api./developer. subdomains) 301-redirects to automattic.com, the unrelated WordPress company, so no live API, documentation, or developer surface remains to harvest. This profile is retained as a defunct a16z portfolio lead.

providers.name: Avegant
providers.description: Avegant is an augmented reality display technology company that develops light engine technology bringing high-performance visuals to lightweight AR glasses designed for everyday wear. Its flagship product, the AG-30L2 LED light engine, is described as the world's smallest LED light engine for augmented reality. Avegant is a venture-backed hardware company (a portfolio company of 500 Global) focused on the optical and display components that power the next generation of AR eyewear rather than on a public developer platform. No public API, SDK, or developer documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Axiometrix Solutions
providers.description: Axiometrix Solutions is a global test and measurement company serving technology-intensive industries through three specialist brands - GRAS Sound & Vibration (acoustic and vibration sensors for challenging environments), imc Test & Measurement (modular data acquisition, signal conditioning, and shock/vibration solutions), and Audio Precision (audio and RF analyzers for quality validation). Its integrated portfolio of sensors, data acquisition systems, control software, analysis software, and test fixtures supports advanced research, R&D, and production/manufacturing test across aerospace, defense, automotive, consumer electronics, audiology and medical technology, communications, semiconductor, and environmental monitoring markets. Backed by Battery Ventures. No public web API or developer program has been identified for this provider.

providers.name: Axon
providers.description: Axon is an early-stage artificial intelligence company building real-time predictive intelligence on a brain-inspired architecture. Its approach centers on small, efficient "world models" that learn continuously on-device rather than depending on large models or the cloud, giving an edge-first design lower latency and lower cost. The initial focus is high-frequency trading and capital markets, where real-time prediction is decisive, with future applications targeted at wearables, edge devices, and robotics. Axon is backed by Northzone, Concept Ventures, a16z Speedrun, and EWOR. As of this profile the company is pre-product with no public developer API, documentation, SDKs, or developer portal; this repository tracks it in the API Evangelist network for enrichment as its developer surface emerges.

providers.name: BeBop Sensors
providers.description: BeBop Sensors was a Berkeley, California smart-fabric sensor company founded in 2014 that designed and manufactured flexible, fabric-based pressure and touch sensors for OEMs across robotics, medical devices, automotive interiors, and virtual reality. Its best known products were haptic VR gloves and "intelligent sensing technology" surfaces that turned ordinary materials into multi-touch, pressure-sensitive inputs. The company raised a $10M+ Series A led by Bullpen Capital and shipped custom sensor hardware paired with bespoke firmware and integration software for enterprise customers. BeBop sold engineered hardware under contract rather than a self-serve developer product, and never published a public API, developer portal, or SDK. The company is no longer operating and its former domain has been repurposed by an unrelated third party.

providers.name: Bumblebee Spaces
providers.description: Bumblebee Spaces is a San Francisco smart-home robotics company that builds app-controlled motorized storage systems for compact urban living. Its ceiling-mounted robotic units lift beds, closets, and storage bins up and out of the way, reclaiming floor space in small apartments, while a built-in camera and mobile app track and retrieve stored belongings on demand. The company sells and installs hardware plus a companion consumer mobile application; it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal. Backed by Bloomberg Beta and Canaan Partners, the profile is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead.

providers.name: Chickin
providers.description: Chickin is an Indonesian poultry-technology company operating a full-stack, integrated ecosystem for chicken farmers across Indonesia. It combines closed-house smart-farming hardware (IoT climate and environmental controllers), day-old-chick and feed supply, farmer financing, and guaranteed offtake and distribution of live birds, aiming to modernize and de-risk small and mid-scale poultry farming. Backed by 500 Global, Chickin runs its operations through a mobile and web application at chickin.id. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable API artifacts; this profile records its public web presence and domain-security posture and remains a lead for further enrichment should a developer surface be published.

providers.name: Comfy *
providers.description: Comfy (comfyapp.com) was a workplace-experience platform built by Building Robotics Inc. that let employees control lighting, temperature, room booking and office navigation from a mobile app, surfaced here as a GV (Google Ventures) portfolio lead. During enrichment the domain comfyapp.com was found to permanently 301-redirect to Enlighted Inc. / Building Robotics Inc., a Siemens Company, where the product has been rebranded as Siemens Building X space and workplace management; the Enlighted/Comfy site further states operations are ramping down. No independent public API, OpenAPI, SDK, developer portal, well-known discovery surface, or security.txt was found for Comfy or its successor as of this pass. This profile is retained as an acquired/defunct stub with domain-security probe data.

providers.name: Congruent
providers.description: Congruent builds AI-native radar hardware and simulation tooling for self-driving cars and end-to-end autonomy. The company pairs a radar architecture that exposes raw sensor data with a world-model-based generative simulator, producing both real and synthetic raw radar returns to train autonomy stacks. Radar is the only depth sensor cheap enough to scale to every vehicle while still working in rain, fog, snow, and dust, where camera and lidar systems degrade. Congruent is an early-stage Y Combinator (W26) company founded in 2025 by Clement Barthes and Evan Scope Crafts, based in the San Francisco Bay Area. It was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; as of this profile the company operates a single marketing website and publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or specification.

providers.name: Crossbar
providers.description: Crossbar, Inc. is a Santa Clara semiconductor company founded in 2010 that develops resistive random-access memory (ReRAM), a non-volatile memory built on RRAM patents licensed from the University of Michigan. Its CMOS-compatible ReRAM targets faster write performance, lower power consumption, and higher endurance than NAND flash at roughly half the die size, and is offered as embedded and standalone memory IP to OEMs and system-on-chip developers across consumer, mobile, enterprise, industrial, and IoT markets. Crossbar is a hardtech portfolio company backed by Kleiner Perkins. As a silicon-IP provider it exposes no public developer API surface; this profile carries company identity and domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Curtiss-Wright
providers.description: Curtiss-Wright is a global integrated business that provides highly engineered products, solutions, and services mainly to the aerospace, defense, commercial power, process, and general industrial markets. Its product portfolio spans rugged embedded computing, mission-critical avionics, electronic packaging, naval propulsion, reactor coolant pumps for nuclear power, surface treatment services, industrial valves, sensors, data acquisition systems, telemetry ground stations, emergency arresting systems for military aircraft, and electronic systems for naval shipbuilding programs. The company traces its lineage to the aviation pioneers Glenn Curtiss and the Wright brothers and today operates across the Defense Electronics, Naval & Power, and Aerospace & Industrial segments.

providers.name: Dimeq
providers.description: Dimeq is a Norwegian maritime safety technology company working to prevent loss of life at sea and set new health, safety and environmental (HSE) standards for the maritime sector. Its Eye-D System is an IoT-based digital ecosystem that delivers real-time positioning of crew and passengers to one-meter accuracy during emergencies, man-overboard detection using environmental sensors, automatic mustering that registers people in seconds, and statistical analysis for accident documentation and prevention, while keeping data anonymous and GDPR-compliant outside of emergencies. The D-Router gateway supports Wi-Fi, Ethernet, PLC, fiber optics, UWB, Bluetooth, LoRa, ZigBee and MATTER connectivity.
