This is a hardware/IoT product company with no public developer portal, API, SDK or documentation surface at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Distributedspectrum
providers.description: Distributed Spectrum, self-described as "The World's First AI Signals Expert," builds edge-AI radio-frequency sensing technology that detects and identifies RF signals to autonomously map threats without expensive hardware or trained operators. Its sensors process data locally to deliver real-time alerts on threat types such as tactical radios, GPS jammers, and drones, and can be deployed anywhere using commercial components to form distributed detection networks. The company is headquartered at 99 Madison Ave, New York, NY, raised a $25M Series A, and is a Felicis portfolio company. No public API or developer program is published at this time; this profile carries the identity and domain-security posture surfaced by the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Dropcam
providers.description: Dropcam is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of accel, bessemer-venture-partners, kleiner-perkins, menlo-ventures and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: consumer. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: EchoStar
providers.description: EchoStar Corporation (Nasdaq: SATS) is a global, fully integrated communications and content delivery leader and provider of technology, spectrum, and connectivity. Through its DISH, Boost Mobile, Hughes, and EchoStar Mobile brands, EchoStar delivers satellite communications, wireless services, and IoT connectivity to consumers, enterprises, governments, and aviation customers worldwide.

providers.name: eigencomm
providers.description: Shanghai Eigencomm Technology Co., Ltd. is a fabless semiconductor company founded in 2017 and headquartered in the Zhangjiang district of Shanghai, China, dedicated to the research, design, and sale of cellular Internet of Things (IoT) communication chipsets and their supporting software. Eigencomm has mass-produced NB-IoT and Cat.1bis chip series that power smart meters, smart security, mobile payment, shared devices, asset trackers, charging piles, wearables, smart firefighting, and smart home appliances, and is developing 5G silicon. The company is backed by SoftBank Vision Fund II, Qiming Venture Partners, and others, having raised roughly USD 171M across multiple rounds. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub; it publishes no public web API, developer portal, or OpenAPI at this time.

providers.name: Energy Micro
providers.description: Energy Micro was a Norwegian fabless semiconductor company, founded in 2007 and headquartered in Oslo, best known for its EFM32 "Gecko" family of energy-friendly 32-bit ARM Cortex-M microcontrollers and the EFR radio products targeting low-power embedded and IoT applications. The company was acquired by Silicon Labs in 2013 and fully absorbed into that company's product lines; its former energymicro.com domain now redirects to silabs.com. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Northzone and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub. Enrichment found no independent, first-party API, developer portal, OpenAPI, SDK, or MCP surface for Energy Micro as a standalone entity — the developer tooling for its EFM32 line lives under Silicon Labs today.

providers.name: EraDrive
providers.description: EraDrive is a space technology company building compact, AI-powered self-driving modules that give spacecraft onboard autonomy — vision-based navigation, control, collision avoidance, and situational awareness computed at the edge. A Stanford Space Rendezvous Laboratory (SLAB) spinoff founded by Sumant Sharma (CEO), Justin Kruger (CTO), and Prof. Simone D'Amico (CSO), EraDrive integrates flight-proven autonomy software with existing satellite infrastructure for space traffic management, on-orbit servicing and logistics, and advanced remote sensing across commercial and defense missions. The company closed an oversubscribed $5.3M seed round in December 2025, co-led by Haystack Ventures with participation from Point Nine, Harpoon Ventures, Brave Capital, 2100 VC, and Entropy Industrial Capital. As an early-stage hardware/software company, EraDrive currently publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Fleetsmith
providers.description: Fleetsmith was a San Francisco-based startup (founded 2016) that provided cloud-based Apple device management (MDM) for IT teams — automated zero-touch setup, patching, app deployment, and security enforcement across Macs, iPhones, iPads, and Apple TVs. Backed by Menlo Ventures and others, Fleetsmith was acquired by Apple in June 2020; Apple subsequently discontinued the standalone product and folded its capabilities into Apple Business Essentials. The company no longer operates an independent developer program or public API, and fleetsmith.com now redirects to Apple Business Essentials. This profile is retained for network history.

providers.name: FogHorn Systems (Johnson Controls)
providers.description: FogHorn Systems was a Sunnyvale, California developer of edge AI and machine learning software for the industrial and commercial Internet of Things (IIoT). Its Lightning Edge AI platform and Lightning EdgeML brought real-time streaming analytics and ML inference to constrained on-premises edge hardware for predictive maintenance, machine optimization, and operational intelligence use cases. Johnson Controls acquired FogHorn in January 2022 and folded its team and technology into the OpenBlue suite of smart, autonomous building solutions, with the former Sunnyvale headquarters operating as a Johnson Controls "AI Hub." FogHorn no longer operates as a standalone brand and publishes no independent public developer surface — no developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or GitHub organization resolve as of this enrichment pass; the former foghorn.io/foghorn.ai domains are parked. This profile is retained as a network company record with no public API artifacts to harvest.

providers.name: Fossil Group
providers.description: Fossil Group is a global designer, marketer, and distributor of consumer fashion accessories including watches, jewelry, handbags, small leather goods, belts, and sunglasses sold under owned and licensed brands such as Fossil, Skagen, Michele, Relic, Misfit, and licensed lines for Michael Kors, Diesel, Emporio Armani, Tory Burch, and others.

providers.name: Freescale Semiconductor
providers.description: Freescale Semiconductor, Inc. was an American semiconductor manufacturer headquartered in Austin, Texas, created in 2004 from the spin-off of Motorola's Semiconductor Products Sector. Freescale designed and produced embedded processing hardware — microcontrollers (Kinetis, S08), i.MX applications processors, ColdFire and QorIQ/PowerPC communications processors, digital signal processors, RF, analog, and sensor products — for the automotive, networking, industrial, and consumer markets. In December 2015 Freescale merged with NXP Semiconductors in a roughly $11.8B deal and ceased to exist as an independent company; its freescale.com domain now redirects to nxp.com. Freescale was a hardware/silicon company, not a web-API provider: it published no public REST/HTTP API, developer portal, or OpenAPI, so there is no live API surface for the enrichment pipeline to harvest.

providers.name: Geekatoo
providers.description: Geekatoo was a Walnut Creek, California on-demand, in-home technology support marketplace that connected consumers to a nationwide network of vetted local technicians for computer repair, network troubleshooting, TV mounting, and home-theater/smart-home installation using a fixed-price and competitive-bid model positioned as an alternative to retail services like Geek Squad. Founded in 2013, it went through the 500 Startups accelerator (sixth batch) and raised roughly $2.2M from backers including 500 Startups, CRCM Venture Capital, DeNA, MicroVentures, and Wefunder. In May 2016 Geekatoo merged with Los Angeles-based HelloTech to form one of the largest on-demand in-home tech support networks in the US; the standalone Geekatoo brand and website (geekatoo.com) are no longer operational. This API Evangelist profile is a 500 Global portfolio lead retained for historical record; the enrichment pipeline found no live developer surface, API, or documentation to harvest.

providers.name: General Instinct
providers.description: General Instinct is a San Francisco company (Y Combinator Spring 2026) building the deployment layer for physical AI. Founded in 2026 by Bill Jiao and Guanming Wang, it distills, quantizes, and deploys large frontier AI models onto constrained edge hardware so robotics, drone, and physical-AI teams can run low-latency models fully offline on devices like NVIDIA Jetson, mobile NPUs, ARM CPUs, the Apple Neural Engine, and Snapdragon. Its first product, Instinct Edge, takes a model, a target device, and a latency budget and returns an offline runtime that hits the budget on-device with no cloud calls, handling model compression, custom kernel optimization (CUDA, Metal, ARM NEON), and the data-to-serving pipeline. It was surfaced as a Y Combinator portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; enrichment searched the public web and found a marketing landing page but no developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, SDKs, or public API surface, so no API artifacts could be harvested. This profile captures the company identity plus the security posture of its public web surface, and remains an identity-only lead pending a discoverable API.

providers.name: General Radar
providers.description: General Radar Corp. (GenRad) is a Belmont, California hardtech company founded in 2016 that designs and manufactures fully solid-state, high-resolution active electronically scanned array (AESA) phased-array radar systems built largely on commercial off-the-shelf hardware. Its products include the C-band GenRad GFC multi-mission AESA radar with a GaN front-end and digital beam-forming, and the Mark-IV 76-81GHz millimeter-wave 3D imaging radar producing LIDAR-like point clouds. The company serves aerospace and defense (U.S. Air Force, Navy, NORAD), counter-drone, airfield foreign-object-debris (FOD) detection, autonomy, wind energy, and weather markets, and has raised over $35M from investors including Kleiner Perkins and Octave Ventures. General Radar publishes no public API, developer portal, SDK, or machine-readable interface; this profile is maintained for API Evangelist network completeness.

providers.name: GYENNO
providers.description: GYENNO is a medical technology company that designs assistive devices and digital-health tools for people living with Parkinson's disease and other movement disorders. Its consumer product line includes the GYENNO Bravo anti-tremor eating utensil (a stabilizing, weighted spoon/fork that counteracts hand tremor) and the GYENNO Skywalk portable freezing-of-gait mobility aid that projects a visual laser cue to help users resume walking, alongside a range of adaptive and weighted utensils and daily-living aids. GYENNO was surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a consumer marketing site only and exposes no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Humane
providers.description: Humane was a consumer AI hardware startup, founded by former Apple engineers, best known for the AI Pin — a screenless, wearable AI-powered device — and its companion Cosmos operating system and Humane.Center cloud service. The company was acquired by HP in early 2025, the AI Pin was discontinued, and its cloud services and humane.com domain were taken offline. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Kindred Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass the company has no reachable web, developer, or API surface.

providers.name: IControl Networks
providers.description: IControl Networks was a smart-home and home-security platform company (OpenHome / Connect, Piper) backed by Kleiner Perkins. It was acquired by Comcast in 2017 (the platform underpinned Xfinity Home) with its residential SaaS business sold to Alarm.com; it no longer operates as an independent entity. Enrichment probe (2026-07-20): the icontrol.com domain no longer serves a website and is now delegated to Comcast nameservers (dns10x.comcast.net); icontrolnetworks.com, developer.icontrol.com, and api.icontrol.com do not resolve. No live developer portal, documentation, or public API surface exists to harvest. Sector: hardtech / IoT.

providers.name: Infiot
providers.description: Infiot was a secure access service edge (SASE) and intelligent edge networking startup that combined SD-WAN, zero trust network access (ZTNA), security service edge, and cloud-delivered edge intelligence into a single-vendor, AI-driven service for connecting branch, remote, and IoT sites. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners, the company was acquired by Netskope in August 2022 and its technology was folded into Netskope's Borderless SD-WAN and Converged Access product line. Infiot no longer operates an independent brand, developer portal, API reference, or public API host; the former infiot.com domain now 301-redirects to Netskope's Converged Access product page, so there is no standalone API surface to enrich. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network as a Lightspeed portfolio lead with its acquisition status recorded.

providers.name: Instart Logic
providers.description: Instart Logic was a web application performance and security company founded in 2010 (originally as Zettata) and headquartered in Palo Alto, California. It pioneered an endpoint-integrated cloud delivery architecture that paired a cloud service with a client-side JavaScript engine (the Nanovisor) running in the browser to accelerate web and mobile web applications, optimize and stream images (SmartVision), and defend applications with bot management and a web application firewall. Backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Kleiner Perkins, Tenaya Capital, Greylock, Sutter Hill Ventures and others across roughly $140M+ in venture funding, the company's technology assets were acquired by Akamai Technologies in early 2020, after which the business wound down. No live developer or API surface remains: the instartlogic.com domain resolves to no website host and is served by Akamai nameservers.

providers.name: IQI Inc (Beijing AIQI Technology)
providers.description: IQI Inc, operating as Beijing AIQI Technology Co., Ltd. (北京爱其科技有限公司), is a mobile-internet company founded in April 2013 that develops smart hardware and robotics products under a "Create more & More fun" philosophy. It is best known for its ONEBOT building-block robots and construction sets — including the Mi Tu (米兔) block robots in the Xiaomi ecosystem and heritage-architecture sets such as the Millennium Mortise-and-Tenon (千年榫), Qinian Hall (祈年殿) and Forbidden City Corner Tower kits. The company sells through its own store, Tmall (ONEBOT flagship) and JD.com. It is a consumer smart-hardware/toy brand; as of this profile it publishes no public developer platform, API, SDK or documentation surface.

providers.name: Iridium
providers.description: Iridium Communications Inc. (NASDAQ: IRDM) is a McLean, Virginia satellite communications company operating a constellation of 66 cross-linked Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites that deliver truly global L-band voice, data, IoT, and positioning/navigation/timing (PNT) services across every region of the Earth, including the polar oceans. Iridium sells satellite phones (Iridium Extreme), satellite messengers, satellite IoT modules and modems (Iridium 9602/9603, Iridium Certus 9770/9810/9704, Iridium Edge, Iridium Edge Pro, Iridium Edge Solar), Short Burst Data (SBD) messaging, broadband Certus terminals, and next-generation Iridium NTN Direct 5G Non-Terrestrial Network services built on 3GPP NB-IoT for direct-to-device smartphone and IoT connectivity. Iridium CloudConnect — co-developed with Amazon Web Services — pipes satellite IoT data as JSON into customer-owned Amazon SQS queues inside their own AWS VPC over a dedicated private Iridium-AWS interconnect, making Iridium the first global cloud-native satellite IoT backhaul. The company serves aviation, maritime, government/defense, land-mobile, autonomous systems, and IoT markets through a partner ecosystem of more than 500 service providers, value-added resellers, and hardware OEMs, and in May 2026 announced a planned acquisition of Aireon, operator of the world's only space-based air traffic surveillance network. Iridium's business model is airtime/subscription revenue plus hardware module licensing and engineering services; there is no public, self-service developer API or OpenAPI — network access is mediated through Iridium-authorized service providers, the Iridium CloudConnect AWS integration, and hardware-level AT-command and SBD interfaces on Iridium modems.

providers.name: Kubota Corporation
providers.description: Kubota Corporation is a Japanese multinational manufacturing agricultural, construction, and industrial machinery, including compact tractors, excavators, mowers, utility vehicles, engines, and water and environmental infrastructure systems sold in over 120 countries. Kubota does not currently publish a public developer API or developer portal; equipment telematics (KubotaNOW) and dealer integrations are handled through partner channels rather than open APIs.

providers.name: Luma Home
providers.description: Luma Home was a smart-home networking startup, backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), best known for its Luma whole-home mesh WiFi system that paired consumer routers with mobile-app network management, parental controls, and security features. The company was acquired by Newell Brands and its product line was subsequently discontinued. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio lead. An enrichment pass on 2026-07-20 found no live company website and no public developer, documentation, or API surface (candidate domains return HTTP 404), so no API artifacts were produced. This profile is retained as a historical company record.

providers.name: Mantari
providers.description: Mantari is a weather-intelligence and earth-sensing company building a decision-intelligence platform that fuses a distributed network of sensors with AI to turn environmental data across oceans, skies, and space into mission-critical, actionable intelligence. It initially targets government and defense decision support, with plans to extend into broader economic and commercial applications. As of this profile Mantari publishes a marketing homepage and a careers page but no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDKs; this record captures its identity plus a live domain-security probe, pending a future developer surface.

providers.name: Nexite
providers.description: Nexite is a retail technology company (website nexite.io) surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures. It operates in the connected-retail / IoT-for-physical-retail space. This profile was added as a stub lead and has been through one local enrichment pass: the public web presence is live but fully gated behind a bot / CAPTCHA challenge, and no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or discovery (/.well-known/) surface could be reached. No public API surface is catalogued at this time; the entry is retained as a company record pending a discoverable API.

providers.name: nomiku
providers.description: Nomiku (Y Combinator W15, backed by Slow Ventures) was a consumer-hardware startup that built an affordable WiFi-connected sous-vide immersion circulator and the companion Tender recipe app, later pivoting to the Nomiku Meals ready-to-cook subscription paired with the Nomiku Smart Cooker. The company emailed customers on December 13, 2019 that it was discontinuing the Smart Cooker and Meals and suspending operations. It exposed no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface; the device was controlled through a private mobile app and cloud backend. Retained in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead identity record for historical and investor-graph completeness only.

providers.name: North
providers.description: North (formerly Thalmic Labs) was a wearable-computing hardware company founded in 2012 in Kitchener, Ontario by University of Waterloo graduates Stephen Lake, Matthew Bailey, and Aaron Grant. It first shipped the Myo gesture-control armband, which read electrical muscle activity to wirelessly control computers and other devices, and later pivoted to Focals, consumer smart glasses with a heads-up display. A Y Combinator Winter 2013 company that raised over $140M, North was acquired by Google in January 2020 and wound down; its products and consumer-facing website (bynorth.com) were discontinued. This profile is retained as a network record. North published no public API, developer portal, or SDKs, so there is no API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Nova Metrix
providers.description: Nova Metrix is a geotechnical, environmental, and materials-testing instrumentation company headquartered in Wakefield, Massachusetts and founded in 2009. It designs and manufactures sensors, instruments, monitoring software, and consumables for structural-health monitoring, construction, civil engineering, energy, and medical markets, operating in more than 90 countries. Nova Metrix is the parent of a family of specialist geotechnical and fiber-optic brands including Roctest, Sensornet, Sherborne Sensors, Soil Instruments, Westbay Instruments, DGSI, Waterloo Hydrogeologic, and Van Essen Instruments. It is backed by Battery Ventures, Commonwealth Capital, and Ascent Venture Partners. As of this enrichment pass Nova Metrix publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API artifacts; this profile carries verified company identity rather than an API surface.

providers.name: Omen
providers.description: Omen (omen.ai) delivers real-time asset intelligence through continuous fluid analysis, monitoring the health of mission-critical machinery in data centers and heavy industry. Its two offerings are a non-invasive permanent sensor that attaches to equipment for continuous, automated fluid (oil, coolant, water) analysis and real-time health tracking, and a portable canister lab that performs on-site, off-site, and field spectroscopic testing. The platform detects wear, contamination, and degradation before failures occur, targeting the machines the world depends on. Backed by CRV. As of this enrichment pass Omen publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, or SDKs; this profile captures company identity only.

providers.name: One Raven
providers.description: One Raven is a Phoenix, Arizona smart-home technology company building a local-first home automation platform designed for homeowners who want simplicity, privacy, and control. Its core product is the One Raven Home Server, which processes and stores home data locally rather than in the cloud, and ships pre-paired with a curated set of devices such as thermostats, smart locks, leak-detection and security sensors. The platform emphasizes local data storage, encrypted remote access, and a subscription-free model. Backed by a $5M seed round led by proptech investor Fifth Wall. One Raven does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface.

providers.name: OnFarm
providers.description: OnFarm Systems, founded in 2012 and headquartered in Fresno, California, was an agriculture IoT data-integration company that offered a customizable dashboard aggregating in-field sensor and remotely gathered data (weather, soil, irrigation) into a single view for farming operations across the US, Europe, and Asia. OnFarm was acquired by SWIIM System in July 2018, at which point CEO Lance Donny became SWIIM's COO. The onfarm.com domain is now parked and listed for sale, and no live public API, developer documentation, or SDK surface remains. This profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio lead; enrichment found no active API surface to harvest.

providers.name: Padminivna
providers.description: Padminivna (padminivna.com resolves to Padmini VNA Mechatronics Ltd.) is an automotive component manufacturer established in 1991, specializing in innovation and manufacturing of technologies for the auto components industry across passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles (M&HCV, LCV), two- and three-wheelers, tractors, and off-road vehicles. Its offerings span ICE, hybrid, and EV powertrains plus sensors and agnostic technologies, with a focus on fuel efficiency, quality, and environmental sustainability. Surfaced as a portfolio lead of norwest-venture-partners; the public site exposes only a vendor portal and employee login and publishes no public developer API or documentation surface.

providers.name: Parstream
providers.description: ParStream was a big-data analytics database company founded in 2011 in Cologne, Germany by Michael Hummel, Joerg Bienert and Norbert Heuber. Its columnar, GPU-accelerated OLAP database was built for Internet-of-Things environments, filtering and analyzing billions of records in sub-second time at the edge of the network, with query access via SQL and a JSON query format plus a C++ API for user-defined query nodes. Cisco acquired ParStream on October 26, 2015 and folded the team into its Data and Analytics Group; the standalone product was declared obsolete and retired in 2018. The former parstream.com domain now redirects to a Cisco end-of-life product page, and no independent developer portal, API, SDK, or discovery surface remains to enrich.

providers.name: Peel
providers.description: Peel Technologies Inc (peel.com) is a Redpoint Ventures-backed consumer technology company known for the Peel Smart Remote mobile app, which turned smartphones into universal remote controls for TVs, set-top boxes, and home-entertainment devices with a TV guide and content discovery layer. As of this enrichment pass the peel.com website resolves over HTTPS but serves only a single-logo placeholder page (frameset redirecting to an S3-hosted logo), indicating the company is dormant. No public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI, SDKs, or /.well-known discovery surface was found; developer/api/docs subdomains do not resolve.

providers.name: Process Sensing Technologies
providers.description: Process Sensing Technologies (PST) is a measurement instrumentation group that designs and manufactures precision sensors and analyzers for moisture, humidity, dew point, oxygen, and trace gas measurement across industrial, pharmaceutical, food, and life-science applications. Its brand portfolio includes Michell Instruments, Rotronic, Analytical Industries, Ntron, SensoScientific, and Isensix, spanning process gas analysis and real-time environmental monitoring. The company now operates under the DwyerOmega brand following its combination with Dwyer Instruments. It was surfaced as a Battery Ventures portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; probing of its public web surface found hardware, software downloads, calibration tooling, and monitoring platforms but no public developer API, SDK, or documentation portal.

providers.name: Revolv
providers.description: Revolv was a smart-home company that built a connected home hub and mobile application to unify control of disparate smart-home devices and wireless protocols from a single app. The company was acquired by Nest (Google) and the Revolv hub and service were subsequently discontinued; owners of purchased Revolv hubs were directed to Nest support for refunds through a deadline of October 31, 2018. This API Evangelist profile is retained as a historical portfolio record. The company publishes no active API, developer portal, SDKs, or public developer surface, so this entry carries only a domain-security probe of its remaining web presence.

providers.name: Riide
providers.description: Riide manufactures connected electric bicycles combining a street-legal 500W ebike (the Riide 2) with built-in GPS tracking, 4G cellular connectivity, remote lock/disable theft prevention, and a removable battery with state-of-charge monitoring. The company pairs hardware with a mobile app and connected-vehicle services. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network; as of this pass the public site is a consumer product/pre-order page ("coming soon") with no documented developer, API, or documentation surface.

providers.name: SIQ Basketball
providers.description: SIQ Basketball is a Techstars-backed sports-technology company that builds a FIBA-approved, sensor-embedded smart basketball and companion mobile app that automatically tracks shooting mechanics, makes and misses, shot arc and other performance data to coach players. Its technology is now marketed under the Spalding brand as the Spalding TF DNA Smart Basketball, sold with an app subscription. The company operates as a direct-to-consumer product and does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; this profile captures its network identity and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Space Runners
providers.description: Space Runners is a digital fashion company that designs and launches digital wearable NFTs for metaverses in collaboration with celebrities and brands. Positioned at the intersection of Web3, gaming, and consumer fashion, the company produces branded digital sneakers, apparel, and wearable collectibles for use across metaverse platforms. Backed by Accel and Pantera Capital, Space Runners operates a consumer-facing brand and marketplace rather than a developer platform; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Spider Fleet
providers.description: Spiderfleet (Spider Fleet) is a Mexico-based intelligent fleet-management platform that helps businesses run and maintain their vehicle fleets. Its public site (spider.com.mx, in Spanish) markets fleet onboarding ("Flotillas"), preventive maintenance scheduling ("mantenimientos"), and quote requests ("cotizacion") for fleet operators, and is backed by 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes only a static marketing website with no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable specification; two navigation links (contact and login) return 404 and the site's TLS certificate is expired.

providers.name: Strella Biotechnology
providers.description: Strella Biotechnology is a Seattle-based produce-quality intelligence company that uses ethylene gas sensors and predictive analytics to reduce food waste across the fresh-produce supply chain. Its product line spans Storage (predicting produce maturity in cold storage), Ripen (automating the ripening process), Sequence (optimizing shipment order to cut shrink), and Monitor (real-time environmental monitoring in logistics). The company reports tracking over two billion pounds of produce across 26 countries and is backed by GV (Google Ventures). As of this enrichment pass, Strella exposes no public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or webhook surface.

providers.name: Swarm Technologies
providers.description: Swarm Technologies is a company surfaced as a portfolio company of social-capital and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. Sector: space. This profile is a lead awaiting the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Taascom
providers.description: Taascom (branded "The As A Service Company", taascom.com) is a San Jose, California company founded in 2019 that provides an IoT-based servitization SaaS platform helping equipment makers shift from transactional capex sales to recurring subscription, pay-per-use, and outcome-based revenue models. Its packaged offerings include Device-as-a-Service, Auto-Replenishment-as-a-Service, and Uptime-as-a-Service. Surfaced as a portfolio-company lead and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub; enrichment found a marketing-stage web presence only — no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDK, or OpenAPI surface at the time of this pass.

providers.name: Toyota Connected
providers.description: Toyota Connected is Toyota Motor Corporation's global connected mobility technology arm, building the data, telematics, and software platforms that power Toyota and Lexus connected vehicle services worldwide. The group operates as a federation of regional subsidiaries — TOYOTA Connected Corporation (Japan), Toyota Connected North America (TCNA, Plano, Texas), TOYOTA Connected Europe (TCEU, United Kingdom), TOYOTA Connected India (TCIN), TOYOTA Connected Asia Pacific, and Toyota Tsusho Connected Middle East — and runs Toyota's Mobility Service Platform (MSPF) and the Drivelink telematics backbone behind Safety Connect, Service Connect, Remote Connect, Destination Assist, Wi-Fi Connect, and the "Hey Toyota" in-vehicle voice assistant. TCNA reports surpassing five million connected customer calls across Toyota and Lexus and runs Toyota's Big Data Center for connected-vehicle data. KINTO — Toyota's mobility services brand for car subscription, car-sharing, ride-hailing, and carpooling (KINTO One, KINTO Flex, KINTO Share, KINTO Ride, KINTO Join) — sits adjacent in Toyota's mobility portfolio and is powered by KINTO Technologies on AWS. Toyota exposes developer portals at developer.eig.toyota.com (Toyota API Portal covering TMC, TMNA, TEMA, TFS, NAMC, and other entities) and developer.toyotaconnected.eu (Toyota Connected EU API services, including Telematics and Vehicle APIs documented with Swagger/OpenAPI), but access is gated to partners and internal Toyota teams — no public, unauthenticated OpenAPI specifications are published. Third-party access to Toyota vehicle data for individual developers is typically brokered through partners such as Smartcar and High Mobility rather than directly via Toyota's own portals.

providers.name: Tule Technologies
providers.description: Tule Technologies was an agricultural technology company that measured crop water stress and actual evapotranspiration (ET) directly in the field, giving growers irrigation guidance through its FieldStat monitoring tool for orchards, vineyards, and row crops. Backed by Bloomberg Beta, Tule has been acquired by and integrated into CropX; the tuletechnologies.com domain now 301-redirects to cropx.com, where Tule's ET monitoring is combined with soil sensing, weather data, and irrigation management in one platform. Enrichment found no independent public API, developer portal, SDK, or documented developer program for Tule Technologies.

providers.name: Veniam
providers.description: Veniam builds intelligent networking software for the Internet of Moving Things, moving data automatically, securely, and cost-effectively between connected vehicles, mobile IoT devices, and the cloud across all available networks (cellular, Wi-Fi, and DSRC). Its platform serves video telematics, connected fleets, industrial IoT, and auto OEM/Tier 1 use cases, and reports processing 110M+ kilometers of mobile IoT data with 130+ granted patents. Founded by Joao Barros, Susana Sargento, Robin Chase, and Roy Russell, the company was acquired by Nexar in 2022. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures. No public developer portal, API documentation, or OpenAPI surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Weft
providers.description: Weft was a Burlington, Vermont based supply-chain logistics startup, founded by Marc Held around 2013-2014, that combined hardware sensors and software to track the shipping of physical goods worldwide in real time. It raised a seed round of under $1M led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Data Elite, with plans for a $5M Series A. The company was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this enrichment pass the company appears defunct: no live corporate website, no developer portal, and no public API surface could be found. Candidate domains were probed and none host an active product (weft.com refused connection, weft.io does not resolve, weft.ai is a parked domain listed for sale).

providers.name: Ditto
providers.description: DUPLICATE STUB — do not enrich. This repository was created from the API Evangelist secondary-market harvest backlog (Forge Global listing for "Ditto stock") and profiles the same legal entity already profiled in depth at all/ditto-live (aid ditto-live). Ditto is an edge-native data sync platform, founded in 2018 by Adam Fish and Max Alexander, headquartered in San Francisco, that lets mobile and edge devices synchronize data peer-to-peer over Bluetooth, WiFi Direct and LAN with or without internet connectivity, backed by an optional cloud tier. The company has raised roughly $136.7M across a 2021 seed, a 2023 Series A and an $82M Series B in March 2025. Its developer surface (ditto.live, docs.ditto.live, the Cloud HTTP API and Edge Server HTTP API) is already captured under all/ditto-live, so no artifacts were generated here — the correct disposition is duplicate retirement into ditto-live per the merge procedure, which is a human-reviewed step.

providers.name: Neuroharmonics
providers.description: NeuroHarmonics is a London-based neurotechnology company and UCL spin-out developing non-invasive brain-health hardware based on focused ultrasound neuromodulation. Its wearable headset uses precisely focused sound waves to safely modulate deep brain circuits without surgery, an MRI, or head shaving, aiming to turn expensive, invasive neuromodulation into scalable, continuous at-home therapy for neurological and psychiatric conditions. Founded in 2016 by Antonio Stanziola, Tim Den Boer, Bradley Treeby and Michael Brown, the company is backed by Speedinvest, UCL Technology Fund, Fusion Fund and Jumpspace Ventures. As an early-stage medical-device company it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Aeroscout
providers.description: AeroScout was an Israeli real-time location systems (RTLS) company that built Wi-Fi-based RFID tags, exciters, and location receivers together with the MobileView software platform to track the location, condition, and status of mobile assets and people, primarily for hospitals and healthcare providers. Menlo Ventures led its Series C round in 2007. AeroScout was acquired by Stanley Black & Decker in 2012 (~$240M) and folded into Stanley Healthcare; the product line and brand now live under Securitas Healthcare / Securitas Technology. AeroScout no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no public developer portal, OpenAPI, or SDKs — integration with the on-premise AeroScout Engine has historically been via a SOAP API for enterprise/HIS systems rather than a public web API.

providers.name: Atlas Wearables
providers.description: Atlas Wearables was an Austin, Texas fitness-technology startup founded in 2013 by Peter Li, Mike Kasparian, and Alex Hsieh. It raised over $500,000 on Indiegogo in 2014 for the Atlas Wristband, a motion-tracking gym wearable whose "Exercise ID" technology automatically recognized strength exercises and counted reps and sets. The company shipped the Atlas Wristband and Wristband 2 and historically promoted an open developer API and integrations with apps such as MapMyFitness and Fitocracy. Atlas Wearables was acquired by Peloton Interactive in late 2020; the company no longer operates independently and the atlaswearables.com domain no longer resolves (it is now held by Peloton Interactive). This API Evangelist profile is retained as a historical record of a former Techstars-associated portfolio lead; no live developer surface, API specification, or documentation remains available to enrich.

providers.name: Calibra Medical
providers.description: Calibra Medical, Inc. was a Redwood City, California medical device company founded in 2004 to make mealtime insulin therapy simpler and more discreet. Its product was the Finesse "patch-pen", a fully mechanical, three-day wearable bolus insulin delivery patch (roughly 2 x 1 x 0.25 inches, 200-unit reservoir, no batteries, display, or handheld controller) dosed by pressing two buttons. Backed by Canaan Partners, Frazier Healthcare Partners, Intersouth Partners, Skyline Ventures, and Three Arch Partners, the company raised approximately $61.5M before Johnson & Johnson acquired it in a reported $77M all-cash deal in 2012, folding it into the J&J Diabetes Care Companies. J&J rebranded the device OneTouch Via but never commercially launched it, and on July 17, 2018 sold select Calibra Medical assets and an exclusive worldwide license to Swiss wearable-insulin firm CeQur. Calibra Medical no longer operates as an independent company: it publishes no developer portal, no API, and no public source repositories, and the calibramedical.com domain now resolves to a parked "domain may be for sale" page. This profile is retained as a historical medical-device company record with no API surface.

providers.name: Conexant Systems
providers.description: Conexant Systems, Inc. was an American fabless semiconductor company headquartered in Irvine, California. Spun off from Rockwell Semiconductor Systems in 1999, it designed mixed-signal and system-on-chip products for audio, voice, imaging, modem, and networking applications, and was best known for its dial-up modem chipsets, audio codecs, and far-field voice-input processors used in smart-home and IoT devices. Conexant's audio and imaging business was acquired by Synaptics in 2017 and the standalone Conexant brand has since been retired. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-company lead; the company publishes no public developer portal, API, or machine-readable API surface (its former conexant.com domain no longer resolves to an active site), so there are no API artifacts to enrich at this time.

providers.name: Corventis
providers.description: Corventis, Inc. was a healthcare technology company that developed wearable cardiac monitoring devices — including the PiiX adhesive sensor and the NUVANT Mobile Cardiac Telemetry (MCT) system — for remote patient monitoring and arrhythmia detection. Backed by Kleiner Perkins, the company was acquired by Medtronic in 2014 and no longer operates as an independent entity. The corventis.com domain now resolves to Medtronic infrastructure (Medtronic nameservers; TLS certificate scoped to Medtronic domains). No public developer portal, API documentation, SDK, or machine-readable API surface exists for this provider.

providers.name: Echelon
providers.description: Echelon Corporation was a pioneer in energy control networking and semiconductors, known for its LonWorks control networking platform and IoT edge computing products. Surfaced as a Mayfield portfolio company (listed as an energy-control-networking milestone/exit), the company is no longer an independent entity — its product lines were acquired (Adesto Technologies, 2018) and now live under EnOcean. There is no live Echelon developer portal or public API surface to enrich.

providers.name: In Charge One, Inc.
providers.description: In Charge One, Inc. is a hardware startup behind "Socket to Pocket," a paid charging system for electronic devices in public spaces. The device lets visitors charge smartphones, laptops, drones, e-bikes, and scooters at cafes, shops, clinics, stadiums, airports, and other venues by tapping a card and paying for access, while venue owners monetize the outlet and earn a commission per plugged socket. It ships in wall-mounted, extension-cord, and anti-vandal street versions. Founded in 2023 by Danylo (Daniel) Tonkopii, co-founder of Delfast electric bikes, and Andriy Zinchuk, the company is based in Los Angeles, California and was developed by Ukrainian engineers. It is a consumer/commercial hardware and payments business, not an API provider: no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface has been published, and its incharge.one domain is currently non-resolving and in registrar redemption/pending-delete status. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and is retained as an identity record.

providers.name: Millennial Fox
providers.description: Millennial Fox, Inc. is a Los Angeles-based consumer company backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners that set out to bridge the gap between entertainment and fitness. Its flagship product, Tracks Battle Squad, was a socially gamified workout companion for iOS and watchOS that integrated with the Apple Health app to turn physical activity into points, badges, and accessories for a virtual 3D fox character. The app launched in 2017, was featured on Apple Music's Planet of the Apps, and has since been removed from the App Store; the company appears inactive and exposes no public API, developer portal, documentation, or well-known surface.

providers.name: Playbrush
providers.description: Playbrush is a consumer oral-care technology brand that makes smart, gamified electric and sonic toothbrushes for children (ages 3+), pairing a Bluetooth-connected brush with a companion mobile app that turns brushing into interactive games and coaching to build good dental-hygiene habits. Founded as a UK/Austria startup and backed by Speedinvest, the Playbrush product line has since been acquired by SUNSTAR and is now sold under the GUM Playbrush brand; the former playbrush.com domain 302-redirects to a Sunstar GUM product page. Playbrush is a hardware/consumer-app company and exposes no public developer portal, API, specification, or /.well-known/ discovery surface. This profile was surfaced as a Speedinvest portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a lead; enrichment confirmed there is no API surface.

providers.name: Silver Spring Networks *
providers.description: Silver Spring Networks was a smart-grid, smart-city, and IoT networking company that built wireless canopy networks and the SLV/Data Platform for utilities, offering RESTful Data Platform APIs (device registration, device metadata, sensor data, and webhook event notifications) plus an SDK on its developer portal at developer.ssni.com. Itron completed its acquisition of the company in January 2018 for approximately USD 830 million and rebranded it Itron Networked Solutions; the standalone ssni.com and developer.ssni.com properties are now offline. Enrichment pass 2026-07-21 found no live API surface: all legacy domains fail to resolve and the historical developer portal is no longer reachable.

providers.name: Lighting
providers.description: Lighting covers the technologies, standards, and APIs related to controlling smart lighting systems, connected bulbs, fixtures, and lighting automation in home and commercial environments.

bands.label: Not Yet Rated
bands.blurb: Providers we have not scored yet — unknown, not zero.

providers.name: Alcatraz AI
providers.description: Alcatraz AI, Inc. builds privacy-first facial authentication for enterprise physical access control, replacing badges, cards and PINs with the face. Its flagship edge device, Rock X, installs in-line between any Wiegand or OSDP reader and an existing access control system and authenticates people in real time at the edge without storing or transmitting a facial image. Founded in 2016 in Cupertino, California, the company pioneered Facial-Authentication-as-a-Service (FAaaS) and layers tailgating detection, 3D liveness, ONVIF video-at-the-door and SIP intercom onto a single reader, managed through a cloud or on-premises Admin Portal with native C-CURE and Genetec integrations and a customer-facing REST API secured with an x-alcatraz-api-key header.

providers.name: Ampere Computing
providers.description: Ampere Computing is a Santa Clara, California semiconductor company founded in 2018 by Renee James and now part of the SoftBank Group. It designs Arm-based Cloud Native Processors — the Ampere Altra and Altra Max families (up to 128 cores) and the flagship AmpereOne family (up to 192 single-threaded cores) — for cloud, AI inference and edge deployments. Alongside the silicon it ships a software stack: Ampere Optimized AI frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow, ONNX Runtime, llama.cpp, Ollama) distributed as first-party container images, tuned GCC/glibc/binutils builds, performance and porting tooling, and an arm64 developer community. Ampere publishes no public developer API — its developer program is a hardware, tooling and porting program rather than an API program.

providers.name: Andium
providers.description: Andium is a New York City based industrial IoT company that combines its own hardware and AI software into an end-to-end remote field monitoring platform for the energy sector. Its InSite smart camera and edge software watch remote oil and gas wellsites for methane leaks, flare and pilot-light outages, tank levels, liquid spills, fire and asset movement, and push real-time alerts to operators instead of sending crews to look. The company reports cutting site greenhouse-gas emissions by up to 65%, field operating costs by up to 45% and windshield time by 80%, and raised a $21.7M Series B led by Aramco Ventures. Andium publishes no public developer program, documentation or specification for that monitoring platform; the only callable, machine-readable API surface on any andium.com host is the Universal Commerce Protocol MCP endpoint on its Shopify-backed merchandise storefront at shop.andium.com.

providers.name: ANELLO Photonics
providers.description: ANELLO Photonics is a Santa Clara, California company building solid-state, high-precision inertial navigation and sensing products for positioning, navigation and orientation when GNSS is jammed, spoofed, blocked or otherwise unavailable. Its products are powered by SiPhOG (Silicon Photonics Optical Gyroscope), a chip-scale optical gyroscope built on standard semiconductor processes. The developer surface is an embedded one rather than a web API: ANELLO Ground INS, Ground IMU, Maritime INS, Aerial INS, X3 IMU and the Evaluation Kit expose a documented ASCII and RTCM-binary message protocol over RS-232 serial, USB-C and UDP/Ethernet, with a public developer manual, a first-party Python configuration and logging tool, a ROS/ROS2 driver that publishes machine-readable .msg/.srv interface definitions, and PX4/ArduPilot and MAVLink integrations.

providers.name: Aperia Technologies
providers.description: Aperia Technologies is a Burlingame, California vehicle-technology company that builds active tire-inflation hardware and predictive tire-maintenance software for commercial fleets. Its Halo automatic tire inflator bolts on at the wheel end and uses wheel rotation to keep tires at their target pressure, while the Halo Connect platform pairs that hardware with machine-learning analytics trained on billions of real-world fleet miles to deliver tire health, leak detection, tread, load and vibration insight across steer, drive and trailer positions. Halo Connect exposes a partner REST API so fleet telematics, maintenance and TMS platforms can pull vehicle records, inflation issues and hardware issues out of the Halo Connect portal.

providers.name: Arccos Golf
providers.description: Arccos Golf is the golf performance-tracking platform behind the Arccos Caddie smart sensors, smart grips and the Arccos Air wearable — the Official Game Tracker of the PGA TOUR. Club-mounted sensors and the Arccos mobile app automatically capture every shot on the course, then AI-driven Strokes Gained analytics, Smart Club Distances, an AI rangefinder and Arccos Caddie strategy turn that shot data into per-round and per-hole insight. Arccos exposes that same data to approved third parties through the Arccos On-Course Data API, a Swagger 2.0-documented REST API over rounds, round stats, clubs, users and a public course/course-version catalog, secured with an OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow and per-resource read scopes, plus registerable HTTPS webhooks for round and account-disconnect events. Its Shopify-hosted storefront additionally publishes an llms.txt and a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) MCP endpoint for agent-driven commerce.

providers.name: High Tech
providers.description: High Tech indexes the APIs, data services, and reference artifacts that power the electronics, semiconductor, hardware, and IoT industries. The landscape covers electronic component data and distribution (Octopart / Nexar, Digi-Key, Mouser, Arrow Electronics, Avnet, Newark / element14), ECAD and PCB design data (SnapEDA, Ultra Librarian, Altium 365 via Nexar Design), hardware lifecycle and IoT device management (AWS IoT, Azure IoT Hub, Particle, Golioth), bill-of-materials and component-search workflows used across hardware product engineering, and the authoritative manufacturer data that anchors a component record (manufacturer part number, manufacturer, datasheet, lifecycle status, RoHS / REACH compliance, real-time inventory and pricing across distributors). This index captures the canonical providers, the shape of a component record as JSON Schema, a JSON-LD context aligning with schema.org Product / Offer / Organization, and the domain vocabulary used across the high-tech component supply chain.

providers.name: RFID
providers.description: Radio-Frequency Identification (RFID) is an automatic identification technology that uses radio waves to read and capture information stored on a tag attached to an object. RFID powers supply chain visibility, inventory management, asset tracking, access control, and contactless payments. The RFID ecosystem includes hardware vendors (Zebra, Impinj, Alien Technology), software platforms (ClearStream, TagMatiks, Jetstream), and open standards (GS1 EPCIS, EPC Tag Data Standard, ISO 18000 series).

providers.name: Teradar
providers.description: Teradar is a Boston, Massachusetts semiconductor and sensing company founded in 2020 by Matthew Carey, Gregory Charvat and Nicholas Saiz that is commercializing terahertz-band vision sensors for vehicles, defense and security screening. Its Modular Terahertz Engine (MTE) is an all-solid-state chip architecture built from proprietary transmit (TX), receive (RX) and Teracore processing silicon, delivering 0.13-degree native angular resolution at 300+ meters in day, night, rain, fog and snow, positioned to sit alongside cameras and to displace radar and lidar in SAE L1-L5 driver assistance and autonomy programs. The company emerged from stealth in late 2025 with a $150M Series B led by VXI Capital with Ibex Investors, Capricorn Investment Group, The Engine Ventures and Lockheed Martin Ventures, and is working with global OEMs and Tier-One suppliers toward a 2028 model-year launch. Teradar is a hardware and silicon company: it publishes a marketing site and product specification sheets, but no public developer program, API, SDK, or machine-readable interface contract.

providers.name: Uhnder
providers.description: Uhnder is an Austin, Texas fabless semiconductor company founded in 2015 that designs the S80 and S81 77 GHz 4D digital imaging Radar-on-Chip (RoC) for automotive ADAS and automated mobility. Its Digital Code Modulation (DCM) approach on a 28nm RF CMOS process replaces analog FMCW radar with a software-defined sensor, and each RoC ships with an ASPICE-qualified Software Development Kit carrying ready-to-integrate software APIs, on-chip user algorithm support and system tools for Tier-1 and OEM radar stacks. Uhnder is a chip supplier rather than a web-API provider: the SDK and its APIs are embedded interfaces delivered under a commercial customer relationship, and the company publishes no public developer portal, documentation host or machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Uptake
providers.description: Uptake Technologies is a Chicago-based industrial AI and predictive-maintenance software company founded in 2014 by Eric Lefkofsky and Brad Keywell. Its SaaS platform ingests telematics, sensor, fluid-analysis and work-order data from heavy commercial fleets and industrial assets, then applies machine-learning failure models — backed by an Asset Strategy Library of roughly 800 equipment types and tens of thousands of failure modes acquired with Asset Performance Technologies in 2018 — to predict component failure before it happens. Products include Uptake Fleet and Radar (predictive maintenance alerts), Compass (work-order data cleansing), Fusion (operational-technology data to cloud) and Scout (rules-based alerting), delivered through the fleet.uptake.com web application, a Geotab Marketplace add-in, and a customer-provisioned REST API gateway at api.uptake.com. Bosch announced its acquisition of Uptake in March 2026.

providers.name: Utilidata
providers.description: Utilidata is an Ann Arbor, Michigan software company building Karman, a distributed AI platform that runs on a custom NVIDIA system-on-module embedded directly into electrical infrastructure — smart meters and grid-edge devices on the utility side, PDUs and power trays inside AI data centers. Karman processes high-resolution AC metrology locally (single-cycle waveform statistics at 1+ MS/s sample rates) to produce "data products" such as Power Quality Analytics, enabling millisecond-level power control, GPU/PSU failure prediction, phase balancing and power-aware scheduling. Utilidata publishes the Karman Power Aware Module as Apache-2.0 open source: a Rust reference implementation that serializes Karman data products as Protocol Buffers (package utilidata.karman.bibimbap.v1), transports them over ZeroMQ, and exposes them to Prometheus and TimescaleDB through a Helm-packaged Kubernetes stack. The company has raised a $100M Series C and counts NVIDIA, Microsoft Climate Innovation Fund, American Electric Power and Renown Capital Partners among its backers.

providers.name: Verve Motion
providers.description: Verve Motion is a wearable robotics company spun out of the Harvard Biodesign Lab that builds SafeLift, a soft powered exosuit for industrial workers who lift repetitively. Inertial sensors woven into the suit detect lifting motion and trigger assistive force that the company says takes up to 40% of the strain off a worker's back, while Verve Logic — its cloud platform — collects the resulting movement data and reports ergonomic risk, unsafe-posture trends and exosuit utilization to safety managers. SafeLift is sold as a subscription bundling the exosuit, the Verve Logic data portal and Verve Care support, and is distributed in part through partners such as HexArmor. Verve Motion publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable specification; the Verve Logic portal at logic.vervemotion.com is a customer-only single-page application that disallows crawling in robots.txt.

providers.name: Zero Motorcycles
providers.description: Zero Motorcycles is an American manufacturer of electric motorcycles and powertrains, founded in 2006 in Santa Cruz, California. It designs and builds street, dual-sport and off-road electric motorcycles across its S, DS, FX and X lines — including the SR/S, SR/F, DSR/X, FXE and XE — around a proprietary Z-Force electric powertrain and aircraft-grade aluminum frame. Its bikes run the Cypher operating system, which pairs with the Zero Motorcycles NextGen mobile app over Bluetooth and cellular telematics for ride data, remote diagnostics, over-the-air updates and performance customization, and with the Cypher Store, where owners purchase software upgrades that unlock additional power, top speed and features. Zero sells internationally through a dealer network and serves retail, fleet and authority/first-responder segments. Its connected-vehicle platform is consumer-facing only: Zero publishes no public developer program, API documentation, SDKs or machine-readable specification.
